title: Seven men in court over violent disturbance on Dublin’s Ormond Quay
description: Men aged from their 30s to 50s to stand trial over alleged incident at a house in 2024
content:
Seven men are to stand trial over an alleged violent incident in Dublin city centre more than two years ago.
Gardaí responded to reports of a disturbance at a property at Ormond Quay, Dublin 1, on August 30th, 2024, when several people were taken from the scene to the Mater Hospital to be treated for non-life-threatening injuries.
Following an investigation by the Garda Special Detective Unit, a file was prepared and forwarded to the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP).
Earlier this month, seven men were arrested and charged in connection with the incident.
They appeared before Judge Karen Dowling at Dublin District Court on Tuesday, charged with violent disorder at Ormond Quay on August 30th, 2024.
The seven men, all with Dublin addresses, are: Conor Hughes (49) of Lakeland’s Close, Kilmacud; Rhys Kane (32), of Achill Road, Ballybrack; 37-year-old Darren Fox of Beechpark, Cabinteely; Keith Hogan (43), Coolevin, Ballybrack; Darren Weldon (55), The New Maltings, Dublin 8; Conor Mills (45) of Queen Street, Dublin 7; and Dean Shannon (40), St Kevin’s Villas, Sallynoggin.
Weldon “made no reply” to his charge, Det Garda Mark Cannon told the court.
Evidence of his six co-defendants’ arrest and charging procedure was given by way of a certificate furnished to the court. They had been charged earlier and were all on station bail.
The judge noted there was no objection to the seven accused remaining on bail and that the DPP had authorised trial on indictment at a higher level.
The men, who have yet to enter pleas, were ordered to appear again on November 27th for gardaí to serve them with books of evidence and for the granting of a return for trial order.
Most had no legal representation for Tuesday’s hearing
Their cases entered the court system amid escalated industrial action, with most Dublin solicitors withdrawing their services over legal aid payment reforms.

title: How the LA Clippers bent the financial rules to become the Manchester City of the NBA
description: Basketball franchise used four different enterprises to funnel truckloads of money to star forward Kawhi Leonard beyond his publicised salary
content:
Stop me if you think you’ve heard this one before. Once upon a time there was a team that shared its home city with a far more successful and globally renowned rival. So, the less-vaunted club decided to bend the rules just a tad. In a league where regulations about the salary cap were supposedly strictly enforced, this unscrupulous outfit opted to cook their books and gain an illegal advantage.
Among the subterfuges deployed was an elaborate scheme ensuring their best player earned many multiples of his official wage through no-show contracts with outside companies that just so happened to have ties to the club owner. Imagine such a thing.
Like their counterparts over in the soon to be very blue half of Manchester , the Los Angeles Clippers’ use of shadow deals to circumvent NBA spending rules and to try to outshine their more illustrious neighbours, the Lakers, was eventually rumbled.
Beyond trousering $50m per season, it turned out their star forward Kawhi Leonard also took home $7m each year from Aspiration, an eco-conscious financial services firm in which the Clippers’ owner Steve Ballmer was heavily invested. Handy money for an endorsement deal that didn’t require him to do any actual endorsing.
He enjoyed a similarly lucrative sinecure with Daktronics, a company that had been paid what many regarded as an exorbitant $100m by Ballmer to build the video screen at the team’s Intuit Dome. Leonard received another $18m through pay for no play arrangements with at least two other businesses, plus a free equity stake in a minor league soccer club in Rhode Island. Oh, and in another violation of league policy, the Clippers also covered all air and ground travel expenses for him and his uncle/adviser, Dennis Robertson.
This extensive chicanery was first exposed by Pablo Torre Finds Out, the eponymous investigative podcast run by a former ESPN journalist. Initially, the Clippers denied everything but then the NBA hired the law firm of Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen and Katz to independently probe the allegations. After 12 months and a legal bill of $50m, the third-party examination of their business practices concluded Torre’s forensic reporting had been correct, and the club was penalised accordingly.
For using four different enterprises to funnel truckloads of money to Leonard beyond his publicised salary, the club has been forced to forfeit five first-round draft picks, fined $30m, and had several key personnel, including the owner, suspended from all team and league activities for between six months and a year. The loss of draft picks will make it almost impossible for the Clippers, currently a young squad of up and comers, to compete for an NBA title for much of the next decade. Perhaps more significantly, the Department of Justice has just begun a criminal inquiry into the shadier corners of their business operation.
Fans of the Premier League and its glacial disciplinary process can only wonder how a governing body could only need one calendar year to sift through such serious accusations, come up with a verdict and hand out a penalty. It’s almost as if time should be of the essence when it comes to trying to preserve the integrity of a sport. Having reacted to news of their impending punishment, by loudly threatening to launch appeals in the hope of creating some sort of elongated sporting version of Jarndyce and Jarndyce – otherwise known as the Manchester City gambit – the Clippers took only a couple of weeks to eventually come to their senses and to meekly agree to take their medicine.
The whole tawdry affair started when Leonard became a free agent in 2019. Fresh off leading the Toronto Raptors to a championship, he had several high-profile suitors, including the Lakers, chasing his signature. Mere months after he ultimately opted to sign for the Clippers, not the most glamorous destination available, there were media reports that his negotiations with various clubs had involved his Uncle Dennis making outrageous contractual demands on his behalf. These included wanting a free house, use of a private plane 24/7, part-ownership of the team, and guaranteed income streams outside his regular salary.
Having investigated those allegations, the NBA somehow found no evidence of any wrongdoing, a conclusion that speaks volumes about their own inadequacies. Six years down the line, Torre blew the story of the relationship between player and club open with enough force to win a Pulitzer Prize. His work also got Uncle Dennis banned from engaging with any basketball player or team for five years. While the league congratulated itself for meting out the toughest penalty in the history of the sport and many around the game regarded it as a “sledgehammer” judgment, plenty reckon it could and should have been a lot worse.
With mandatory relegation not an option and having won no titles that could be stripped away, the fine is especially nonsensical. Ballmer is worth an estimated $145bn. Demanding he pay $30m in restitution is the equivalent of asking somebody earning $100k a year to fork over 20 cents. Even if he is also required to foot the $50m bill for the investigation, this causes him far less pain than the ominous news the relentless Torre is continuing to dig into the Clippers’ affairs.
For his part in this debacle, Leonard was fined $700,000 and has since been traded back to the Toronto Raptors where he will earn $57m per season. The show must go on.

title: Trump’s backing fails to lift Netanyahu as Israel heads for defining vote
description: Israel’s longest-serving prime minister has staged a remarkable political recovery. Now, with  the US president at his side, he is seeking to extend it
content:
N ext Tuesday, October 27th, Israelis head to the polls in a vote that could herald the political demise of Binyamin Netanyahu , Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, who has led the country for all but 18 months since 2009.
The polls show that neither the Netanyahu bloc of right-wing and religious parties nor the disparate “bloc of change” (the anti-Netanyahu bloc) will have a 61-seat majority in the 120-seat Knesset parliament.
If the projected seats of the two Arab parties are included, then there is a clear majority for the opposition, but Avigdor Lieberman, head of the right-wing Yisrael Beiteinu - one of the four bloc of change parties - says he will not sit in a coalition which is dependent on Arab parties.
However, campaign promises may be discarded after October 27th, and Netanyahu is convinced that his divided opponents will bury their differences and strike a deal to remove him from power during coalition negotiations.
It remains to be seen what impact, if any, Sunday’s endorsement of Netanyahu by US president Trump will have on the polls.
Early indications are that his reelection bid has received no boost from — and may have even been damaged by — Trump’s unusually explicit endorsement.
A poll by the country’s top-rated TV station found projections for the vote are unchanged, Channel 12 said on Monday, citing a survey from earlier in the day that gave Netanyahu’s Likud party 21 of parliament’s 120 seats, with 24 going to Yashar, lead by main challenger, Gadi Eisenkot.
The poll was carried out after Trump on Sunday called Netanyahu “strong, brave, and brilliant” and gave his “total endorsement” to Israel’s longest-standing leader.
While the impact of Trump’s Truth Media post may take longer to show up in polling, the Channel 12 survey hints at the US leader’s waning popularity among Israelis and the likelihood that many of them have already made up their minds on who to vote for.
Gadi Eisenkot, leader of the centrist Yashar, predicted by almost all polls to emerge as the largest party, says he will aim to form a government even if the Zionist opposition parties fall short of a 61-seat majority.
Next Tuesday’s election marks the first opportunity Israelis have had to pass judgment since the October 7th, 2023, Hamas attack on southern Israel, considered the biggest catastrophe in the country’s 78-year history, when 1,200 people were killed and another 250 taken captive in to Gaza.
In the weeks immediately following the attack, Netanyahu’s political support plunged dramatically, with support for the Netanyahu coalition dropping from 65 to 43–44 seats. About 70-80 per cent of Israelis said they believed Netanyahu bore personal responsibility and a clear majority favoured his resignation.
[ Can anyone end the Netanyahu era? Opens in new window ]
His strategy for political survival was twofold: avoid an early election at all costs and prevent the formation of a state commission of inquiry to investigate the October 7th disaster. Avoiding an early election meant paying off his coalition partners - engaging in never-ending wars and delaying a hostage release deal to keep the far-right parties happy, and avoiding drafting the ultra-Orthodox into the army to appease the religious parties.
Three years on, as Israelis prepare to vote, it’s clear that his strategy has worked. He likely won’t be able to clinch a majority, but the polls show he will be able to prevent his opponents from doing so, with a hung parliament the most likely outcome.
Under such a scenario, Netanyahu will continue as caretaker prime minister and Israel will go to the polls again in the spring.
President Yitzhak Herzog has vowed to do everything in his power to prevent Israel from heading into another round of elections if next week’s result fails to produce a clear winner.
“I’m doing everything I can to ensure Israel has a stable government,” he said. “But I’ll go further than that: I will do absolutely everything I can to prevent repeat elections. We must do everything possible to avoid going through this again and again and again.”
Between 2019 and 2021, Israel held four rounds of elections before a government led by Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid was formed. But this only lasted 18 months before the current Netanyahu coalition was elected.
[ Israel’s former spy chief sues Netanyahu for ‘blood libel’ over October 7th attacks Opens in new window ]
After the final results are calculated, Herzog will task the candidate he believes has the best chance of forming government with cobbling together a coalition within 28 days (with a possible 14-day extension) - this isn’t necessarily the head of the largest party.
The president can also mediate between factions if there is no clear majority, in an advisory role.
The election may be determined by two interrelated factors: the fate of two parties hovering around the minimum threshold and voter turnout.
A new right-wing party, Amcha Yisrael (People of Israel) led by former general Ofer Winter and the (IDF) Reservists, led by former centre-right lawmaker Yoaz Hendel, are both hovering close to the 3.25 per cent threshold required for a minimum of four Knesset seats.
Winter has resisted intense pressure from Netanyahu’s Likud party to quit the race and the argument that if Amcha Yisrael ends up beneath the threshold, the result will be wasted right-wing votes. The Reservists could potentially join either a Netanyahu-led coalition or an Eisenkot government if there is a promise of legislation to draft the ultra-Orthodox.
In such a close contest, much may depend on voter turnout.
[ Sally Rooney’s novels are not easy to find in Israeli bookstores despite their popularity Opens in new window ]
A high turnout will mean Amcha Yisrael and the Reservists will need more votes to cross the threshold.
Arab Israelis make up 21 per cent of the population and traditionally voter participation is significantly lower in comparison to the majority Jewish population – around 53 per cent at the last election compared to 70 per cent overall.
The current Arab parties have 10 seats between them, but polls indicate this could rise to 13 or 14 seats this time round, and both parties are stressing their priority is to replace Netanyahu as prime minister, even if they will be excluded from a governing coalition. Additional reporting: Bloomberg

title: Man arrested in connection with murder of Paul O’Connor in Mallow
description: Postmortem results yet to be released but it is understood the man suffered two gunshot wounds
content:
A man has been arrested in connection with the murder of Paul “Bosco” O’Connor, whose body was found in undergrowth on the banks of the river Blackwater in Ballyellis, Mallow, Co Cork , last Thursday.
The man, who is eastern European, is in his 30s. He was arrested at 6pm on Monday in Mallow.
He is being held in Mallow Garda station under section 50 of the Criminal Justice Act 2007. This allows gardaí to detain suspects for six days.
Paul O’Connor was a native of Connolly Road in Ballyphehane on the south side of Cork city.
His body was discovered by a person out walking last Thursday at about 1.30pm. Gardaí cordoned off the scene for a technical examination.
The results of a postmortem carried out at Cork University Hospital by Assistant State Pathologist Dr Margaret Bolster were not released for operational reasons.
However, it is understood the deceased suffered two gunshot wounds.
It is believed Paul O’Connor travelled from Kent Train Station in Cork city to Mallow station last Wednesday, arriving shortly after 7.20pm.
Gardaí are interested in speaking with anyone who was on the same train. They would also like to speak to anyone who was in the vicinity of Mallow town between 7.20pm on Wednesday and 1.30pm Thursday who may have seen O’Connor.
Gardaí are also interested in speaking with any person who may have been in the vicinity of the banks of the river Blackwater at Ballyellis between 7.20pm last Wednesday and 1.30pm on Thursday.
Any road users or pedestrians who were in the area and who may have camera footage are asked to make this footage available to investigating gardaí.

title: Bread, butter and a slice of cheese: It’s Copenhagen’s coolest breakfast
description: The nouveau Bolle med ost first appeared in a post-peak-pandemic onslaught of bread-baking and have since become a calling card for the city’s best bakers
content:
C openhagen is famed for its innovative gastronomy and elaborate dishes. But these days its hottest food is its most basic: just bread, butter and hard cheese. And Copenhagen’s top bakeries are in a dead heat to make the best one around.
It’s called a bolle med ost (bun with cheese), shortened by many to BMO, an abbreviation that was entered into the biggest Danish dictionary this year.
Often served open-faced, this sort-of-sandwich is all about the fundamentals – sparer than smorrebrod and a test of how sublime the simple can be. That’s a 180 from the best-known Danish cuisine, which has been foraged, fermented and tweezered into submission over the last two decades.
The BMO has become a calling card for Copenhagen’s best bakers. Batch after batch, they experiment with the bread, the cheese and, yes, even the butter as they strive to stand out in a city obsessed with understated excellence. The BMO is hard to mess up, but almost impossible to perfect.
“You can’t pretend with BMOs,” says Anne-Sophie Lahme, a Danish trend researcher who focuses on food. “You can’t fake it. It has to be really, really good.”
Danes grab BMOs almost anytime – after run club, before dates, between meetings. They’re a filling snack and not all that expensive. At many of the top bakeries they sell for about 45 Danish kroner (roughly €6), in line with other baked goods.
Now, thanks to a phalanx of influencers, tourists have it on their must-try list, along with a cardamom bun and a cinnamon bun.
And where there’s hype, there’s optimisation.
Two brothers have written a BMO cookbook with 25 recipes. In June, Burger King released its own “Gourmet BMO”, although this time the “B” stood for burger. And die-hards run Instagram accounts chronicling their search for the ideal specimen. For one popular account, a married couple who are both mathematicians spent months fiddling with an algorithm to fairly compare the bounty.
In July, the Danish newspaper Politiken joined the fray and published a ranking of the city’s 50 best BMOs.
“This is how all Copenhageners tell the quality of a bakery,” says David Dyrholm, the critic who masterminded the list. He’d pitched the project almost as a joke. But to his delight, his editor loved the idea, and Dyrholm found himself surprised by the variety.
“There are thousands of these being sold every day,” he says. “There’s a lot of money made on this. So why not take it seriously ?” Eventually, he ate about 65 bolle med ost, which cost more than 2,000 kroner (about €268).
Because bread is not just bread in Denmark, he had many questions along the way: What type of flour did any given bakery use? Did they mill their own? How long was the ferment? Did they roll the bun in seeds or cornmeal?
And what about the cheese? A beloved Danish cow’s cheese called Gammel Knas? Comté? Should that cheese be presliced or sliced to order? And should the butter be salted? Browned? Whipped?
“I like nerding out about this stuff,” Dyrholm says, a little sheepishly.
[ Chicken-fed salmon is coming to Irish supermarket shelves Opens in new window ]
The nouveau-BMOs first appeared a few years ago, in a post-peak-pandemic onslaught of bread-baking. Sourdough starters passed between friends and new bakeries opened, street by street.
At some point the abbreviation was born, and quickly proved divisive. To sceptics, the nickname sounds a lot like gentrification – dressing up a beloved family food in frippery.
“It is literally just a bun with butter and a slice of cheese,” says Nina Bauer, a Danish food historian.
Claus Meyer, a titan of Denmark’s food scene who co-owns Meyers Bageri, says, “I could not see myself entering a bakery and asking for a ‘BMO’.”
Thomas Spelling, owner of the microbakery Rondo, almost shudders at the idea. “I would never say that myself,” he says.
But he’s fine with customers calling it whatever they want. The bolle med ost is, hands down, Rondo’s bestselling product, he says. He would never retire it. “It would be like opening a bar and not having draft beer,” he says.
BMOs are also the bestseller at Hart, which has 13 locations around Copenhagen and sells 50,000 each month. “It’s its own category,” says Talia Richard-Carvajal, Hart’s creative director. The chain keeps finessing the recipe, she says, trying dozens of cheeses to find the right one and tweaking the bread, in search of a “glass-shard” crunchy crust.
The cheese Gammel Knas almost tells the story of the trend on its own. By 2024, BMOs had become so popular that Gammel Knas supplies began to run low. Danish newspapers reported a “cheese crisis”. Customers raced to stores.
Gammel Knas needs to mature for more than 24 months to develop its signature crunchy protein crystals. But new bakeries kept opening and demanding more cheese. For months, Sofie Biltoft-Riis, the director of Arla Unika, the company that produces the cheese, was in meetings about how to deal with the BMO skyrocket.
“My phone was ringing day and night,” she says. “The whole country went quite crazy.”
Copenhagen may be reaching a BMO plateau. But the snack is still the bestseller at any bakery of repute. No longer as hyped, they’re just part of the fabric of the city.
And locals have perfected eating them. Even though a bolle med ost can be snarfed one-handed, it’s not. At least not by any self-respecting Copenhagener.
[ Menopause and weight gain: What you can do about a ‘frustrating’ symptom Opens in new window ]
I found this out the hard way. I’m from New York City. I can knock back a slice of pizza in a minute flat. So with the first few BMOs I tried, I combined them into a sandwich, and ate quickly and efficiently with both hands.
“That’s the burger method,” says Dyrholm, the Politiken critic.
Two friends set me straight. “It’s just, like, very, very important that you eat it like this,” says Emma Toft Kromann, holding it open-faced.
“If you see someone eating it like a burger, you know they’re not from here,” adds Ophelia Ernland.
A bolle med ost is the elevenses of a city caught between hustle and hygge. It’s a little treat, something to savour, even on the go, even if it’s just bread and butter and cheese.
– This article originally appeared in The New York Times .

title: Ryanair chief Michael O’Leary predicts 20% increase in airfares next year
description: O’Learys says the Middle East conflict will force airlines to pass on increases in fuel costs
content:
Ryanair Holdings chief executive Michael O’Leary predicted a record increase in European air fares next year as the Middle East war continues to drive up oil prices, forcing airlines to pass on their fuel costs to consumers.
Ticket prices are set to increase by as much as 20 per cent next year, O’Leary said on Tuesday during a press conference in Brussels. As a result, airline margins will get squeezed because even the jump in fuel surcharges won’t make up for the higher oil bill, he said.
“You’re going to see the biggest increase in airfares, I would say, in history in Europe in the next 12 months,” O’Leary said. “The question is, will that increase in airfares be enough to cover the dramatically higher oil bills? I don’t think it will be.”
The comments by the head of Europe’s largest budget carrier add to the more pessimistic outlook for the aviation industry, which has been forced to contend with a dramatic jump in costs even as travellers continue to splurge on air tickets.
O’Leary said most European airlines, including his own, lack significant hedging next year to protect against higher oil prices. In addition, there’s less capacity in the market as some airlines struggle, while higher taxes are further dimming the picture for the industry.
[ Ryanair doesn’t expect big delivery delays on Boeing software issue Opens in new window ]
“We’re 85 per cent unhedged next year, and most of the other European airlines are in a similar position,” he said.
Ryanair dropped as much as 2.2 per cent in morning trading in Dublin, bringing the decline to about 25 per cent for the year. At that rate, that would be the worst annual stock return since 2018.
O’Leary used his expletive-laden press conference to dish out against regulation in markets like France and Belgium, where Ryanair will reduce its footprint in response to higher taxes. He reiterated that the European aviation industry will continue to consolidate as weaker players struggle to survive in a high-cost environment.
Air Baltic Corp and Spain’s Volotea are the latest European carriers to undergo restructuring as higher costs take their toll. Last week, Lufthansa won the race against Air France-KLM to acquire a stake in Portugal’s state-owned TAP. Meanwhile, US private equity firm Apollo Global Management is laying out the framework to take over British carrier EasyJet.
Airlines across the world have suffered from soaring jet fuel costs since the Iran war began in late February. Ryanair’s most recent earnings in July showed the conflict hit its profit and caused later bookings amid concern about jet-fuel supply availability.
O’Leary said separately that he aims to receive the first delivery of the carrier’s Boeing Max 10 aircraft in January, with about 16 more expected through April. – Bloomberg

title: Eisiúintí eisceachtúla Éireannacha
description: Tá ionadaíocht éirimiúil á déanamh ag na ceoltóirí seo ar Éirinn ar an ardán náisiúnta agus idirnáisiúnta araon
content:
Tá an Rómánsachas beo beathaíoch. Tá luach faoi láthair ar an bhféiniúlacht, sainiúlacht, agus sainmhíniú pearsanta, agus iad á lorg sa stair, san oidhreacht, sa gcultúr náisiúnta agus pearsanta, ag cur i gcoinne an homaiginithe chultúrtha is baol dúinn sna meáin le linn mhonaplacht seo an teicnealathais.
Ní mise is moltaí faoi chuid den ‘athghabháil’ seo. Ní dóigh liom gur féidir rian an chaipitleachais ná an choilíneachais a ruaigeadh le díol earraí ná féinbholscaireacht. Ach tá ag éirí linn, dé réir a chéile, ár bhfréamhacha a aimsiú, a ainmniú, agus a thabhairt isteach sa ré seo le, tá súil agam, todhchaí níos gile a mhúnlú.
B’fhiú a lua go mbíonn baol comhghuaillíochta ann idir an athghabháil chultúrtha, an t-éilíteachas agus an ciníochas. Is cúis bhróid é go bhfuil ceoltóirí traidisiúnta agus trialacha inár measc ag tíocht ón bpobal, le fréamhacha sa ndúchas, lena gcraobhacha oscailte do nua-Éireannaigh, agus ardán á thabhairt go leanúnach do dhea-chúiseanna in Éirinn agus ar fud an domhain.
…tá sainfhuaim forbartha go cumasach ag Trá Pháidín le fios domhain ceirde maidir lena n-uirlisí, seánraí agus cúrsaí léiriúcháin…
Chuige sin, seo trí nua-eisiúint a léiríonn an dea-chruth atá ar nuacheol na hÉireann, a bhfuil fréamhacha acu sa dtraidisiún, agus féidearthachtaí ollmhóra i ndán do na cruthaitheoirí a bhfuil ionadaíocht éirimiúil á déanamh acu orainn ar ardáin náisiúnta agus idirnáisiúnta:
The Wran - The Stone Man (eisithe an 9 Deireadh Fómhair)
Ba iad The Wran mo phríomhrogha agus ceoltóirí á roghnú d’ardán na Collchoille ag Electric Picnic i mbliana, agus níor cuireadh aon díomá orm. Ba phribhléid dom luathchóip dá n-albam a fháil ag an am agus táim gafa leis ó shin. Is aoibhinn liom nach bhfuil cur i gcéill i gceist leo. Is ceoltóirí cumasacha iad nach bhfuil gá acu le mórthaispeántas ná áibhéil maidir lena n-íomhá ná fuaim. Deartháireacha iad, dlúthnasc atá le cloisteáil sna harmóin shnasta agus cóiriú teann an cheoil. Sileann a mblas féin trí chuile shiolla agus nóta den albam. Níl drogall orthu spás agus am a thabhairt dá bhfoinn, agus is éasca a bheith sciobtha chun siúil in atmaisféar agus rithim na rianta rollacha. Léirítear meas don traidisiún gan a bheith srianta aige. Ní bhraitheann a rianta nuachumtha, Dunford’s March cuir i gcás, as alt ar chor ar bith leis na hamhráin thraidisiúnta atá bailithe acu le scéalta deoraíochta, agus filleadh ar an dúchas, a insint. Buaicphointe is ea an leagan aoibhinn den amhrán sean-nóis Aird Uí Chuain, atá chomh beo ábhartha anois is bhí sna 19ú céad.
Trá Pháidín - Cloch ‘s Claí (eisithe an 25 Meán Fómhair)
“Níl aon ideas fágthaí againne!” arsa bréag-ionadaí TG4 ag deireadh an amhráin Fothrach an Cheirtleáin. Tá féith ghéar ghrinn agus ideas ag Trá Pháidín féin. Níl aon ghné de shaol na nGael slán óna dteanga ghlic - ó eagraíochtaí teanga go na meáin, ó lucht TikTok na hathbheochana go mífhorbairtí tuaithe agus Gaeltachta. Is maith ann é: tá gá le glórtha neamhbhalbha a chuireann ar ár gcluasa fíorchás na nGael idir mhaith agus olc, agus idir cháineadh agus súgradh, ina stíl scigmhagaidh atá dílis do Myles na gCopaleen, fear a bhfuil tagairt dó ar an albam. Tá stangadh agus spraoi in amhráin ar nós Seachtain na Gaeilge agus Anglicize Everything a bhain gáire os ard asam scaití.
Léiriú atá san albam nach gá géilleadh don domhandú (ná don Bhéarla) le haitheantas a thuilleamh, agus nach gá nideog na sainspéiseanna, scéalta, ná in-jokes na nGael (thaitin Plaza Pheig Sayers thar cionn liom) a chaolú le lucht éisteachta a mhealladh. Anuas air sin, cnagairí gan stad na hamhráin. Ní ghéilltear aon chuid den atmaisféar fairsing don ghreann. Tugann a gcumas ceoil cead a gcinn dóibh a rogha rud a rá, agus deirtear go snasta é in éindí le “ceol traidisiúnta na hÉireann, an t-ornáideachas, an tionlacan agus focla smartáilte eile a bhfuil breis is trí shiolla iontu,” dar leo. Cé go ndiúltódh siad d’ardmholadh intleachtúil (agus ní mise is fearr atá cáilithe chuig léirmheastóireacht intleachtúil), is saothar máistriúil gradamúil é seo. Idir iar-rac, snagcheol, agus uirlisí neamhthraidisiúnta fite go snasta i bhfoinn Ghaelacha agus spreagtha ag an gceol traidisiúnta, tá sainfhuaim forbartha go cumasach ag Trá Pháidín le fios domhain ceirde maidir lena n-uirlisí, seánraí agus cúrsaí léiriúcháin atá eisceachtúil, bíodh an ceol á chruthú i nGaeilge nó go deimhin as Béarla.
Mholfainn an ceirnín a cheannach ó Plugd i gCorcaigh - gnó neamhspleách agus an-seirbhís seachadta go deo - ach tá sé ar fáil go forleathan agus ar Bandcamp i bhfoirm dhigiteach leis.
RÓIS - Mo Léan (le atheisiúint le Domino Records, an 20 Samhain)
Bean eile nach ngéilleann ach dá mian féin. Athdhúisíonn Mo Léan seanchleachtas an chaointe le fuinneamh fíochmhar, fuaim shainiúil agus léiriúchán trialach. Tá sé á eisiúint, go domhanda an uair seo, leis an lipéad ceoil Domino. Fiosraítear deasghnátha agus nósanna a bhaineann leis an mbás agus an tórramh san albam speisialta seo le duine de na ceoltóirí is uathúla atá ag cruthú in Éirinn i láthair na huaire. Tá réimse a glóir agus éagsúlacht a cleachtas eisceachtúil ar chuile bhealach, agus is trí thairseach an alltair a mheallann sí an t-éisteoir le suantraithe, caointe, agus rianta ó Sinéad O’Connor agus The Prodigy araon. Speisialta.

title: Alberta voters reject plan for referendum to leave Canada
description: Victory for prime minister Mark Carney after a referendum campaign that created divisions in the country’s oil-rich heartland
content:
Voters in Canada’s Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin a process towards independence, delivering a victory for the prime minister, Mark Carney , and supporters of Canadian unity.
With more than 1.5 million votes counted, 76 per cent supported remaining in Canada, while close to 24 per cent backed beginning a process toward separation, according to unofficial results from Elections Alberta.
Carney, who grew up in Edmonton, said: “Albertans made a clear choice. They chose unity, to build together, and to take care of each other. Above all, Albertans chose Canada.”
He said the result would allow Canadians to move forward together and accelerate efforts to diversify trade, develop major infrastructure projects and make Canada a global energy powerhouse, with Alberta at its centre.
Alberta’s separatists, however, saw a silver lining. “We don’t have the final results. I think the numbers are going to fluctuate, but it is fair to say that at least a quarter of Albertans feel that Alberta needs to be treated better,” said Keith Wilson, a leader of the separatist movement.
The Alberta premier, Danielle Smith, welcomed the early results, saying they showed widespread support for remaining in Canada. “Albertans have voted for a stronger Alberta in a united Canada,” Smith posted on social media.
Even though the vote was not explicitly about independence – a point that frustrated separatists – the ballot question nonetheless exposed divisions in Alberta’s politics and raised questions about the durability of national unity.
[ Alberta is flirting with independence. Is Canada facing a messy break-up? Opens in new window ]
Delays at roughly 100 of the 1,400 at polling stations across the province pushed results back by more than two hours, but shortly after polls closed on Monday evening the results suggested a decisive win for those looking to remain in Canada.
The separation question – whether to remain in Canada or begin a legal process that could lead to a second vote – was one of 10 put to Albertans on Monday. The others covered issues including immigration, healthcare, education and the province’s constitutional powers. Elections Alberta said the remaining results could take days to count.
In the days leading up to the vote, provincial leaders and federal politicians crisscrossed the province to make the case for a unified country.
Carney warned against a vote from residents of the oil-rich province simply looking to “send a message” to the federal government. “A vote against Canada is a dangerous bluff that will lead to years of deep uncertainty and lost opportunities for Albertans and Canadians,” he told an energetic crowd last week.
The Conservative leader, Pierre Poilievre, whose parliamentary seat is in the province, told a crowd of supporters that Albertans were not “quitters”.
“To those people who are thinking about taking out their frustration on the current government by voting for separation in the referendum, I say this: Canada is more than a government,” he said. “It is a people, a flag, a land, a history and a promise.”
Data from Elections Alberta indicated roughly 43 per cent of eligible voters – or 1.3 million Albertans – had already cast ballots before Monday’s vote through advance voting and mail-in ballots. That figure pointed to a potentially higher turnout than the province’s last referendum in 2021.
Smith’s tenure as leader of the United Conservative party is due in large part to separatists within the party who ousted her predecessor, Jason Kenney. In recent months she has tried to placate both the separatists and federalists in the party, in a province where a majority is not interested in secession.
The referendum became a political liability for Smith’s party, whose popular support has tumbled in recent months, including with the loss of a one-time conservative stronghold in a byelection.
Still, members of the separatist movement said they would continue their push for independence.
In an interview before the results, the Calgary mayor, Jeromy Farkas, a staunch opponent of the independence movement, said the city’s “best future is here, as a Canadian city,” amid fears that uncertainty could lead to capital flight.
“I am Canadian because I’m Canadian, not in a transactional way and regardless of the flavour of prime minister,” Farkas said. “And I’m going to continue to make the case for how our future is strongest together, because no result will permanently put this to bed. “The separatist movement sees this as a long-term project.” - Guardian
[ Separatists win Quebec provincial election in blow to Mark Carney Opens in new window ]

title: Data centres plan in Co Waterford refused planning permission after backlash
description: Loss of Kilmeaden’s ‘village character’ would be contrary to local development plans, Waterford City and County Council says
content:
Planning permission sought to transform a former cheese factory site in Kilmeaden, Co Waterford , into a data centre campus has been refused over concerns about its impact on the “character” of the village.
The contentious proposed development, which received hundreds of submissions, was met with significant backlash from locals.
The proposal was submitted to Waterford City and County Council by Crag Rathnew DC Limited, a subsidiary of Irish company Echelon Data Centres, and local property developer Kent Homes in September 2025.
Alongside three data centres, a solar farm with more than 43,000 panels and an energy centre building with 16 gas-powered turbines, it detailed two apartment buildings comprising 48 apartments, alongside offices, a community centre, gym, supermarket and a childcare facility.
Those opposing the plans previously raised concerns over noise, emissions, light pollution, strain on water services and depreciation of house value.
Refusing permission, the council said the applicant failed to demonstrate there was “existing capacity in the electricity grid” to support the development.
It also pointed to a lack of “significant onsite renewable energy” to power the proposed development.
The council said the proposed project would have potential for “significant adverse impacts” on the environment and would be contrary to the sustainable development of the area.
Noting its scale and design, and its proximity to neighbouring homes, the council said the development would result in “excessive visual intrusion” and could also affect the character of Kilmeaden village.
“It is considered that the proposed development would represent a disproportionate impact on the amenities of the area,” it said, adding that “loss of village character” would be contrary to local development plans.
The council also said the site was not served by an adequate wastewater network to accommodate the development.
It said it was also not satisfied the applicant adequately demonstrated the project would not give rise to potential of “flood risk”.

title: Australian MP Helen Haines loses leg as surgeons fight to save the other after alleged attack
description: Helen Haines was rammed twice in an apparent targeted attack
content:
The man accused of attacking Helen Haines allegedly made a U-turn before ramming the independent MP twice in an alleged targeted attack near her electorate office, causing her to lose one of her legs.
The politician was airlifted from Wangaratta in northern Victoria to Melbourne’s Alfred hospital for emergency surgery on Monday night.
Surgeons were on Tuesday fighting to save Haines’ other leg, as the 65-year-old remained in a critical condition.
A 43-year-old Tarrawingee man alleged to have driven the Toyota LandCruiser was arrested at the scene. The alleged attacker is Brendan Nugent, Guardian Australia has confirmed.
Police were expected to interview the suspect on Tuesday, police said.
Australia’s prime minister Anthony Albanese confirmed authorities believed the attack was deliberate.
“Helen Haines represents the best of our political representatives,” the prime minister said on Tuesday afternoon.
“Kind, compassionate, a person of integrity, totally committed to strongly representing the people of that beautiful part of Victoria.”
The home affairs minister, Tony Burke, said witnesses alleged the driver completed a U-turn before the incident.
“What witnesses have described is the driver doing a U-turn to get into the car park and to ram Helen against a vehicle, then to reverse and do it a second time,” he told ABC radio.
“A bystander ran towards the scene, got the driver out of the vehicle and held the driver until police arrived.”
Ricky Jefferies, whose barbershop is next door to Haines’ office, ran from his shop to help after hearing the crash.
“I had no choice but to take him out of the car because it was the right and safest thing to do,” he told reporters on Tuesday morning.
Jefferies, who returned to work on Tuesday morning, alleged the driver had a knife on him. “He didn’t pull it out,” he said. “Basically just … took it out of his pocket and threw it away.”
Burke said: “I think every Australian is grateful for those moments when a hero like this runs towards the most dangerous place.”
The home affairs minister said the nation’s security agencies and police would be working through what more could have been done to prevent the alleged attack and to help keep others safe.
On Monday, Burke reported that there had been 1,067 reports of harassment or threats against high office holders in Australia in the last financial year, an increase from 951 the year before.
“We already knew that we needed to do more to be able to keep people in public office safe and we have been,” he said.
“While we don’t make public the dollar figures and the exact provision of security for obvious reasons … we had a very significant uplift in the budget.
“There is a direct line between the temperature of debate and things willing people will say, and then when people are willing to take action.”
Albanese has been joined by leaders and parliamentarians from across the country in calling for a calming of political discourse.
The mayor of Wangaratta, Irene Grant, expressed gratitude to Jefferies for stepping in to stop the man.
“I spoke to the barber this morning and he just shrugged his shoulders. He seemed to just take it in his stride. This was something that he had to do and he did it,” she said.
“He was extraordinarily modest about the very brave action that he took yesterday … he did an amazing job.”
Wangaratta, the rural city in which the incident occurred, is a tightknit community in north-east Victoria. At the last census it had a population of about 20,000 people, while the broader local government area had just under 30,000.
Haines was elected to federal parliament in 2019 and has been key to the establishment of the National Anti-Corruption Commission, as well as campaigning for rural health services, telecommunications access and pushing back on misuse of taxpayer funds, or pork barrelling. - Guardian

title: Your Open Day checklist: What to ask before choosing a college
description: Here are some questions that may help you get the most out of an open day
content:
Open days are a perfect chance to get a feel for what a third-level institution is really like. They give prospective students an opportunity to explore courses, meet lecturers and current students, and see the campus for themselves.
In The Irish Times today, we have a special pullout to help fifth and sixth year students get the best out of the many upcoming open days by third-level institutions.
And, of course, you can read it all at irishtimes.com/education
Open days are a perfect chance to ask questions.
Before you go, it can help to spend a bit of time thinking about what matters most to you. Is it the course content? Career opportunities? Accommodation? Financial support? Student life?
The answers to these questions could play a big role in where you decide to study.
Try to arrive with a list of things you would like to find out. Take notes as you go, and don’t be afraid to ask follow-up questions if something isn’t clear. Remember, open days aren’t just about colleges making an impression on you, they’re also your opportunity to decide whether a college feels like the right fit.

title: Ag freastal ar an bhfoghlaimeoir fásta
description: Tá fo-sheánra iomlán litríochta ann atá dírithe ar dhaoine fásta atá ag foghlaim na Gaeilge
content:
Pléadh seánra na húrscéalaíochta cúpla seachtain ó shin sa tsraith seo, ach inniu ní mór dúinn aghaidh a thabhairt ar fho-sheánra tábhachtach dá cuid – úrscéalta d’fhoghlaimeoirí fásta. Is fo-shéanra é seo a thugann deis do lucht úsáide na Gaeilge a gcuid taithí litríochta a thabhairt cúpla céim eile ar aghaidh; taisteal ó bheith in ann pionta a ordú go muiníneach nó beannú agus leas a bhaint as a gcúpla focal, chomh fada le léitheoireacht cheart a chur díobh agus iomrascáil den chéad uair go minic le litríocht sa teanga mar dhuine fásta. Bíonn bearna mhór ar uairibh idir an seomra ranga agus an tseilf leabhar, agus ní éiríonn le go leor foghlaimeoirí an bhearna sin a thrasnú.
Saothair ghearra, le plota teoranta dea-scríofa agus dea-mhínithe, is ea na húrscéalta don fhoghlaimeoir fásta; go hiondúil bíonn idir 20,000 agus 25,000 focal in aon leabhar amháin. Mínítear focail dheacra ag bun gach leathanaigh, agus bíonn foclóir/gluais bheag ag deireadh an leabhair. Insítear scéal iomlán amháin i ngach leabhar, agus bíonn líon teoranta carachtar, caibidlí gearra, agus insint bheoga i nGaeilge shimplí iontu. Go minic, baineann ábhair na n-úrscéalta seo le cúrsaí laethúla agus réadúla: an grá, an choir agus — le léargas taitneamhach ar an scéal féin — daoine fásta ag foghlaim na Gaeilge agus mic léinn ollscoile. Is é an focal ‘fásta’ atá lárnach. Bíonn spriocanna ag foghlaimeoirí fásta; bíonn siad neamhspleách agus tugann siad taithí saoil leo chuig saothar ar bith atá le léamh. Ní maith leo go labhrófaí leo amhail is gur leanaí iad. Sin é an fáth go bhfuil Biddy Uí Laoghaire — príomhcharachtar i dtríológ le Alan Desmond (An Foghlaimeoir Fásta (2006), Gaeilge agus Grá (2007), agus An Gaeilgeoir Grámhar (2011)) — chomh tábhachtach sin: bean atá caoga bliain d’aois, gan mórán oideachas foirmiúil aici, a chláraíonn i rang Gaeilge agus a dtagann athrú mór ar a saol dá bharr. Is leagan ficseanúil den léitheoir í féin.
Má chríochnaítear úrscéal — is cuma cé chomh tanaí is atá sé — athraíonn sé an dearcadh atá ag an léitheoir orthu féin…
Tháinig sraith amháin de na saothair seo chun cinn mar gheall ar bhearna a aithníodh sa mhargadh. Iar-eagarthóir sinsearach leis an nGúm, agus eagarthóir le Foclóir Stairiúil na Nua-Ghaeilge san Acadamh Ríoga ab ea Éamonn Ó hÓgáin, a chaith seal ar Bhord na Leabhar Gaeilge. Thart ar thús na mílaoise, mhol sé siúd do Mhairéad Ní Chinnéide, a bhí ag plé go deonach le COMHAR, leabhair a fhoilsiú taobh leis an iris mar nach raibh mórán litríochta ar fáil do dhaoine fásta a bhí ag iarraidh a gcuid Gaeilge a fheabhsú mar a bhí sa Bhreatain Bheag agus i dtíortha eile. Bunaithe ar an gcomhairle sin, chuir an teach foilsitheoireachta neamhbhrabúis tús le sraith de na húrscéalta seo.
Bhain an chéad leabhar, an scéal bleachtaireachta Paloma le Pól Ó Muirí, duais de chuid an Oireachtais amach sa bhliain 2000. Tháinig saothair eile ina dhiaidh sin: scéalta corraitheacha le Mícheál Ó Ruairc, ina measc Trasna na dTonnta (2001); scéalta rúndiamhra agus rómánsacha le Catherine Foley, ar nós Sorcha sa Ghailearaí (2005); Trioblóid (2005) le Colmán Ó Drisceoil (a tháinig le dlúthdhiosca); agus scéal faoi dhídeanaithe sa bhliain 1945 le Peter Härtling, a aistríodh faoin teideal Turas in Éadan na Gaoithe (2005). Tá an raon níos leithne ná mar a thugann an lipéad ‘léitheoireacht éasca’ le fios. Breathnaíonn Teifeach (2002) le Ó Muirí ar chúrsaí dídeanaithe in Éirinn, agus leanann Teach na gColúr (2006) mac léinn ón bPolainn a n-athraíonn a saol nuair a dhéanann sí fiosruithe faoi theaghlach a máthar. Le chéile, tugann siad léargas ar Éirinn a bhí ag athrú go tapa san am sin. Faoin mbliain 2012, bhí cúig úrscéal déag sa tsraith, agus go leor acu tar éis duaiseanna a bhaint ag an Oireachtas. Mhaoinigh Foras na Gaeilge taifeadtaí — ar chaiséad ar dtús agus ar dhlúthdhiosca ina dhiaidh sin — agus tháinig podchraoltaí agus ríomhleabhair ina ndiaidh sin freisin. Faoi aimsir na paindéime, bhí idir fiche agus cúig úrscéal is fiche foilsithe
Tá tábhacht faoi leith leis an seánra seo: bíodh go dtagann líofacht as méid mór ábhar, is cinnte go dteastaíonn uaireanta an chloig leis an nochtadh ceart a bhaint amach ar bhrí focal i gcomhthéacs. Is í an léitheoireacht an bealach is inrochtana chun é seo a dhéanamh, go háirithe don iliomad foghlaimeoirí nach gcloiseann an Ghaeilge á labhairt go tapa ach go hannamh. Ar an ábhar sin, tá sé simplí le háitiú gur fiú níos mó leabhar is féidir leat a chríochnú ná sárshaothar a thréigtear ar an gceathrú leathanach.
Tá an ghné maidir le spreagadh i gceist freisin. Níl aon riachtanas ar fhoghlaimeoirí fásta teacht ar an láthair le bheith ag foghlaim mar atá ar scoil, agus bíonn rath sách ‘luath’ ag teastáil uathu. Má chríochnaítear úrscéal — is cuma cé chomh tanaí is atá sé — athraíonn sé an dearcadh atá ag an léitheoir orthu féin: aistrítear ó bheith i do dhuine atá ag déanamh staidéar ar an nGaeilge chuig duine a bhíonn ag léamh sa teanga. Agus teastaíonn léitheoirí ó litríocht ag gach leibhéal, ní hamháin ag an tairseach is airde. Bíonn sé de bhuntáiste go leathnaíonn an t-úrscéal don fhoghlaimeoir bonn na pirimide teanga sin go mór.
Tá an seánra tar éis a chos a chur i dtír in áiteanna eile freisin. Bhuaigh Gaistí Geilt le Brian Ó Baoill (Coiscéim, 2013) comórtas liteartha Oireachtas Gaeilge Cheanada sa bhliain 2012.
Ní bheadh sé ceart a rá go raibh borradh mór leanúnach faoi na saothair seo ag tráth ar bith. Is réimse ciúin speisialaithe é i gcónaí, agus is obair dhúshlánach í an scríbhneoireacht féin. Is dúshlán é ficsean maith a scríobh laistigh de theorainneacha teangeolaíocha dochta, díreach mar a oibríonn file laistigh d’fhoirm faoi leith. Tá fuaim, podchraoltaí agus sruthú ag dul san iomaíocht anois do thráthnónta na bhfoghlaimeoirí freisin, agus is é sin an fáth gur réamhbhreathnaitheach an cinneadh é dlúthdhioscaí agus taifeadtaí a fhoilsiú le leabhair i dtús na sraithe.
Ní shábhálfaidh an t-úrscéal foghlama an teanga ach an oiread, agus níl aon duine ag maíomh go ndéanfaidh sé amhlaidh. Ach cuireann sé an chéad chéim eile ar fáil don fhoghlaimeoir fásta sin ag aon aois. Do dhuine fásta a bhfuil Gaeilge idirmheánach acu atá gnóthaithe sách crua agus ocras orthu rud éigin le léamh, is doras oscailte é úrscéal gairid maith le gluais ag bun an leathanaigh. Cabhair mhór is ea é freisin chun scoláirí ollscoile a spreagadh nuair nach bhfuil aon chultúr i léitheoireacht na litríochta don phléisiúr thart orthu in aon teanga, Béarla ná Gaeilge san áireamh. Ba chóir do níos mó scríbhneoirí agus léitheoirí siúl tríd an doras oscailte sin, agus ba chóir do níos mó siopaí leabhar na teidil seo a chur ar sheilfeanna san áit a bhfaighidh foghlaimeoirí iad. Is é an chéad leabhar a léitear chun críche i nGaeilge an áit a dtosaíonn an léitheoir rialta.

title: Limerick mayor John Moran contacts gardaí over online death threats
description: Moran says he has been subjected to homophobic comments throughout his tenure so far
content:
The State’s only directly elected mayor has said he has contacted gardaí about a number of threats made against him online.
Mayor of Limerick John Moran said there have been homophobic comments and that he has been called “Cyclops”, referring to his lazy eye, throughout his tenure so far.
Speaking on RTÉ Radio’s Morning Ireland on Tuesday, he said in the last week the abuse had worsened, with threats made against his life.
“It hurts me,” he said. “It hurts probably other people who also have physical differences, to be seeing that people think they can do that. Then you have the clear homophobic references to me, associations that just because you’re a friend of the mayor that you’re also an open target for this.”
Moran said his family had also been worried by the threats, which was “equally tough to know that they’re worrying”.
He said he would be meeting Limerick City and County Council management on Tuesday morning and had also contacted gardaí who were gathering the material from online.
“I spent quite a long time not actually doing anything on this because you just don’t want to make a bigger issue out of something, and in some ways you don’t know will that just encourage you know more people . . .
“In terms of the role of the mayor, it hasn’t necessarily been given the support it might have if you’re an employee in another company or if you’re even a politician at national level. There are supports available. They’re not here locally.”
The Mayor of Limerick has no car or driver or supports for going to meetings, he said.
“That was fine for me for the first while. But now, it makes you think twice when you’re at an event and you go walking up the street to get a taxi just because you are well known, you’re a public figure, and you don’t know what crazies [are] out there.”
Moran said it was important local leaders spoke up against this kind of behaviour “so people realise it’s not appropriate”.
“I think people should reflect on their behaviours,” he added. “You can get angry if you want, but there’s a sort of a false anger or a feeling that you’ve got to be angry to just have proper public discourse and actually talk about stuff.”
He said he had been surprised and disappointed by the abuse directed towards him but hoped “this chapter can be put behind us, and we can just all rally together and actually make sure that for the kids and others, this Christmas is the best Christmas ever”.
Some of the abuse directed towards Moran is understood to have came after the closure of roads in the city centre was announced for the Georgian Christmas markets.

title: A fundamental flaw remains with the Champions Cup
description: Meanwhile, St Patrick’s Athletic’s title chances are all but over after loss in Derry
content:
The Champions Cup has had its lift-off, a successful one too for its Irish contenders, Gerry Thornley reckoning that, on the whole, the tweaks made to its format worked well over the weekend. His chief quibble, though, is that after injecting some life into the season, the competition now returns to hibernation until the second round in December. “Alas, that fundamental flaw remains.”
The focus, then, returns to the URC, Connacht at home to bottom-of-the-table Zebre on Friday, Linley MacKenzie talking to backs coach Gerard Mullen ahead of the game. And Ulster are off to South Africa where they play Pretoria Bulls on Saturday - buoyed by their Challenge Cup win over Zebre last Saturday.
Then there’s the small matter of that Leinster v Munster meeting at the Aviva Stadium , Leinster assistant coach Tyler Bleyendaal hopeful that his side can avoid a repeat of last season’s defeat at Croke Park by his former club. They will, though, be without Jack Conan who injured his shoulder against Clermont - not good news for Andy Farrell who names his squad for the November internationals tomorrow.
In his Whistleblower column, Owen Doyle rates last weekend’s officiating, some of Matthew Carley’s decisions in Leinster’s game prompting a few “invective-laden” text messages from his pals. But Carley got off lightly compared to Owen’s view of the match officials’ fluorescent flamingo pink/canary yellow shirts. Let’s just say, he won’t be buying a replica version for himself any time soon.
In Gaelic games, our techy wizards have produced two highly snazzy interactive maps that let you see the state of each county’s club football and hurling championships. Just hover over the county of your choice and all will be revealed.
Hover over Meath and you’ll be reminded that Wolfe Tones emerged triumphant from the county’s football final at the weekend. Gordon Manning talks to their manager Shane McCoy who will be “leaving no stone unturned” in the effort to rectify Meath’s dire record in the Leinster championship.
St Patrick’s Athletic’s league-winning record is a bit dire itself, it being 13 years since they last won the title. And their hopes of ending that drought are all but over after their defeat by Derry City at the Brandywell on Monday night, Gavin Cummiskey reporting on the game.
In golf, Rory McIlroy has his work cut out if he’s to win a record-equalling eighth Race to Dubai, Philip Reid taking a look at the sparkling form of Spain’s Eugenio Chacarra whose India Championship win sent him to the top of the standings. Did McIlroy play in India to help grow the game there? “Dog shit,” said Kevin Kisner , the player-turned-broadcaster reckoning it was the handsome appearance fee that lured him to Delhi. McIlroy, naturally enough, has responded.
TV Watch : A Champions League group phase game fit for a final: PSG host Barcelona at the Parc des Princes this evening (Virgin Media Two and TNT Sports 2, 8pm). At the same time, Liverpool are at home to Villarreal (Premier Sports 1) and Manchester City meet AEK Athens (TNT Sports 1).

title: Cnuasach filíochta dátheangach eisithe ag Ryan Hennessy
description: Thall is Abhus: Ryan Hennessy; Sperrin Design;   Scoil Gheimhridh Ghaoth Dobhair agus Trá Pháidín
content:
Tá cnuasach filíochta eile scríofa ag an chumadóir amhrán mór le rá Ryan Hennessy, agus an uair seo tá leagan deas Gaeilge le dul le hachan cheann den 32 dán. Is í Póilín Rainsford, bean chéile Jimmy Rainsford ó Picture This, a chuir Gaeilge ar na dánta sa leabhar galánta seo In Another Lifetime.
Ag seoladh an leabhair i mBéal Feirste an tseachtain seo caite, dúirt Hennessy go bhfaigheann sé spreagadh ar leith ó chultúir agus ó theangacha eile timpeall an domhain.
“Tá dúil mhór agam i bhfilíocht agus litríocht na Peirse, cé nach bhfuil focal Peirsise agam. Is breá liom an stíl atá acu. Tá a fhios agam go bhfuil bealaí áirithe le rudaí a rá i nGaeilge nach bhfuil againn sa Bhéarla agus bhí suim agam mo chuid filíochta féin a fheiceáil i dteanga eile. Cheap mé go mbeadh sé cosúil le dearcadh iomlán eile a chur os comhair an lucht léite. Is dóigh gur cic sa tóin atá ann freisin mar gheall nach bhfuil mórán Gaeilge agam féin. Bhí mé i gcónaí ag iarraidh feabhas a chur ar mo chuid Gaeilge. Sílim go bhfuil go leor daoine mar sin, nuair a fhágann siad an scoil agus nach leanann siad ar aghaidh leis an Ghaeilge. Is cinnte go bhfuil náire orm faoi.
“Bhí mé ag iarraidh onóir a thabhairt dár dteanga dhúchais agus glacadh le gach aon seans a bhíonn agam é sin a dhéanamh. Tá an t-ádh orm a bheith in ann an Ghaeilge a scaipeadh agus a chur i lámha daoine eile timpeall an domhain. Tá mé in ann a thaispeáint do dhaoine, ar bhonn idirnáisiúnta, gur fíortheanga í an Ghaeilge agus go bhfuil sí ag bláthú i mbéal an phobail.”
Agus an dara bliain de Sheachtain Faisin na hÉireann tagtha chun críche, is iomaí dearthóir agus stíleálaí Éireannach a tháinig chun cinn ar an ardán le linn na seachtaine. Bhí éadaí ó chuid de na brandaí is mó i dtionscal an fhaisin in Éirinn le feiceáil ann, brandaí cosúil le Paul Costelloe, Aoife Ireland, Sasha Donnellan, Louis Copeland agus Dare to Howl, ach is í Karen Hegarty ó Sperrin Design a sheas amach dom féin go pearsanta.
Is as Contae Thír Eoghain do Karen Hegarty agus dearann sí éadaí comhaimseartha ildaite, a nascann “oidhreacht tuaithe na hÉireann agus fuinneamh fhaisean comhaimseartha na sráide i mBéal Feirste”. Is breá liom go mbíonn na píosaí uilig solúbtha agus is féidir iad a chaitheamh agus a stíleáil ar bhealaí éagsúla, agus tá an t-éadach trom taipéise a úsáideann sí go hálainn ar fad.
Chaith Saoirse-Monica Jackson dungaraithe Sperrin Design i siút Vogue ag tús na bliana seo, agus más aon chomhartha é sin don bhranda, ní i bhfad go mbeidh Sperrin Design i measc na mbrandaí is mó agus is aitheanta sa tír seo.

title: Legal aid dispute escalates as rhetoric ramps up
description: Inside Politics: Jim O’Callaghan’s latest comments were no slip of the tongue and will doubtlessly further rile the solicitors
content:
For months now, there has been a dialogue of the deaf between criminal legal aid solicitors and Minister for Justice Jim O’Callaghan . Now the ante has been unmistakably upped.
To briefly recap: O’Callaghan has overhauled the system for criminal legal aid, introducing a flat fee per trial rather than a payment for each appearance. He has argued that the system led to more appearances and longer trials, with suggestions of sharp practice.
The lawyers responded in the summer by withdrawing some services, saying they were safeguarding the interests of accused persons and their accusers, and the future of the legal aid system.
Months passed, both sides haranguing each other from a distance, with some minor concessions but no substantial progress. On Monday, the solicitors extended their action, expanding the withdrawal of services.
Reporting from the courts on Monday, our legal affairs correspondent Mary Carolan wrote that a senior judge was “coerced” into adjourning six rape and sexual offence trials involving accused people on bail as the dispute escalates.
O’Callaghan has markedly intensified his language – telling RTÉ News on Monday evening that “some solicitors decided to disrupt six rape cases”, and of his concern that “the only cases they sought to disrupt were rape cases that were going on”.
This is no slip of the tongue – he will repeat comments in the same vein in his opening remarks to the Oireachtas justice committee on Tuesday. His words will doubtlessly further rile the solicitors, who reject the assertion.
He also downplayed the impact of the action – while legal practitioners say there has been upheaval. Both these things cannot be true at the same time.
The hope was some sort of fudge could be ironed out over summer, but none came. Now, with the action and the rhetoric ramping up, the respective sides seem more entrenched than ever.
