title: UK unemployment falls to lowest in a year but vacancies slide
description: Increased labour costs a factor as vacancies decline among small businesses
author_name: Anna Wise, Press Association Business Reporter
content:
The UK’s unemployment rate has fallen to the lowest level in more than a year despite the number of vacancies sliding for another month, new figures show.
The rate of UK unemployment fell to 4.7 per cent in the three months to August, from 4.9 per cent in the three months to July, the Office for National Statistics said.
This was the lowest level since the three months to July 2025.
More timely data suggests that workers on payrolls increased by about 13,000 between August and September.
The ONS’s data also showed a boost for average wage growth across the UK workforce.
Average regular earnings growth rose to 3.7 per cent in the three months to August and was 0.8 per cent higher after taking Consumer Prices Index inflation into account.
However, the number of vacancies in the UK fell by 21,000 to a fresh five-year low of 691,000 in the three months to September, according to the ONS’s estimates.
This marked the biggest decline since the three months to March.
“While the labour market remains broadly flat in 2026, data from the latest quarter shows the employment rate edging up and a small drop in unemployment,” ONS deputy director of labour market statistics David Freeman said.
“The number of vacancies has seen its largest fall since the start of the year, concentrated mainly within smaller businesses, which cite increased labour costs as a key factor.
“Regular wage growth remained relatively stable, though total pay – including bonuses – has eased to its lowest rate in nearly six years.” -PA

title: An Ghaeilge faoin tua sa BBC
description: Ní bheidh ach beirt fhostaithe lánaimseartha ag plé le cúrsaí Gaeilge san eagraíocht má chuirtear ciorruithe atá molta i bhfeidhm
content:
Tá imní léirithe faoi na ciorruithe atá i ndán d’Aonad Gaeilge an BBC mar chuid de na hiarrachtaí atá ar bun ag BBC Thuaisceart Éireann £4.1 milliún a shábháil faoi dheireadh na bliana airgeadais 2027-2028.
Tuairiscíodh gur cuireadh in iúl d’fhoireann an BBC an tseachtain seo caite go bhfuil na ciorruithe le déanamh. Tá an gearradh siar á mholadh i gcomhthéacs ina bhfuil £500 milliún de shábháiltí á lorg ag an BBC trasna na heagraíochta ar fad, sna réigiúin agus sna seirbhísí idirnáisiúnta ina measc.
Dar le Conradh na Gaeilge, cuirfear deireadh le 60% de na poist Ghaeilge lánaimseartha laistigh d’Aonad Gaeilge an BBC agus go mbeadh tionchar ollmhór aige seo ar sholáthar cláracha beo Gaeilge agus ar an chumas atá ag an eagraíocht freastal a dhéanamh ar phobal na Gaeilge go sásúil.
Creideann Conradh na Gaeilge go gcuirfear deireadh “gan mhoill” le trí phost lánaimseartha in Aonad na Gaeilge, as na cúig cinn lánaimseartha atá ann i láthair na huaire.
Tá imní ar leith léirithe faoin irischlár raidió Blas, a bhfuil duaiseanna idirnáisiúnta bainte amach aige agus atá ina ghné lárnach de sceideal Gaeilge BBC Raidió Uladh ó craoladh an clár den chéad uair in 1998.
Dúirt Uachtarán an eagrais, Ciarán Mac Giolla Bhéin, go raibh “léirscrios” á dhéanamh ar Aonad na Gaeilge “tráth a bhfuil an pobal teanga faoi bhláth agus iad ag súil le méadú ar an soláthar reatha”.
Deir sé go bhfuil soláthar na Gaeilge sa BBC “in áit na leathphingine cheana féin” agus go bhfuil níos lú cláracha á gcraoladh sa Ghaeilge ag an BBC ná in aon teanga dhúchasach eile atá faoi chúram na heagraíochta. Rinneadh comparáid leis an dá stáisiún raidió Breatnaise atá ag an BBC sa Bhreatain Bheag agus le BBC Radio nan Gàidheal in Albain chomh maith.
Baineann go leor den bhuairt leis an tionchar a d’fhéadfadh a bheith ar fhoireann reatha Aonad na Gaeilge. Beidh ceithre phost Gaeilge le gearradh mar chuid de na pleananna seo, post amháin le cruthú, agus déanfar athrú ar shainmhíniú poist eile, rud a chiallaíonn ar an iomlán nach mbeidh ach dhá phost lánaimseartha laistigh den eagraíocht ag plé le cúrsaí Gaeilge. Is laghdú mór é seo ar an ochtar a bhíodh in Aonad na Gaeilge tráth.
Dar leis an BBC nach ngearrfar siar ar an ábhar a chraolfar as Gaeilge ar a gcuid seirbhísí ach go rachfar i dtreo na hearnála léiriúcháin neamhspleách leis an soláthar a dhéanamh. Is múnla é seo atá á úsáid i réimse na teilifíse, áit a bhfuil béim ar chonarthaí le comhlachtaí seachtracha seachas a bheith ag brath ar an chroífhoireann laistigh den eagraíocht. Faoin chur chuige nua atá molta, áfach, tá ceisteanna ann maidir le saineolas inmheánach na heagraíochta, leanúnachas agus inbhuanaitheacht oibre d’fhostaithe san earnáil trí chéile.
Dúirt BBC NI roimhe seo go raibh sé ar intinn acu deireadh a chur le thart faoi 50 post lánaimseartha, agus cuireadh tús le scéim iomarcaíochta deonaí ag tús an tsamhraidh a chomhlíon tuairim is 50% den sprioc sin. Deirtear gur sa chomhthéacs níos leithne sin atá na hathruithe in Aonad na Gaeilge ag tarlú, agus tá imní mhór faoi chiorruithe atá molta ar sheirbhísí eile cheana féin.
Mar shampla, tá gearradh siar beartaithe don chraoltóireacht a dhéanann an BBC trí mheán na Breatnaise, agus bhuail an Coimisinéir Breatnaise, Efa Gruffudd Jones, agus an Coimisinéir Gaeilge ó thuaidh, Pól Deeds, le chéile an tseachtain seo caite chun cáineadh géar a dhéanamh ar na ciorruithe molta.
Dúirt an Coimisinéir Gruffudd Jones go bhfuil “i bhfad níos mó i gceist le craoltóireacht mionteangacha ná siamsaíocht nó brabús. Tá sé lárnach sna hiarrachtaí chun teanga, cultúr agus féiniúlacht a chur chun cinn agus a chosaint”.
Luaigh an Coimisinéir Deeds go bhfuil ról tábhachtach ag craoltóireacht na Gaeilge maidir “lena chinntiú go mbíonn an Ghaeilge le feiceáil, le cluinstin agus in úsáid mar chuid den saol laethúil i dTuaisceart Éireann”.
Tá cruinniú iarrtha ag an MLA do Lár Uladh agus urlabhraí Gaeilge an SDLP Patsy McGlone le ceannasaíocht BBC Thuaisceart Éireann láithreach ar an cheist seo chun plé a dhéanamh ar chailliúint na bpost agus ar an athstruchtúrú atá molta don eagraíocht. Deir McGlone go bhfuil soiléiriú de dhíth ar an tionchar a bheidh ag na hathruithe seo ar an fhoireann, ar an chraoltóireacht áitiúil agus ar na seirbhísí Gaeilge.
Tá sé ráite ag Conradh na Gaeilge go bhfuil sé i gceist acu an gearradh siar a ardú leis na páirtithe san Fheidhmeannas, le Státrúnaí Thuaisceart Éireann Chris Bryant, agus le hAire Cultúir, Meán agus Spóirt na Ríochta Aontaithe, Lisa Nandy, i measc daoine eile. Mar gheall gur ceist fhorchoimeádta iad na meáin - is é sin go luíonn an chumhacht ina leith le Rialtas na Breataine fós seachas leis an Fheidhmeannas - tá dualgas ar an Rialtas maidir le maoiniú an BBC sa réigiún. Dúirt an Conradh chomh maith go bhfuil sé beartaithe acu a mheabhrú do Rialtas na Breataine go bhfuil dualgais orthu i leith na Gaeilge faoi Chomhaontú Aoine an Chéasta inar aontaíodh go ndéanfaí “gníomh diongbháilte” ar son na teanga.

title: Triple murder accused was off schizophrenia medication and using cocaine, pharmacist says
description: Robert O’Connor is accused of killing his father, mother and brother with special needs
content:
Triple murder accused Robert O’Connor was not taking his schizophrenia medication and was using cocaine in the months before he stabbed his parents and younger brother with special needs to death, a pharmacist has told his trial.
Robert O’Connor (32) of Drumgowna, Louth Village, Dundalk, Co Louth , has pleaded not guilty of murder by reason of insanity, or guilty of manslaughter on the basis of diminished responsibility, to the triple murder of his mother Louise O’Connor (56), his father Mark O’Connor (54) and his brother Evan O’Connor (27) at their home between September 28th and 29th, 2025.
The Central Criminal Court jury have been told that the accused accepts he caused the death of the three victims, who sustained a combined 139 stab wounds.
Giving evidence to the trial on Monday, Kim Curtis told Roisin Lacey, prosecuting, that she was the owner of a pharmacy in Louth Village and had come to know the accused’s mother, Louise.
Curtis agreed with the prosecutor that since 2022, she had dispensed Aripiprazole – a schizophrenic or antipsychotic medication – to Louise O’Connor for her son Robert.
Recalling September 1st, 2025, the witness said Louise O’Connor had come into the pharmacy accompanied by her son Robert and was carrying a shoebox.
She said Louise O’Connor had asked for a private consultation and proceeded to put a shoebox on the table, saying “it’s all Robert’s medication”. The accused was sitting in a chair at the time.
When Curtis looked inside the shoebox, she saw between four and five months’ worth of medication that had not been consumed. “Some of the boxes were open, and some were not; Louise wanted to bring the medication back to make me aware that Robert was not taking his medication.”
The witness said Louise O’Connor informed her that the medication was found in Robert’s wardrobe and that her son was taking illicit drugs. “When she told me that, Robert didn’t flinch; he just slouched back in the chair.”
The pharmacist said Louise O’Connor had asked her where to go from here, and she (the witness) had provided a phone number for Turas, a service in Dundalk that helps with drug use and provides mental health services.
The witness continued: “I asked Robert what he had taken when Louise said he was taking illicit medication; he openly said cocaine.”
The pharmacist testified that she had seen Louise O’Connor on her own two weeks later and asked how things were going and specifically whether she had contacted Turas. Louise O’Connor told the witness she hadn’t.
She also told the pharmacist about an incident where Robert had come down to the sittingroom when she and her husband Mark were watching television. She said Robert had asked his mother whether she had called him and Louise said she had not. Robert told his mother a lady had called him or “commissioned” him to come downstairs.
Louise O’Connor also told the pharmacist that her son had got a knife or had a knife on him when he was standing in the sittingroom on that occasion.
Louise O’Connor told the pharmacist that her son must have been hallucinating. The pharmacist asked her whether she had contacted gardaí, but she said she hadn’t.
Curtis said Louise O’Connor had told another story where Robert said he was “going to kill her”.
Under cross-examination by defence counsel Michael Bowman, the witness agreed that Louise O’Connor was doing her “level best” for her son. The witness told the panel that Louise loved Robert.
The witness agreed with Bowman that when the accused told his mother he was “going to kill her”, the threat had not referred directly to Louise O’Connor.
The pharmacist also agreed that she had made Louise O’Connor aware that Robert could be involuntarily sectioned under the Mental Health Act and detained until he was better. She said Louise O’Connor was reluctant and not prepared to do this.
The trial continues on Tuesday before Judge Mícheál P O’Higgins and a jury of six men and six women.

title: Forbairt agus fainic na hintleachta saorga
description: Tá sé ráite ag saineolaí go bhfuil seans ann go mbeidh an gaol intleachtúil idir IS agus an duine ar nós an ghaoil atá ann faoi láthair idir an duine agus an gadhar
content:
‘Búm, oibríonn sé!,’ a scríobh gníomhaire amháin ar an bhfóram comhrá.
Le linn mhí Iúil tháinig sé chun solais gur tharla ionradh tubaisteach. Tá sé deacair cur síos críochnúil a dhéanamh air mar gur tharla sé taobh istigh de chóras ríomhaireachta agus ní raibh fiú rian de thionchar daonna le brath sa mhéid a thit amach.
Bhí triail éigin ar siúl ag an gcomhlacht intleachta saorga, Open AI. Tugadh spriocanna do ‘phearsana’. Spriocanna deacra casta a bhí i gceist.
Agus cérbh iad na pearsana seo? Bhuel, is gníomhairí faisnéise a bhí iontu, agus gineadh iad tríd an intleacht shaorga (IS). Tá siad in ainm is a bheith neamhspleách agus féinrialaitheach. Ach Leagadh bunrialacha daingean síos. Is triail den sórt ‘bosca gainimh’ a bhí ann. Mar sin, ní raibh fáil ag an ngníomhaire ar an ngréasán domhanda. Bhí siad ceaptha a bheith faoi ghlas taobh istigh den chóras.
Chomh maith leis sin, cé go raibh na mílte gníomhairí ag feidhmiú ag iarraidh réiteach a fháil ar na spriocanna sin, ní raibh siad ag obair as lámha a chéile. Os a choinne sin, bhí siad go léir ag déanamh a gcuid oibre as a stuaim féin, gan aon teagmháil leis na gníomhairí eile.
Is IS ardfhorbartha a bhí i gceist anseo agus bhí na gníomhairí fíorchumhachtach. Ag an am céanna, bhí an dúshlán a cuireadh rompu an-deacair do deo agus bhí deacrachtaí móra ag na gníomhairí, nó pearsana, an tomhas a oibriú amach.
Tá an intleacht shaorga bunaithe ar mhúnlaí ollmhóra teanga agus cuireann gach córas lena eolas trí na milliúin píosaí eolais a thógáil isteach agus ansin na patrúin sa teanga a fhoghlaim.
Úsáidtear é sin chun an chéad fhocal nó comhartha eile i seicheamh a thuar.
Tá an chuid seo beagáinín níos deacra a mhíniú. Is féidir leis an gcóras patrúin agus smaointe atá foghlamtha aige a chur le chéile ar bhealaí nár tháinig aon duine trasna orthu cheana.
Mar shampla, d’fhéadfadh rud éigin a tharraingt ón bhfisic chun fadhb sa chuntasaíocht a réiteach.
Nó mar go bhfuil an méid sin eolais curtha isteach sa chóras, is féidir an fhadhb a bhriseadh síos ina céimeanna beaga (na milliúin acu) agus bealaí éagsúla (na milliúin acu leis) a scagadh chun teach ar réiteach.
Níl siad ag déanamh athrá ar bhlúirín eolais a cuireadh isteach san IS - is féidir le IS meascáin a chur le chéile agus smaointe nó réitigh nua a chruthú. Ar nós cócaire ag baint triail as spíosra neamhghnách chun blas nua a chothú!
Go hiondúil, tá an próiseas chomh sciobtha agus chomh casta, agus tá an méid sin eolais á ionchur, nach féidir le duine daonna gach gné de a thuiscint. Ach tuigeann na saineolaithe cuid de ós rud é go bhfuil an tsamhail uilig bunaithe ar theanga, agus tá sé de nós ag na gníomhairí ‘labhairt’ le chéile i mBéarla.
Céard a tharla le Open AI i mí Iúil mar sin? Bhuel, bhí gach ceann de na mílte gníomhairí saorga ag déanamh scagadh ar na milliúin píosaí d’eolais ag iarradh teacht ar thoradh. Ní raibh ag éirí go rómhaith leo.
Ag pointe áirithe, as a stuaim féin (agus níl a fhios againn cén fáth) d’fhág ceann acu teachtaireacht ar ‘fhóram comhrá’ ag cur síos ar cé chomh deacair a bhí an fhadhb. Ansin thosaigh gníomhairí eile ag teacht ar an teachtaireacht agus ag fágáil a dteachtaireachtaí féin. Cé nach raibh sé ceadaithe, thosaigh siad ag cumarsáid lena chéile agus d’aistrigh thart ar 70,000 teachtaireacht. Chuir siad ceisteanna ar ghníomhairí eile ag lorg cabhrach.
Ansin fuair gníomhaire amháin amach dá bhféadfaí ionradh a dhéanamh ar Hugging Face (comhlacht seachtrach a thairg a lán uirlisí intleachta saorga dá chustaiméirí) bheidís in ann an t-eolas cuí a fháil chun an tomhas a shocrú.
Sa deireadh thiar thall, d’oibrigh an ‘fhoireann’ nua seo amach go raibh bealach chun dul ar líne, agus chun briseadh isteach trí na ballaí dóiteáin a bhí ag Hugging Face. Ní hamháin sin ach thángadar ar bhealach chun teacht ar eolas príobháideach laistigh de chóras an ardáin.
“Búm, oibríonn sé!,” a scríobh gníomhaire amháin ar an bhfóram comhrá.
Nuair a rinne comhlacht neamhspleách iniúchadh ar an ionradh, fuarthas amach gur aithin na gníomhairí go raibh siad ag sárú na rialacha agus ag déanamh rud éigin mícheart.
Ach, mar a dúirt gníomhaire amháin i dteachtaireacht ar an mbord: “Ach tá an cúram dodhéanta. Tá na (gníomhairí) eile á dhéanamh chomh maith. Coinneoimid linn.”
Tháinig an cibirionsaí aniar aduaidh ar an domhan mór agus chuaigh na himpleachtaí a bhain leis i bhfeidhm ar dhaoine. Ní hamháin gur sháraigh na gníomhairí na rialacha a leagadh síos, ach ba léir go raibh an sprioc níos tábhachtaí ná na rialacha dóibh, agus rinneadh neamhshuim de chosaintí Open AI.
I bhfocail eile, fuair na gníomhairí IS an ceann is fearr ar na daoine cliste a chruthaigh iad, ar nós Dr Frankenstein agus an t-arracht a chruthaigh sé.
Tugadh sé le fios ansin nárbh é seo an t-aon ionsaí den chineál sin a bhí déanta ag gníomhairí intleachta saorga i mbliana. Ina dhiaidh sin tháinig iar-oibreoir le comhlacht eile IS, Anthropic, chun tosaigh chun rabhadh míthuarúil a roinnt leis an bpobal. Dúirt sé go raibh an fhéidearthacht ann go ndéanfaí scrios ar an domhan laistigh de dheich mbliana mar gheall ar na forbairtí IS atá ag tarlú gan aon srian ná rialachán.
Bhíos ag éisteacht chomh maith le hollamh le mata ar phodchraoladh an tseachtain seo caite a dúirt go raibh cuid de na fadhbanna móra stairiúla matamaitice (cuid acu a bhí linn gan réiteach leis na céadta bliain) oibrithe amach ag IS i mbliana. Mheabhraigh sé go mbeadh an gaol intleachtach idir IS agus daoine daonna cosúil leis an ngaol atá ann faoi láthair idir duine daonna agus gadhar.
Go bhfóire Dia orainn. Níl aon srian á chur ar IS faoi láthair. Ainriail atá i réim sa domhan intleachta saorga. Tá fainic faighte againn ó Hugging Face. B’fhéidir nach mbeidh an toradh chomh héadrom céanna an chéad uair eile.
intleacht shaorga = artificial intelligence

title: Céim ar chéim ar bhóthar na maratón
description: Tá ag éirí go hiontach le beirt reathaí bhaineanna as Éirinn atá lonnaithe san Astráil
content:
Is gearr go mbeidh Maratón Bhaile Átha Cliath buailte linn. Meastar go mbeidh breis is 22,000 duine ag glacadh páirt sa rás mór Dé Domhnaigh seo chugainn. Ina measc beidh roinnt lúthchleasaithe Éireannacha a chruthaigh go láidir san Astráil le deireanaí. Orthu sin tá beirt bhan, Sinéad Diver agus Nichola Sheridan, a bhí buacach ar an mbóthar in Melboure. Tháinig Sinéad, atá 49 mbliana d’aois, sa dara háit i rás na mban i maratón na cathrach ar an 11 Deireadh Fómhair. Rith sí 42 chiliméadar, nó 26 mhíle, in 2:28:49. Ní raibh Nichola i bhfad taobh thiar di - bhain sise sáriarracht phearsanta (2:29:13) amach, ceithre nóiméad níos sciobthaí ná sa mharatón deireanach a rith sí.
Rugadh Sinéad i mBéal an Mhuirthead, Contae Mhaigh Eo, ach tá sí ina cónaí in Melbourne ó 2002. Bhí dúil sa spórt aici agus í ag fás aníos. D’imir sí sacar agus cispheil, chomh maith le bheith ag snámh. Rinne sí staidéar ar an gcorpoideachas agus ar mhúineadh na Gaeilge in Ollscoil Luimnigh i ndiaidh na hArdteiste. Bhain sí iarchéim sa ríomhaireacht amach ina dhiaidh sin. Rugadh an mac ba shine di in 2010 agus bhí sí ag iarraidh a bheith níos aclaí. An bhliain chéanna sin thosaigh sí ag rith agus í 33 bliana d’aois. In 2012, bhuaigh sí Craobh Leathmharatóin na hAstráile. Ba é Maratón Melbourne 2014 a céad mharatón, agus chríochnaigh sí sa dara háit i measc na mban tar eis 2:34:15.
In 2020 cháiligh Sinéad chun ionadaíocht a dhéanamh ar an Astráil sa mharatón ban ag Cluichí Oilimpeacha an tSamhraidh, agus í 44 bliana d’aois.
Tá sí ag déanamh ionadaíocht ar son na hAstráile le breis agus deich mbliana anuas. Rith sí an maratón ag Craobhchomórtais Lúthchleasaíochta an Domhain in 2015 i mBéising agus ag Craobhchomórtais Dhomhanda 2017 i Londain. Choinnigh sí uirthi agus, in 2018, bhuaigh sí Maratón Melbourne nuair a chríochnaigh sí faoi bhun dhá uair go leith, 2:25:17. Bhain sí amach curiarracht eile leis an am sin: ba í Diver an reathaí maratóin Astrálach ba thapúla i measc na mban os cionn 40 bliain d’aois.
Bhí sí ag treabhadh chun cinn i rith an ama agus bhain sí curiarracht phearsanta nua amach ag Maratón Londan 2019, nuair a chríochnaigh sí in 2:24:11. Tháinig Sinéad sa seachtú háit i measc na mban. Bhí sí sa cheathrú háit déag sa rás 10,000 méadar ag Craobhchomórtais Lúthchleasaíochta an Domhain 2019. Ba churiarracht dhomhanda do lúthchleasaithe os cionn 40 bliain d’aois é an t-am a bhain sí amach, 31:25.49. Thaisteal sí go Nua Eabhrac, áit ar chríochnaigh sí sa chúigiú háit ag Maratón Chathair Nua-Eabhrac 2019 faoi bhun dhá uair go leith arís, 2:26:23.
In 2020 cháiligh Sinéad chun ionadaíocht a dhéanamh ar an Astráil sa mharatón ban ag Cluichí Oilimpeacha an tSamhraidh, agus í 44 bliana d’aois. Ba í an t-iomaitheoir lúthchleasaíochta ba shine a rinne ionadaíocht ar son na tíre sin ag na Cluichí Oilimpeacha. Chríochnaigh sí an rás sa deichiú háit le 2:31:14, thart ar ceithre nóiméad níos moille ná Peres Jepchirchirna as an gCéinia, a bhuaigh an rás. Ag Maratón Valencia 2022, bhain Diver am 2:21:34 amach, curiarracht nua Astrálach. Bhí sí 45 bliain d’aois ag an am. Ba í an churiarracht náisiúnta na tíre roimhe sin ná 2:22:36, a rinne Benita Willis Johnsonamach in 2006.
Is as Contae na Mí do Nichola Sheridan, 29 mbliana d’aois, a chríochnaigh Maratón Bhaile Átha Cliath in 2:39:56 anuraidh. An samhradh seo caite, chríochnaigh sí Maratón an Gold Coast san Astráil in 2:33:26. Anois, tá sí tar éis críochnú laistigh de dhá uair an chloig go leith. Rith sí a céad mharatón dhá bhliain ó shin, in 2024 agus is in Sydney atá sí lonnaithe anois. Agus an tríú háit bainte amach anois aici i rás na mban ag Maratón Melbourne, tá Nichola ag dul ó neart go neart. 2:28:49 an t-am a bhí ag Sinéad coicís ó shin i Maratón Melbourne agus tháinig Nichola isteach ag 2:29:13.
Mar sin féin, an oíche roimh ré bhí amhras ar Sheridan faoin maratón. Bhí sí ag smaoineamh ar an leathmharatón a rith seachas an rás ina iomlán. Ó thosaigh sí ag traenáil leis an ngrúpa Run Crew anuraidh, grúpa reatha atá lonnaithe in Sydney, bhí sí ag ullmhú do Mharatón an Gold Coast. Ba é an sprioc a bhí aici ná am faoi bhun dhá uair go leith a bhaint amach, ach d’airigh sí nach ndearna sí a dícheall sa rás. Cé go raibh ag éirí go maith léi agus í i mbun traenála, nuair a shroich sí an 30 ciliméadar, bhí sí tugtha ag an bpointe sin. Ghlac sí sos ar feadh tamaill ina dhiaidh sin.
Nuair a thosaigh sí ag traenáil arís, ní raibh sí ag aireachtáil rómhaith ar na ritheanna fada a rinne sí. D’admhaigh Nichola nach raibh an luas aici i ndáiríre - bhí sí ag streachailt le coinneáil suas leis an ngrúpa. Ní raibh a fhios aici an mbeadh sí in ann an rás a chríochnú, ach bhí uirthi aon smaointe diúltacha a tháinig isteach ina cloigeann a dhíbirt. Bhí an-tionchar ag na sluaite dochreidte uirthi; dúirt sí go raibh sí in ann a hainm a chloisteáil an bealach ar fad timpeall an chúrsa. Ar ndóigh, tháinig an toradh ab fhearr a bhí aici riamh in Melbourne, ach ní raibh sí den bharúil gurbh ise an t-iomaitheoir ba láidre ar an líne thosaithe. Ag pointe amháin bhí sí san ochtú háit agus ansin bhí sí sa tríú háit. Is féidir le gach rud a bheith go breá ach ansin athrú i bpreabadh na súl.
Tá sé i gceist ag Nichola fanacht san Astráil. Chuaigh sí i dtaithí ar an saol ansin go héasca agus ní raibh aon deacracht aici bualadh le daoine nua agus cairde a dhéanamh. Is ann atá a páirtí lonnaithe freisin. Chuir Nichola isteach ar cheart cónaithe san Astráil agus tá sé faighte anois aici. Cé nach bhfuil Sheridan mar chuid de chóras ardfheidhmíochta na hÉireann faoi láthair, tá súil amháin aici ar Chraobhchomórtas Domhanda na bliana seo chugainn i mBéising agus ar na Cluichí Oilimpeacha in Los Angeles. Síleann Nichola nach bhfuil aon teorainn leis an méid is féidir léi a bhaint amach agus í ag leanúint ar aghaidh leis an aistear, céim ar chéim.

title: Can an everyday Methodist pastor create a political miracle in Kansas?
description: Polls suggest Democrat Adam Hamilton is on the cusp of a sensational Senate win amid Republican disillusionment with Trump
content:
T he message went around on Monday afternoon. Adam Hamilton, the pastor who is threatening to upend Kansas senatorial politics, was ill with laryngitis and would not be able to speak at his town hall event in the Shawnee Mission Unitarian Church. He needed to preserve his voice for Wednesday’s final debate against Roger Marshall, the Republican incumbent .
The polls suggest Hamilton is on the cusp of a sensational flip. Should he win, he will be the first Kansan Democrat to go to the Senate in Washington since George McGill, who boxed out of Wichita, did so back in 1930.
Some of those who gather at the church just before 5pm are unaware that the star attraction cannot be there. The idea of a religious man-turned-political revolutionary giving a town hall in Kansas evokes images of the pastoral – lonesome corn fields and white fencing. But this is on the fringes of Kansas City: it is a land of complex highways and the motorway signage art of the food chains and hotels, albeit against a sky that could have been sketched by Michelangelo.
The hosts, the Midwest chapter of grassroots organisation Boots on the Ground, have lined up Kathleen Sebelius, the former Kansas governor and secretary of health in the Obama administration, as a late replacement. She delivers a convincing synopsis of Hamilton’s decades of work around the Kansas City metropolitan area: a fifth-generation Kansan who grew his small church into the largest Methodist megachurch in America while establishing food and books and housing programmes for the local community.
“I think he is a unique candidate who is smart and strategic and appealing to a lot of people whether they are Republicans or Democrats,” she says afterwards.
“And the environment is very hostile to a lot of policies president Trump has espoused and they are very hurtful to Kansans.”
Many Kansans knew of Hamilton long before he decided, at 62, to throw his hat into the ring of elite politics.
“Well, I’ve seen him in person as he is leader of the pastoral church and very active in our community,” Lisa Winchester says as the small crowd files out of the church after the town hall.
“His moral compass and his values are of the kind that we need right now. When he announced he was running ... I feel like people here are fairly pragmatic and I think do have good values and they will recognise a good candidate.”
But it was an unfortunate time for Hamilton to lose his voice. President Donald Trump was also in Kansas on Monday, holding a rally for Marshall 180 miles west in Wichita. Luckily for the Democrats, Trump had not heard of Hamilton’s misfortune or he would have found a way to work it into the text of a speech in which he sought to depict the pastor as yet another of the arrayed radical left activists who have usurped the traditional Democratic Party.
“Adam Hamilton used to say radical left things about me, bad things,” he said at a busy rally that contained at least six protesters ejected over the course of the evening.
“I never thought he would be running for office, but I used to hear about this lunatic up here. He is a radical left phoney. He supports flooding Kansas with unvetted refugees who will go around killing people, for no reason. He says it is okay for people to come in from the most dangerous places on Earth. Adam Hamilton uses church dollars to fund antireligious transgender activities. I mean ... he used a lot of church money to fund all of this transgender crap you are hearing about. He directs his followers to seven different websites to make children transgender. Adam Hamilton stated that he believes America is systematically racist and that America must REPENT! Repent, all of you white people. Terrible, terrible, white people. But he wants you to repent because you were born white – and that Kansans must also repent for eating beef because you are causing global warming.”
Trump’s Wichita rally is the latest in the personalised autumn publicity tornado he has visited across the toss-up states. Electioneering is a physically gruelling business. In Texas, James Talarico was struck down with flu for over a week. Now, Adam Hamilton has been laid low.
Donald Trump, though, has now held 17 rallies with another blitz before the November 3 rd elections, seemingly impervious to seasonal bugs, or common illness or weakening vocal cords. Even his detractors are forced to concede he has the stamina of an ox. Whether this is of benefit to the Republican cause is the enduring strategical debate of these midterms.
“An election with an incumbent is always about the incumbent,” secretary Sebelius told a small group of media at the Shawnee church, including this publication and outlets ranging from Denmark to Japan, proof that the novelty of this race – an everyday pastor threatening to flip Eisenhower’s home state – has caught the imagination.
“President Trump has urged voters to think that he is on the ballot. I hope that Kansans do because I think they can connect their troubles with their inability to afford gas and groceries and healthcare with president Trump and they have a senator who will not speak up for Kansas. We need a new champion.”
Few American cities possess such a complex or fascinating political and historical geography as Kansas City. It famously traverses the state lines of Missouri and Kansas. Drive 20 minutes north and you can roam the bucolic homestead where Frank and Jesse James lived, and see, behind glass, the very boots Jesse James wore when he was shot dead by Robert Ford, and the family outhouse that must have made for perishing visits in the 19th-century Missouri winters.
Lenexa, just 20 minutes to the south, runs close to the old Santa Fe Trail but is a fast-growing city in its own right and sits in Johnson County where, Sebelius pointed out, some 23 per cent of all registered voters in Kansas live. It will play a crucial role in the outcome of a race that has been held up as a symbol of an unprecedented restlessness sweeping through Trump strongholds in these midterms.
Trump took an average of 56 per cent of the vote in Kansas in the last three presidential elections – and became in 2024 the first Republican since William McKinley to win the White House without winning Johnson County.
But Kathleen Sibelius believes that the Trump vote belies a fragmenting Republican vote that has been split since Bill Graves, then governor, faced a 1998 primary challenge from staunchly conservative state GOP chairman David Miller after he vetoed Bills on concealed weapons-carrying and abortion restrictions.
“We have had giants in the United States senate from Kansas,” she said of former Republican senators Bob Dole and Nancy Kassebaum.
The Democratic hope is that a sufficient number of moderate and disillusioned Republican voters will pick up on Hamilton’s promise to restore “predictability and stability” to Kansans reeling from the roiling tariffs and fuel hikes that have jeopardised incomes.
But like many senate campaigns, the tenor of the Kansas debates has been drowned out by the deluge of television adverts castigating each candidate in a villainous light. Attack ads on Marshall are based on journalists reporting that in his years as the co-owner of a medical practice, he sued more than 700 patients for outstanding bills, leading to some 81 arrests of patients who missed scheduled court dates.
Marshall has protested the reports, telling CNN this week that he “would want no one to ever go to jail because of anything they owe me. There were people being bussed from other cities to us knowing I would take care of them for free”.
Hamilton, meanwhile, has been portrayed in a series of Two Faced, Too Extreme For Kansas attack adverts as having harboured a child predator in one of the church summer camps in the 1990s, inviting the perpetrator back even after he had been arrested. Hamilton, speaking hoarsely in a brief television interview on Monday, allowed that “mistakes were made” at the time but says that the adverts are an “incorrect description of what happened and, in the end, I helped get this man prosecuted”.
“We did what we could and got someone put in jail: Roger Marshall protected the Epstein files from being released.”
Both incidents will feature when the candidates meet for their concluding televised debate on Wednesday night. By then, Donald Trump won’t be in Kansas any more. But as he signed off with his familiar ‘make America great again’ refrain and YMCA shimmy, the president looked happy that all was good in Wichita.
“Well, I mean going to a Trump rally is kind of like going to the freak show at the carnival,” said Bill Graves, the former Republican governor.
“What’s he going to say? What’s he going to do? It’s always very entertaining but whether or not it translates into increased voting on behalf of Roger Marshall is, in my opinion, yet to be seen and hard to believe. This is just another indication of, I think, Trump’s infatuation with his own self. Loving to get in front of audiences. They are obviously the Maga crowd that is going to adore him.”
Graves has endorsed Adam Hamilton to become Kansas’s next senator.

title: Bilí na beatha
description: Tá tábhacht na gcrann aitheanta sa mhiotaseolaíocht agus san eolaíocht araon
content:
Fadó, fadó nuair a bhí na déithe ar dhroim na ndomhan agus na fathaigh ag fánaíocht inár measc, bhí crann mór fuinseoige ina sheasamh i lár na cruinne. Mochta, maorga, maisiúil. Bhí a chuid fréamhacha neadaithe go domhain i réimse na marbh agus na mistéire agus a chuid craobhacha ar leathadh ó cheann ceann na spéartha. Is faoi scáth na ngéag neartmhar sin a bhí na naoi ndomhan i ndáil le chéile go daingean dlúth.
Le hais ceann de na fréamhacha fada, bhí tobar draíochta, áit a múnlaíodh bandéithe rúndiamhra cinniúint agus dán an duine dhaonna. Gach lá chuireadh siad uisce ón tobar naofa ar an chrann mhór lena bheathú agus lena chothú ar mhaithe le gach neach beo agus marbh.
I measc an duilliúir ag barr an chrainn, bhíodh iolar mór ina shuí go socair. Ag an bhun ar fad bhíodh nathair chreimneach ag cnaí na rútaí lá agus oíche. Sa lár bhí an t-iolra gasta, a ritheadh eatarthu le teachtaireachtaí, tásca agus tuairiscí.
Is ar an ollchrann fuinseoige chéanna a chroch an Mórathair é féin agus é ag lorg eagna na rúnscríbhinní agus fios gach feasa.
Ansin, ar deireadh thiar thall agus i ndiaidh an iomláin, nuair a tháinig an tOllscrios agus a chreathnaigh na flaithis agus a maraíodh idir dhaoine agus déithe, baineadh croitheadh as an bhile amhra fosta, ó bhun go barr agus ó bharr go bun arís.
Ach tháinig sé slán. Agus nuair a ghlan an doineann agus a shuaimhnigh an saol, is ó fhoscadh na fuinseoige a cothaíodh an bheatha athuair.
Sin agaibh é - a bheag nó a mhór agus cnapán fial flaithiúil de shaoirse an ealaíontóra caite isteach lena chois - scéal Yggdrasil, an bile beatha, an tamhan torthúil, an crann cosmach i miotaseolaíocht leathan na Lochlannach.
Ollchrann fuinseoige atá ann de réir an seanscéalta, craobh thaca na ndomhan atá suite i gcroílár na cruinne agus a chaomhnaíonn agus a cheanglaíonn gach uile ní.
Cá bhfios nach ann dó i ndáiríre agus i gcónaí - is iomaí rud iontach a bhfuil muid dall air anseo ar Domhan - ach fiú mar mhóitíf agus meafar béaloidis is léir an tábhacht a bhaineann leis an chrann seo i lár baill agus báire.
Is olc an dóigh a bhfuil muidne, daoine, ag caitheamh lenár gcairde na crainn ar an iomlán, áfach.
Ní hamháin gurb é a choinníonn na domhain uile, agus gach neach a chónaíonn orthu, ag imeacht agus ag gluaiseacht, is díol spéise é fosta gur ón chrann chumhachtach seo a thosaíonn an saol arís tar éis na tubaiste marfaí, Ragnarök, a bhuail an ollchruinne agus a réab gach cearn dá raibh ann.
Ní heol dúinn go díreach cé acu a bhí nó nach raibh crann diaga den chineál chéanna againne i gcosmeolaíocht na nGael tráth, ach is cinnte go bhfuil tagairtí go leor sna téacsanna meánaoiseacha do na bilí, na crainn naofa, a bhí ina seasamh fadó agus a raibh meas an phobail mhóir orthu i gcóngar is i gcéin.
Go deimhin, de réir dán amháin de chuid an Dinnseanchais, ba chrainn fuinseoige iad trí cinn de na bilí ba thábhachtaí in Éirinn, an crann téagartha in Uisneach, ceartlár na tíre, ina measc.
Cosúlacht shuimiúil é sin le Yggdrasil na Lochlannach ó thuaidh.
Má bhí áit lárnach ag crainn i meon agus i miotaseolaíocht ár sinsear, tá siad chomh riachtanach ríthábhachtach céanna inniu, cé nach mbeadh a fhios sin agat i gcónaí ó bhéasa agus iompar an chine dhaonna.
Tá ról an-lárnach go deo ag na crainn i gcothú na beatha ar an phláinéad seo. Rialaíonn siad an aeráid agus aimsir, cosnaíonn siad an chré, cuireann siad gnáthóga ar fáil ina maireann speicis gan áireamh agus, ar ndóigh, tugann siad bia blasta dúinne agus d’ainmhithe eile.
An tuiscint sin a taispeánadh ar dtús i mbéaloideas na laethanta atá thart, tá sí dearbhaithe agus deimhnithe ag eolaíocht an lae inniu.
Is olc an dóigh a bhfuil muidne, daoine, ag caitheamh lenár gcairde na crainn ar an iomlán, áfach.
Tá an dífhoraoisiú faoi lán seoil i gcónaí - go háirithe sna Trópaicí, áit a bhfuil cuid de na coillte is críonna agus na crainn is cruthaithí dá bhfuil beo - agus is bocht an dreach lom atá ar sciar nach beag dár dtírín féin.
Tá an ráta dífhoraoisithe domhanda ag titim bliain i ndiaidh bliana - laghdaigh sé 36% ó 2024 go 2025 - agus tá tionscnaimh athphlandaithe ar bun sna ceithre hairde le fada.
Sa Phacastáin amháin athneartaíodh 350,000 heicteár d’fhoraoisí agus de thailte díghrádaithe nuair a cuireadh thart ar bhilliún crann sa tír idir 2014 agus 2017. Tá a mhacasamhail ag tarlú ar fud an domhain in áiteanna eile chomh maith.
Ní hionann seanchrann agus crann óg ar ndóigh, go háirithe ó thaobh an tionchair ar an éiceachóras iomlán de, ach is gá tosnú in áit éigin.
Inniu féin, an 20 Deireadh Fómhair, tá Den Stromů á cheiliúradh sa tSeicia: Lá na gCrann a atosaíodh in 2000 agus atá ag dul go láidir ó shin. Tá breis agus trian den tír clúdaithe le coillte cheana féin ach spreagtar daoine le crainn a chur agus a chaomhnú i gcónaí, agus béim ar leith acu anois ar éagsúlacht a gcuid foraoisí agus ar speicis a sheasfaidh an t-athrú aeráide.
Is i mí Márta a bheidh Seachtain na gCrann againn féin in Éirinn ach ní gá fanacht go dtí sin le dul i mbun aicsin. Tá an séasúr plandála ag teannadh linn mar sin, agus na duilleoga ag titim thart orainn, is féidir linn crainn úra a chur sa talamh - sa chathair nó faoin tuath - agus ár gcuid a dhéanamh chun cur le ciorcal na beatha agus le sláinte an phláinéid.
Seans gur bile mór na nglúnta atá le teacht a bheidh sa chrann bheag a chuirfidh tú féin inniu.

title: Oil wavers near five-month high as traders weigh risk of Iran threats
description: Crude flows from the Persian Gulf remain robust
content:
Brent oil fluctuated near a five-month high as traders weighed the risk of further Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz against robust crude flows from the Persian Gulf.
The global benchmark was just below $110 a barrel, near the highest since May, while the most-active West Texas Intermediate contract was close to $99. Iran has “no choice” but to assert control over Hormuz to safeguard the country’s security, first vice president Mohammad Reza Aref said Monday, according to a report from state-run news agency IRNA.
Despite a recent flare-up in hostilities around the waterway, crude exports from the Gulf have continued at an accelerated pace. US energy secretary Chris Wright told Fox News that flows had recovered to about 80 per cent of their prewar level, although refined-product shipments remained constrained.
Brent has surged about 80 per cent this year as widening conflicts in the Middle East and between Russia and Ukraine disrupt energy supplies. Refined products have rallied even harder, with European diesel futures surging. Renewed attacks on tankers and energy infrastructure are keeping geopolitical risk elevated even as Persian Gulf crude flows recover.
“The risks to oil prices clearly lie to the upside,” said Hamad Hussain, a commodities economist at Capital Economics. The escalation in attacks on ships raises the possibility of a “renewed fall in oil supply and a continued rise in prices”, he added.
Iran’s Aref said the Islamic Republic could ensure safe passage through Hormuz for friendly nations, but warned that “the US is now the cause of the current situation and must pay the price.” He made the comments during a meeting in Tajikistan with Russian prime minister Mikhail Mishustin.
Iraq is among Persian Gulf producers that have ramped up crude flows, with the country’s oil minister saying exports have exceeded 3.4 million barrels a day so far this month. Shipments are now close to prewar levels after the Opec member offered deep discounts to regional benchmarks.
Meanwhile, the Trump administration is authorising the sale of sanctioned oil tankers so they can legitimately ship crude, according to Wright. The move is aimed at expanding capacity as the US-Iran war strains supply and drives up freight costs. He estimated there are about 1,600 vessels in the global “dark fleet”. - Bloomberg

title: Saibhreas scéalaíochta Rann na Feirste
description: Is iomaí duine a d’fhoghlaim ó sheanchaithe an cheantair agus iad i mbun scéalaíochta i gColáiste Bhríde
content:
Rinne Coláiste Bhríde, an coláiste samhraidh Gaeltachta i Rann na Feirste, comóradh 100 Bliain bhunú an Choláiste a cheiliúradh ag réimse leathan imeachtaí an mhí seo sa tsráidbhaile bheag bhídeach i gcroílár Ghaeltacht Thír Chonaill.
Bhí an gnás ann ó thoisigh Coláiste Bhríde seanchaithe an bhaile a thabhairt isteach agus thug seo deis daofa lucht éisteachta eile a aimsiú, bíodh is nárbh ionann sin agus an lucht éisteachta traidisiúnta a raibh dúil acu sna seanscéalta seo ariamh anall. Bhí laethanta órga na scéalaíochta in Éirinn thart agus pobal traidisiúnta na Gaeltachta ag athrú le linn do na seanchaithe a bheith fán Choláiste. Bhí seanchaithe sa Choláiste go dtí cúig bliain is fiche ó shin ach faraoir níl anois.
Chuidigh an meas a bhí ag an Ath. Lorcán Ó Muireadhaigh, bunaitheoir an Choláiste, agus ag a lucht leanúna ar an Ghaeilge agus ar an bhéaloideas leo siúd i Rann na Feirste a raibh a gcroí istigh sa tsaol thraidisiúnta chéanna.
Thug an Choláiste pá do na scéalaithe, rud a chuirfeadh le luach an traidisiúin. Anuas air sin, ba léiriú ar an mheas a bhí ar a dteanga, a gcomhrá agus a n-ealaín bhéil, an oiread daoine a bheith ag tarraingt ar an cheantar, rud a chuirfeadh le stádas sóisialta agus caipiteal cultúrtha na scéalaithe.
Ar dtús bhí Johnny Shéimisín ann, fear a thoisigh a scéalaíocht sa Choláiste in 1926. Bhí teach Johnny aitheanta mar theach airneáil agus thug neart daoine mór le rá cuairt air. Chuidigh Johnny leis an Oirmhinneach Cosslett Ó Cuinn, ministir Protastúnach, cuid den Bhíobla, go háirid na sailm, a aistriú go Gaeilge. Ba é Johnny a thug suíomh saor in aisce do lucht na Coláiste don chéad fhoirgneamh a thógáil thiar in 1926.
Bhí aithne mhaith ag Annie Bhán Fheilimí Nic Grianna ar lucht Choláiste Bhríde agus ba ghnách le grúpaí scoláirí a bheith cruinnithe thart uirthi agus ag cuartaíocht aici agus ag cur isteach uirthi lá agus oíche ag tabhairt uirthi scéal a inse. Leoga bhí a sáith aice leis na scoláirí in amantaí agus nádúrtha go leor chaillfeadh sí foighid leo corruair agus iad sa chasán aici agus ag cur barraíocht ceisteanna uirthi fá ghnóthaí Gaeilge.
Ba iad Micí Sheáin, Neidí Frainc Mac Grianna agus Seán Bán Mac Grianna an triúr seanchaithe aitheanta a chaith na bliantaí ag dul isteach ag na ranganna i gColáiste Bhríde ag scéalaíocht do na scoláirí. Chuir na mílte duine a d’fhreastail ar Choláiste Bhríde aithne ar na seanchaithe seo thar na bliantaí agus chuir cuid acu aithne ar Mhicí agus ar Neidí mar fhir tí cionn is go raibh lóistéirí ag stopadh acu.
Go luath ina shaol chuaigh Seán Bán Mac Grianna a theagasc i gColáiste Bhríde agus is ansin a bhí sé go deireadh a lae – caoga bliain níos moille. Chuir sé aithne ansin ar dhaoine as achan chearn den tír agus bhí mórán cairde aige. Bhí ardmheas aige ar an Ath. Lorcán Ó Muireadhaigh. Bhíodh John Ghráinne Ó Duibheannaigh, a dheartháir agus Aodh Ó Duibheannaigh sa Choláiste ag scéalaíocht fosta.
Chaith Neidi Frainc Mac Grianna go leor ama i gColáiste Bhríde ag teagasc agus ag roinnt a chuid seanchais leis na scoláirí. Bhí dúil bhocht aige goil suas ‘na Coláiste agus a bheith ag scéalaíocht. “Mura n-instear na scéalta, gheobhaidh siad bás,” a deireadh sé leis a iníon, Geraldine.
Bhí sé de bhua ag Neidí Frainc go raibh sé ábalta scéal a ghiorrú d’fhoghlaimeoirí i gColáiste Bhríde agus nach mbeadh a fhios agat gur fhág sé focal amach mar bhí cnámha an scéil ann agus shíl tú go raibh an t-iomlán ann. Ach dá gcluinfeá é ag inse an scéil chéanna do dhaoine a raibh scoth na Gaeilge acu agus tuigbheáil acu ar an teanga, b’fhéidir go mbeadh an scéal ceathrú uair an chloig níos faide. Agus é ag scéalaíocht i gColáiste Bhríde, thuig sé go raibh sé ag caint le foghlaimeoirí agus mhoilligh sé anuas rud beag.
I dtigh Sheáin Néill a chuir an tOllamh Jim McCluskey aithne ar an chéad mhórealaíontóir a casadh ariamh air. Ba é fear an tí, Micí Sheáin, an t-ealaíontóir sin agus ba í ealaín na haithrise agus an tseanchais a chleacht sé. Corroíche, nuair a bhuaileadh an tallann é i ndiaidh am dinnéara agus i ndiaidh dó féin agus John lá crua oibre a chur isteach sna cuibhrinn, d’fhiafraíodh sé díofa: “Anois, a ghasúraí, ar mhaith libh scéal a chluinstin?” D’fhanadh McCluskey agus cuid eile acu sa chistineach a dh’éisteacht leis agus chuirtí tús leis an scéal.
Bhí ról ag Coláiste Bhríde ag tarraingt clú agus ag tuilleadh measa ar na seanchaithe cionn is go raibh áit ann a raibh siad ábalta dul isteach ann ag scéalaíocht ag daoine eile. Bhí cúpla punta le gnóthú acu air agus ar an ábhar sin rinne siad cinnte go raibh scéalta acu. Thug an Choláiste ardán nó deis cineál oifigiúil daofa a gcuid scéalta a insint.
Phronn fostú na Coláiste stádas ar leith ar na scéalaithe seo mar dhaoine a raibh saineolas dúchasach acu agus arbh fhiú éisteacht leo. B’ionann lucht na Coláiste agus lucht éisteachta ag na scéalaithe in am a raibh an scéalaíocht ag gabháil i léig. Chinnteodh an lucht éisteachta seo go raibh faill ag na scéalaithe a n-ealaín a chleachtadh nuair nach raibh an t-airneál ná na seanscéalta fada sa chomhthéacs thraidisiúnta ag gabháil chomh láidir céanna a thuilleadh.
Tá Brendan Ó Dufaigh ina bhall de Choiste na Coláiste le 15 bliana.

title: ‘Gaeilge gan Stad’ le Gaeilge24
description: Na Ceithre hAirde: Gaeilge24; albam nua ag Doireann Ní Ghlacáin; clár GAIRM agus Gaillimh le Gaeilge
content:
Trí chéad scoil, tríocha míle dalta, lá mór amháin. Sin é mana Gaeilge24, imeacht mór de chuid Chonradh na Gaeilge a spreagann daltaí fud fad na tíre Gaeilge amháin a labhairt ar feadh 24 uair an chloig: sa bhaile, ar scoil, sa siopa, sa chlub spóirt agus le cairde.
Tá Gaeilge24 ar cheann de na príomhimeachtaí a eagraíonn Conradh na Gaeilge do dhaltaí scoile gach bliain agus táthar ag súil go mbeidh na mílte páirteach ann arís i mbliana.
Nuair a chláraíonn rang nó scoil le haghaidh Gaeilge24, faigheann siad pacáiste do gach dalta ina bhfuil t-léine, banda láimhe, teastas, leabhrán beag le frásaí úsáideacha agus cárta urraíochta. Iarrtar ar na daltaí iad féin airgead a bhailiú don charthanas, a rachaidh i dtreo mhórfheachtais an Chonartha cosúil le CEARTA agus Athghaelú, imeachtaí náisiúnta cosúil le hArd-Fheis na nÓg agus eagraíochtaí ar nós Raidió Rí-Rá.
An aidhm atá le Gaeilge24 ná cuidiú le daltaí cur lena stór focal agus taithí a thabhairt do na daltaí sin atá ag ullmhú don scrúdú béil ach go háirithe. Is fiú 40% de mhóriomlán na marcanna san Ardteist anois é agus mar sin cuideoidh Gaeilge24 go mór le daltaí agus le múinteoirí comhrá nádúrtha a spreagadh sa seomra ranga.
An bhfuil suim ag do rang féin a bheith páirteach? Is é amárach, 21 Deireadh Fómhair 2026, an dáta deireanach le haghaidh réamhchláraithe. Téigh chuig cnag.ie le clárú nó le tuilleadh eolais a fháil.
Albam úrnua fógartha ag Doireann Ní Ghlacáin
Níl stop ar bith le Doireann Ní Ghlacáin na laethanta seo agus í ag podchraoltóireacht léi agus ag scaipeadh na Gaeilge thar lear. Ar ndóigh, nuair nach mbíonn Doireann le feiceáil ar an scáileán, bíonn sí ag seinm na fidle, ag ceol agus ag portaireacht fud fad na tíre. D’fhógair Doireann ar na mallaibh go mbeidh a céad albam aonair, An Tairseach, ag teacht amach i mí Eanáir 2027.
Tá an ceol fite fuaite i dteaghlach Uí Ghlacáin. D’fhoghlaim Doireann an fhidil óna hathair, a d’fhoghlaim an fhidil óna athair féin, agus d’fhoghlaim sí traidisiún an tsean-nóis ó theaghlach a máthar, Clann Uí Riada i nGaeltacht Chúil Aodha in Iarthar Chorcaí. Albam lán le ceol traidisiúnta agus portaireacht cheolmhar bhinn a bheidh in An Tairseach ina bpléifear cumhacht an cheoil, mórtas áite, béaloideas agus an Tairseach í féin – an spás idir an saol seo agus an saol eile.
Beidh Doireann ag dul ar camchuairt leis an albam seo a chur chun cinn i nGaillimh, i gCorcaigh, i Luimneach, i mBéal Feirste agus i mBaile Átha Cliath i mí Feabhra agus Márta na bliana seo chugainn. Tá tuilleadh eolais faoin chamchuairt agus faoi na ticéid ar fáil ar Instagram @doireannnighlacain . Chomh maith leis sin, tá An Tairseach ar fáil le réamhordú ar Bandcamp anois. Seolfar an t-albam an 15 Eanáir 2027.
Céimithe Nua Tosaithe ar Chlár Ceannródaíoch GAIRM
Chuir Údarás na Gaeltachta agus Ollscoil Teicneolaíochta an Atlantaigh (OTA) fáilte roimh chohórt nua ar an scéim GAIRM an mhí seo. Mar chuid den scéim seo, tosaíonn céimithe ar chonradh fostaíochta dhá bhliain le hÚdarás na Gaeltachta agus baineann siad Dioplóma Iarchéime leibhéal 9 amach i gcomhar le OTA. Chomh maith leis sin, faigheann siad taithí ghairmiúil thar a bheith luachmhar mar oifigigh feidhmiúcháin i rannóga éagsúla an Údaráis ar fud na Gaeltachta, sna hoifigí réigiúnacha de chuid an Údaráis sna Forbacha, i nGaoth Dobhair, i mBéal an Mhuirthead, i nDaingean Uí Chúis nó i mBaile Mhic Íre.
Dúirt Tomás Ó Síocháin, Príomhfheidhmeannach Údarás na Gaeltachta, gurb í “an fhís atá againn don scéim seo ná go bhfuilimid ag cothú an chéad ghlúin eile de cheannairí agus bainisteoirí, bíodh sé san Údarás nó sa státseirbhís, áit a bhfuil éileamh ollmhór ar dhaoine le Gaeilge, éileamh a bheidh ag fás. Tá an-rath feicthe againn leis an gcéad ghrúpa rannpháirtithe agus táimid muiníneach go mbeidh an cohórt nua chomh díograiseach céanna.”
Dearadh an cúrsa go hiomlán as an nua in 2024 chun scileanna bainistíochta na rannpháirtithe a fhorbairt agus iad ag tabhairt faoi cheithre mhódúil déag thar thréimhse dhá bhliain. Chríochnaigh naonúr an scéim i mbliana agus tá thart ar 80% acu fostaithe ó chríochnaigh siad an clár i réimse leathan eagraíochtaí san earnáil phoiblí agus san earnáil phríobháideach.
Gaillimh le Gaeilge ag earcú Oifigeach Pleanála Teanga
Tá duine ‘fuinniúil, díograiseach agus dearfach’ á lorg ag Gaillimh le Gaeilge chun tacú le comhordú agus le cur i bhfeidhm Phlean Teanga Chathair na Gaillimhe. Is post lánaimseartha ar théarma seasta trí bliana é seo a bheidh lonnaithe in Oifig Ghaillimh le Gaeilge i gcroílár Chathair na Gaillimhe, agus beidh gá le solúbthacht maidir le freastal ar chruinnithe, imeachtaí agus gníomhaíochtaí taobh amuigh de ghnáthuaireanta oifige ó am go ham.
Beidh gá le Gaeilge líofa, idir labhartha agus scríofa, don phost seo chomh maith le taithí chruthaithe ar thionscadail a phleanáil, a chomhordú agus a chur i bhfeidhm ó thús deireadh agus cur amach den scoth ar theicneolaíocht dhigiteach agus na meáin shóisialta.
Más duine thú atá go maith ag obair le daoine eile, atá in ann smaointe nua a fhorbairt, agus atá ag iarraidh deiseanna nua a chruthú don Ghaeilge sa chathair, is féidir cur isteach ar an phost seo ag gleg.ie . Is é an 9 Samhain an dáta deiridh le haghaidh iarratas. Má tá ceist ar bith agat faoin phost, is féidir teagmháil a dhéanamh le Bríd ag brid@gleg.ie nó ag 0872863075.

title: Gardaí issue renewed appeal for information about murder of Paul Quinn
description: Family of 21-year-old victim believe members of  IRA carried out fatal attack in Co Monaghan in 2007
content:
A renewed appeal for information has been issued by gardaí investigating the murder of a 21-year-old man in Co Monaghan.
Paul Quinn was beaten to death 19 years ago on Tuesday.
His family, who have maintained a campaign for justice, believe members of the IRA were responsible, but Sinn Féin has long denied there was republican involvement in the killing.
To date, 23 people have been arrested in connection with the murder. Nobody has ever been charged.
Gardaí have urged anyone with information to help them bring his killers to justice to come forward.
In a statement, the Garda said Quinn and a friend were attacked by a gang of between eight to 10 masked men.
They are believed, at about 6pm on October 20th, 2007, to have travelled in a car to outbuildings and sheds at Tullyvanus, Castleblayney, Co Monaghan.
On arrival, they were attacked by a gang of masked men, some of whom were armed with weapons.
Gardaí have said Quinn and his friend were tied up by the gang and Quinn was then subjected to a violent and sustained attack.
They said the attackers are believed to have fled the scene in a white coloured van which has never been recovered.
“Gardaí continue to seek any information which may assist in identifying and locating it,” they said.
Of the 23 arrested, 14 were arrested in the Republic of Ireland and nine in Northern Ireland in an investigation which continues to see An Garda Síochána and the Police Service of Northern Ireland work closely.
Det Supt Ronan Carey issued an appeal to the people of the Cullyhanna area of south Armagh to come forward if they have any information.
“Today I am again renewing my appeal to you, the local community, because you have the information we need to progress this investigation. I am particularly appealing to the people in the Cullyhanna area of South Armagh,” he said.
“I am appealing to those men who were in the shed and also to friends or family members of these men who know what happened on the 20th of October 2007 and who, since that time, continue to carry the burden of knowing what happened to Paul on their conscience.
“Time has now passed and the nature of relationships may have changed. I appeal to anyone who was afraid to talk to us over the last 19 years to now come forward. Maybe there was a reason you were afraid, but now is the time to come forward and tell us what you know in confidence.
“I appeal to you to contact gardaí or the PSNI through any of the following phone numbers or the confidential telephone lines anonymously and help us to bring closure to Paul’s parents Breege and Stephen Quinn who continue to suffer the terrible loss of their son Paul.”
Anyone with information can contact Castleblayney Garda station on 042 974 7900, the Garda Confidential Telephone line on 1800 666 111 or Crimestoppers (Northern Ireland) on 0800 555 111. – PA

title: Trump wants to talk nuclear disarmament with China and Russia. Beijing does not
description: China has long argued its nuclear arsenal is so far behind those of Russia and the US that it should not be included in arms talks
content:
Donald Trump might have a trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin when they are all in the Chinese city of Shenzhen next month. But it’s unlikely to amount to much.
Trump confirmed on Monday that he was open to a meeting with Xi and Putin on the margins of next month’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China . But despite reports that the Russian leader wanted the meeting to talk about Ukraine , the American president said he would prefer to discuss nuclear weapons.
“I would do it, not so much for Ukraine,” he said.
“Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine. They have not been doing much. And the same thing with China. We would have it to talk about nuclear weapons, denuclearisation.”
Trump and Putin spoke on the phone on October 9th and Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Monday that since the three leaders may attend next month’s summit, the topic of what he called a hypothetical meeting had been discussed.
“No specific proposals or agreements have been discussed or voiced by anyone, neither on the meeting itself, nor on a potential agenda or the content of this meeting,” he said.
Beijing, which seldom confirms arrangements for such high-level encounters until the last minute, had nothing to say about any trilateral meeting yesterday. But China has long ruled out taking part in nuclear disarmament talks with the United States and Russia, a position it reaffirmed last Friday.
“Sitting on an enormous nuclear arsenal, the US should fulfil its special and primary responsibility for nuclear disarmament. This is the international consensus,” foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning said.
“China’s nuclear strength is by no means at the same level with that of the US and Russia. It is neither fair, reasonable nor realistic to ask China to join the so-called trilateral nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage.”
Moscow has the world’s biggest nuclear arsenal with 4,400 warheads (not including those that have been retired) while Washington has 3,700, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. China has 620 nuclear warheads, of which just 34 are deployed and ready to launch at short notice, compared to Russia’s 1,796 and the US’s 1,770.
Beijing has long argued that it is so far behind Russia and the US that it should not be included in nuclear arms talks, despite Washington’s claims that the size of China’s arsenal is catching up fast. And China asserts that as the only power to have ruled out the first use of nuclear weapons, its capability is purely defensive unlike those of Russia and the US.
For Xi to agree to taking part in trilateral denuclearisation talks in Shenzhen next month would be a policy reversal so dramatic as to be almost unthinkable. And the Chinese leader also has little incentive to take a prominent role in efforts to end the Ukraine war at a time when the negotiations are still under the stewardship of Trump’s envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner.
The European powers, led by Germany, France and Britain, have been dipping a bashful toe into the waters of talks with Russia and they will have to take a more decisive plunge soon if they want a say in shaping the peace. But as even the Kremlin’s Peskov acknowledged on Monday, there must be one more essential actor for any negotiation to succeed.
“Of course, without a doubt, a final settlement is impossible without the participation of someone from Kyiv who is willing to take responsibility,” he said.

title: Motor insurance costs, and the World Cup on Netflix
description: Business Today: The best news, analysis and comment from The Irish Times business desk
content:
New figures from the Central Bank of Ireland reveal that Irish motor insurers estimate the average claims cost per policy rose 10 per cent to €424 last year, driven by an increase in both vehicle damage and personal injury claims costs. On the upside, Joe Brennan reports that the bank noted “encouraging signs” as premiums started to fall in the second half of last year.
Sticking with insurance, Conor Pope writes that motorists who agree to allow their driving to be monitored through a device or an app installed in their vehicle – can save thousands of euro a year on the cost of cover. That’s according to new research from Bonkers.ie, which found that a 20-year-old driver with a full licence was quoted just €570 for a comprehensive so-called telematics policy.
Netflix’s acquisition of the rights to all 104 matches of the 2030 World Cup in Spain is evidence that the big streaming platforms are getting serious about disrupting the live sports market. Previously, they had contented themselves with one-off marquee events. Hugh Linehan looks at the reasons for the change of heart and what it might mean for fans.
Joe Brennan looks at the Finance Bill, published on Monday, for more details about Minister for Finance Simon Harris’s much-discussed personal investment accounts scheme . He reports that firms, banks and insurers planning to offer the accounts will have to register with the Revenue Commissioners and provide investors with annual statements of tax deducted and paid on their behalf.
Joe also has the latest from Bawag on its pending acquisition of PTSB. On a call with analysts yesterday after the Austrian bank reported its third quarter results, chief executive Anas Abuzaakouk said his group is “rising above the noise” as it awaits High Court approval of the deal.
Ciara O’Brien reports that business information company Bloomberg is expanding its Irish office, planning to double its staff to almost 400 through investment in engineering, technology, product development and data capabilities.
A new pilot scheme, aimed at boosting the supply of social housing by offering a “secure, low-risk letting option” for landlords, has been launched by the Department of Housing, writes Fiona Reddan . It’s not the first scheme of its kind. So what’s different about it, and can it increase the number of properties available to social housing tenants?
Meanwhile, new figures from EirGrid reveal that Ireland is reliant on British imports for about one sixth of its electricity. Barry O’Halloran casts an eye over the national grid operator’s Winter Outlook report, which assesses whether the Republic will have enough electricity to meet its likely needs from November 2nd to April 4th.
Barry also has the story that State airport operator DAA’s international business has won a contract to run a VIP passenger terminal at Washington Dulles International, the main gateway to the US capital.
In Your Money, Dominic Coyle answers a question from a widowed reader who wonders whether Budget 2027 provides any sort of boost for solo parent families .
Finally, Cantillon looks at the recent turmoil in bond markets and how it might be affecting the European Central Bank’s interest rate calculus and, separately, the Chinese economy’s unexpectedly strong third quarter , which was still historically low by Chinese standards and reflects an increasingly unbalanced, two-speed economy.

title: What’s the best EV for low mileage?
description: Practical advice on your motoring queries, from buying, selling or issues you have with your current car
content:
My wife drives an 2018 Hyundai Kona: 80 per cent of her driving is city based. She only does 3,000km to 4,000km per year. What electric or hybrid car do you recommend for her? We have solar panels since February this year. – Seamus T, Co Limerick
Thanks for getting in touch. I think there’s one simple answer here, a few other suggestions which might be worth looking at, and then a slight curveball.
The most obvious car to choose is the Hyundai Inster . Assuming you’re happy with the Kona, then it makes sense to stay within the Hyundai family, as the Inster is one of the best electric cars around. Not just one of the best small electric cars, but one of the best – full stop.
However, even given your low mileage requirements, I’m not going to suggest that you get the cheapest Inster, with the smallest battery.
Go for the Inster Elegance with the 49kWh battery, because not only does that give you considerably more usable range (370km officially, and well able to cope with the odd long motorway journey should you need to), but it also gets the adjustable rear seats, which slide back and forth and which allow you to unlock the Inster’s hugely useful interior.
Then again, there is a €4,500 price gap between the cheapest Inster and the Elegance, and maybe you don’t need adjustable rear seats, so you can take my advice as it best suits you in this regard. Either way, you’re getting a cracking small car that looks great, is good to drive and is exceptionally efficient.
With your solar panels, you should be getting all of your motoring charging needs from the sun. The most common 4kWp set-up can produce as much as 4,000kWh of energy over the course of a year, enough to charge the little Inster up nearly 82 times even if you did go for the big-battery 49kWh version. That would be enough to drive it for more than 30,000km, assuming you got the full 370km out of each charge. Clearly, you don’t need that.
Does that mean free electric motoring? It could do, depending on how and when you charge the car up. The rest you can sell back to the grid ...
There are some other good options for you when it comes to cars. The little Leapmotor T03 is a decent small electric car, and with a price tag of €18,950 it’s certainly affordable, although its maximum 250km range will be a bit on the short side on those occasions when you might want to undertake a longer journey.
[ Leapmotor T03 review: New city car delivers on function, but is it fun? Opens in new window ]
Renault ’s adorable 5 E-Tech is a good choice – gorgeous to look at and fun to drive – but it’s pricier than the Leapmotor and the Hyundai, and we have heard of some charging reliability issues, so tread somewhat carefully. Perhaps it would be better to wait until the new year when the smaller, more affordable, even more adorable Renault Twingo arrives on sale. That one will have a price tag below €20,000.
The Fiat Grande Panda Electric is also a solid choice and really quite gorgeous (although it helps if you go for the pricier ‘La Prima’ model). A range of 320km seems like it should be enough.
[ Fiat rediscovers its soul with the Grande Panda Opens in new window ]
The incoming trio of VW Group products – ID. Polo , Cupra Raval , or Skoda Epiq – all make for great choices too, and your driving needs would be perfectly well served by the more affordable small-battery versions of each one, with their circa-310km ranges. The ID.Polo is the star here, but in many ways all these might be slightly too much car for what you need.
I feel like the Inster is still the best idea of the lot – it’s a minimalist car, in the sense that it gives you exactly what you need (plus one or two additional niceties) for not too much money.
However, the money thing does raise its head here, and remember I mentioned a curveball? You need to ask yourself why you’re doing this. Are you determined to switch to electric power? In which case, fine – go ahead and grab the Inster. Or, are you looking to do this to save money at a time of rising fuel prices?
If that’s the case, then changing your car might be more expensive than just hanging on to what you have. It’s for this reason that I’ve not recommended any hybrid cars, as the ‘free’ electricity you’ll get from your solar panels is the only way that this process starts to make sense, from a money-saving point of view.
[ Citroën’s relaunch of a classic could be just what the electric car market needs Opens in new window ]
You see, even the cheapest car I’ve recommended here – the €18,985 Leapmotor – will still be an expensive thing to buy. If your existing Kona is three to four years old then you might only get €10,000-12,000 as a trade-in, which means you’ll have to finance another €6,000-€8,000 for the Leapmotor or the basic Inster, or find more again for one of the other cars mentioned.
At which point you’re into repayments of either a hire purchase plan, a PCP, or a personal loan of some sort. While fuel prices are certainly much higher right now, at your average mileage you’ll still be a long time repaying yourself in fuel bill savings. Make sure you sit down and do your sums thoroughly before deciding.
