title: Two men (20s) arrested by gardaí investigating drug-related intimidation
description: Search operations were carried out in Meath and Dublin on Monday morning
content:
Two men in their 20s have been arrested by gardaí investigating drug-related intimidation.
Gardaí from Dublin ’s North Fógra Investigation Unit carried out search operations in Meath and Dublin on Monday morning.
The arrests form part of an ongoing investigation into drug-related intimidation, gardaí said.
Both men are being questioned at Garda stations in Dublin under Section 50 of the Criminal Justice Act, 2007.
Since it was set up in 2023, the unit has arrested and charged 45 people with more than 120 offences in relation to drug-related intimidation.
The Garda said the unit is currently engaged in 15 active investigations. – PA

title: Rapist Simon McGinley jailed for repeatedly breaching release conditions
description: McGinley was sentenced to 21 years in prison in 2009 for rape of elderly woman, having been previously jailed for ‘C Case’ rape
content:
The rapist at the centre of the 1990s “C Case” has repeatedly breached the conditions of his release from a 21-year sentence imposed in 2009 for the rape of an elderly woman, a court has heard.
Simon McGinley (52) appeared before the Central Criminal Court on Monday, when Judge Tony Hunt was informed he received a 2½-year jail term in Dundalk Circuit Criminal Court last week.
McGinley was jailed for repeatedly breaching the notification requirements of his release from jail in 2021 under the Sex Offenders Act, Fiona McGowan, prosecuting, told the court. These conditions include notifying the gardaí about a change of address.
McGinley, formerly of Latlorcan Court, Co Monaghan, and originally from Dundalk, was jailed for 21 years in 2009 for the rape of an 86-year-old woman in her own home.
He was previously jailed for eight years in 1998 for raping the then 13-year-old girl at the centre of the “C Case” in August 1997.
This girl became pregnant as a result of the rape and had to apply to the courts to access an abortion in the UK, which her parents resisted. She was granted permission to travel in December 1997.
The court heard McGinley previously appeared before the Central Criminal Court in 2023 in relation to breaching the conditions of his release. On that occasion, two years from his 2009 sentence were reactivated with six months suspended.
Having offended again since then, he was before the Central Criminal Court on Monday in relation to that six-month suspension.
McGinley had no solicitor present due to the withdrawal of services, but he told Hunt he was happy for the hearing to proceed.
The judge said he would reactivate three months of the six-month suspension, which he noted would run consecutive to the 2½-year sentence imposed in the Circuit Court last week.
“I want to bring finality to this matter,” the judge said. He told McGinley he needed to start complying with the requirements.
“All you have to do is give an address,” the judge told him. “I’m not going through this rigmarole. If you don’t start complying, you will be sentenced over and over again in the circuit court.”
McGinley agreed and thanked the judge before returning to custody.

title: Limerick teenager pleads guilty to hit-and-run that killed nurse Áine O’Reilly
description: Keelan O’Connell (19) of Scanlon Park, Castleconnell, was under the influence of drugs at time of fatal incident
content:
A teenager has been further remanded in prison ahead of sentencing after he pleaded guilty to his role in a fatal hit-and-run in Co Limerick.
Keelan O’Connell (19), of Scanlon Park, Castleconnell, who was under the influence of drugs at the time, admitted the charge before Judge Colin Daly at Limerick Circuit Criminal Court.
Áine O’Reilly of Pallasgreen, Co Limerick , died at the scene of the crash when her car collided with a vehicle forced into its path after it was hit by O’Connell’s vehicle.
The collision occurred on the N24, at Grange West, Boher on February 13th. Áine O’Reilly, a nurse, was on her way to work at Shannondoc, Limerick, at the time.
Garda Tony Burke, of Henry Street Garda station, previously told the court O’Connell was driving a “high-powered” Volkswagen Golf “at excess speed” when he attempted to perform a “dangerous manoeuvre” moments prior to the crash.
He said O’Connell collided with a Peugeot car as he attempted to undertake it, forcing it into the path of Áine O’Reilly, who was driving a Nissan Micra.
Burke said O’Connell “fled the scene on foot” without offering assistance to Áine O’Reilly or the driver of the Peugeot.
O’Connell handed himself in to gardaí a few days later. He admitted during interviews under caution that he had consumed “cannabis” and “fast gas” , said Burke.
Áine O’Reilly suffered “catastrophic injuries” and died at the scene, the garda said.
Following his arrest, O’Connell was refused bail after Burke put forward strenuous objections in court. He told the hearing O’Connell would continue to commit serious crimes, including dangerous driving, and would pose “a further risk of loss of life” to citizens if bailed.
Burke said CCTV footage, dashcam footage, as well as statements provided from independent witnesses provided “strong” evidence against releasing O’Connell, who told gardaí he won the Volkswagen Golf in a raffle a few days prior to the fatal collision.
He did not make any reply when charged earlier this year but pleaded guilty to eight charges on Monday. These included dangerous driving causing death, dangerous driving causing serious bodily harm to the Peugeot driver, hit-and-run charges of failing to remain at the scene, failing to offer assistance, failing to report the collision to gardaí, as well as driving without a licence and without insurance.
The judge remanded O’Connell in continuing custody for a sentence hearing in November.

title: Russell Brand had ‘maniacal grin’ as he dragged woman into toilet and raped her, court told
description: Comedian faces charges of rape and sexual assault against six women, which he denies
content:
Russell Brand had a “weird maniacal” grin on his face like a clown when he grabbed a woman’s breasts before dragging her into a toilet and raping her, a court has heard.
The 51-year-old comedian is accused of orally raping the MTV worker as he told her: “You want to do this,” and: “Come on, don’t be a spoilsport.”
The woman said she was shaking and “numb” after the assault at a birthday party at a bar in Soho, London, 2004.
Brand faces three charges of rape, three of sexual assault and one of indecent assault against six women, in allegations spanning 10 years from 1999 to 2009. He denies all the charges and has pleaded not guilty.
The TV personality sat still and upright in the dock on Monday as the woman’s pre-recorded police interview was played to jurors at Southwark crown court.
She told detectives she found Brand funny on Big Brother spin-off shows on Channel 4, but that he sexually assaulted her within a minute of meeting her at the bar.
She said: “He literally just grabbed my boobs, out of nowhere, just in the middle of a conversation and I just remember this weird maniacal grin, looming in front of me as he just grabbed my boobs.
“I was completely in shock and was like: ‘What the hell are you doing? I’ve literally just met you.’ Then literally he grabbed my arm and dragged me into the toilets.”
She broke down in tears as she recounted how, within seconds, Brand allegedly orally raped her in the toilet as she told him: “What are you doing? I don’t want to do this.”
She said: “I pushed him away and said: ‘Come on, come on, don’t be a spoilsport.’ He kept pushing my head down and wouldn’t let me go. I just froze. I didn’t know what to do.”
She said she closed her eyes during the alleged attack and remembered a man knocking on the toilet door saying: “Are you okay?” before she walked out in a daze.
“I remember this really, really clearly – he turned to me and went: ‘Oh, I guess we should swap numbers now’, like it was just all normal, like he hadn’t just forced me to do that,” she recalled.
The woman alleged she then recalled being “steered” into Brand’s car before the comedian’s driver ferried them to a different bar in Camden.
“I was in disbelief and shock and I felt this nudge and I looked around and he [Brand] had his penis out again in the car and he was going ‘come on, come on, suck it’ and I was just like ‘no’. He took ‘no’ for an answer then.”
The woman said she told a friend Brand had attempted to rape her but did not tell him the full extent of what had happened, telling police: “I just felt this shame that I allowed him to do that to me. I just didn’t want to admit it to myself, not to anyone, but it had happened.”
Days later she told another colleague part of what had happened and told them Brand was a “sexual predator”.
She said 2023 media reports about Brand’s alleged sexual misconduct led her to come forward to police, telling the officer: “Seeing it all in the press has made me relive it all.”
In cross-examination, Brand’s barrister, Ian Winter, suggested the woman had “happily accompanied” Brand to the toilets and that she had been excited and charmed to meet him.
“I was not charmed in the slightest. I’d met this person for a minute before I was sexually assaulted,” she replied.

title: ‘This is a big club with a tremendous history’ - Duncan Ferguson named as new Glentoran manager
description: Ferguson was an assistant manager at Everton  before taking charge at Forest Green and Inverness
content:
Duncan Ferguson has been appointed manager of Irish Premiership side Glentoran.
Ferguson, 54, has signed what the Belfast club have a described as a multiyear contract, with his former Dundee United team-mate Gary Bollan joining him as his assistant.
Ferguson takes over from Declan Devine after the former Derry City and Bohemians boss left the club in September after two and a half years in charge.
“I am delighted to become manager of Glentoran,” Ferguson told the club website.
“This is a big club with a tremendous history, and it is a great opportunity for me. I know that success here will be judged on what we win.”
Ferguson was previously assistant manager to Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez at Everton and was in caretaker control of the Toffees twice, before taking charge at Forest Green and Inverness.

title: More than €650,000 spent on fire-safety works at Farmleigh House
description: Work not yet complete at Phoenix Park property, which is used as accommodation for visiting heads of state
content:
More than €650,000 has been spent on fire-safety works at Farmleigh House in the Phoenix Park after an inspection found defective doors that would not close properly and gaps in fire protection.
An internal assessment of the historic Dublin property – which is used as accommodation for visiting heads of state and other dignitaries – identified dozens of issues, including two locations where fire doors were needed but none were fitted.
Internal documents estimated the cost of works to improve safety for visitors and members of the public would be around €853,000, excluding VAT.
Records released under Freedom of Information detail spending so far of €653,000, excluding VAT, with the final bill yet to be settled.
The work was carried out after an assessment in August 2022 found significant safety issues including fire doors that did not close when released.
An inspection identified missing and damaged seals, gaps around the tops and sides of doors, and several examples of an issue termed “non-compliant hold open”.
One door had a large crack in its panel while others were warped or got caught on the floor when swinging shut.
According to the project documents, 104 internal doors, windows or cabinet doors would need to be upgraded or replaced.
Separately, new escape signage, fire stopping and electronic security locks were also required, according to the records.
A business case prepared in the summer of 2024 suggested construction would take about a year but that the house would remain available for use while the works were under way.
It said planning permission was not required as the work would be classed as maintenance of a protected structure.
Asked about the project, a spokesperson for the Office of Public Works (OPW) said the works were necessary to bring the historic property “in line with current fire-safety building regulations”.
They said: “As a result of an internal fire-safety report of the building, revised upgrades were carried out including fire-stopping measures, upgrading multiple internal doors and windows, upgrading of electronic security locks, and other necessary fire-safety and security improvements.
“These structural protection works are designed to safeguard occupants during a fire or emergency.”
The spokesperson said the works had to be completed carefully to protect Farmleigh House’s original features, furniture and artwork.
“Although this project is nearing completion on site, the OPW is unable to provide final costs until account is agreed,” they added.

title: Ardagh’s new owners to sell food-cans joint venture
description: Dismantling of Paul Coulson’s packaging  empire continues
content:
Ardagh Group ‘s creditors-turned-owners are pressing ahead with plans to dismantle the packaging multinational built by Irish financier Paul Coulson over 25 years, with a deal announced on Monday to sell its food-cans joint venture.
The company, which traces its roots back to the 1932 foundation of the long-defunct Irish Glass Bottle Company, said it would receive $90 million (€80.2 million) in net proceeds from the sale of its 42 per cent stake in Trivium Packaging to Connecticut-based packaging group Silgan Holdings.
Trivium’s majority owner, the Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, is also selling its stake to Silgan in a deal that puts an enterprise value on the highly-indebted business of $3.4 billion (€3 billion).
The deal comes less than a week after the Luxembourg-based Ardagh Group, which recorded $9.6 billion of sales last year, excluding Trivium, got the go-ahead from a court in the grand duchy to proceed with a plan to sell its 76 per cent-owned drink-cans unit, Ardagh Metal Packaging (AMP).
AMP, which is listed in New York and has a market value of $2.8 billion, is the most valuable part of the corporate giant built by Coulson through a series of debt-fuelled acquisitions over the years.
That was before he lost control of the business last year to a group of senior unsecured and junior bondholders – who were owed $4.2 billion – in a significant debt restructuring. The deal saw legacy equity holders, led by Coulson, being paid $300 million to walk away.
[ Ardagh weighs selling African glass unit Opens in new window ]
The new owners were reported earlier this month to be weighing the potential sale of Ardagh Group’s African glass business. Conversations over a possible sale of the unit, which Ardagh bought in 2022 for an enterprise value of $1 billion, are said to be at an early stage.
The Trivium sale is expected to close in mid-2027 and is subject to required regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions, Ardagh Group said.
“The sale agreement of Ardagh Group’s minority investment stake in Trivium represents a favourable outcome for all stakeholders,” said Ardagh Group chairman Mar Porto. “For Ardagh Group, the disposal of a noncore investment helps to simplify our overall business and organisational structure, with the net cash proceeds expected to be used towards reinvestment in the business or towards debt reduction.”
Ardagh Group’s net debt amounted to $8.89 billion at the end of June, which equated to 6.1 times its earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation for the preceding 12 months.

title: European governments opted for ‘Trumpian’ turn on development aid, says Richmond
description: Cutting back Irish development aid in Budget 2027 would have sent out ‘terrible message’
content:
Several European governments took an unfortunate “Trumpian” turn by cutting back on humanitarian development aid for short-term populist gain, Minister of State Neale Richmond has said.
In unusually critical remarks aimed at other European countries, the Fine Gael TD said recent decisions in the Netherlands, Sweden and Finland to scale back budgets for development aid were an exercise in “ideological isolationism”.
Richmond, the Minister of State responsible for international development, said there was “never any real serious push” to cut the State’s aid contributions during recent budget negotiations.
The Department of Foreign Affairs had argued that cuts in Budget 2027 would have represented the first reduction in development assistance since the financial crash more than a decade ago.
“A €20 million cut to our aid budget would not make a huge impact on our overall domestic budget, but it would send a terrible message,” Richmond said.
More broadly, he added, there was a sense across Europe that slashing the amount of money earmarked for overseas development aid had become “acceptable”.
“The Finnish government, the previous Swedish government, the previous Dutch government, very much went for the Trumpian agenda,” he told The Irish Times.
The withdrawal of the US as a major contributor of development aid, and a decision by President Donald Trump’s administration to shutter USAid , has created a huge funding shortfall across humanitarian organisations and projects in the global south.
At a time when civil society was calling for Europe to step up and help fill the gap, the opposite had happened, Richmond said. Trump’s decision had kicked off a “contagion” that saw European governments consider pulling back as well, he added.
Late last year, the Swedish government – which relied on the support of the far-right Sweden Democrats party – announced it was phasing out development aid to Zimbabwe, Mozambique and three other countries, to free up funds to send to Ukraine.
The previous Dutch coalition government, which for the first time included Geert Wilders’s far-right Party for Freedom, proposed cutting €1 billion from its development budget over a five-year period. However, a new government led by centrist prime minister Rob Jetten, sworn in earlier this year, said it would reverse some of those cuts.
The drive to cut back on development aid was down to an “ideological isolationism” pushed by populist right-wing forces on the rise across Europe, Richmond said.
“In this environment, standing still is something that shouldn’t be underestimated,” he said.
The conversation inside the European Union had shifted to a better place more recently, with some governments walking back planned cuts, he said.
Richmond said commentary during the fuel protests had questioned why the State was providing financial support to Ukraine during its war with Russia, or funding development projects in Africa.
He said the debate about irregular migration should not be limited to the idea of “building bigger walls”. More attention should be put on giving people “the resources and the reason to stay in their own country longer, to have better lives”.
Populist rhetoric about slashing overseas aid budgets was “great for a soundbite” but actually undermined Europe’s security in the long run, he added.
“You look at the amount of funding that’s been pulled out of Mali by European actors and then who’s filled the gap? Russia,” Richmond said. “If you pull out of particularly sub-Saharan Africa, it gets filled by China and Russia.”
Politicians needed to do a better job of making the case for development aid.
“This works. It’s a good thing that for 25 years in a row HIV/Aids infections went down,” he said.

title: Liam Gallagher, who hasn’t released a worthwhile song since 1995, is wrong about Fontaines DC
description: Liam Gallagher has accused Fontaines DC of ‘not being good enough’ to open for them despite releasing five dud-free albums while Oasis rack up a fortune as a nostalgia jukebox for Gen-Xers
content:
R ock stars of a certain age love to live in the past – and for proof you only have to look to 54-year-old Liam Gallagher and his tragic attempts to start a Blur v Oasis-style feud with Dublin’s all-conquering Fontaines DC .
Liam recently took to social media to claim Fontaines “don’t have any tunes” and are “not good enough” to open for Oasis on their Cash Grab 2027 world tour, coming to a credit card bill near you very soon.
Not good enough? Oh really, Liam – and you would know, not having released a worthwhile song since 1995 and today living an artistically aimless (if extremely lucrative) shadow existence as nostalgia jukebox for Gen Xers who can’t bear to chuck out their old bucket hats.
Yes, 1995, the year of (What’s The Story) Morning Glory and the last time Oasis achieved anything of cultural relevance. Their final moment of pop music pertinence predates high-speed internet, the smartphone, the Irish housing bubble, the genre of nu-metal, the birth of the entire line-up of indie band Geese and the moral collapse of Manchester City into a cash-drunk parody of a top-flight soccer team.
Talk about clinging on to old glories. Ever since, the Gallaghers and their fanbase have been getting by on the fumes of the band Oasis used to be. And were they even that good to begin with, or just a terrace-anthem dumbing-down of the transcendent indie pop made by Liam’s idols The Stone Roses ?
Liam’s delicate ego is still presumably recovering from Fontaines’ hard-to-disagree-with assertion in 2024 that the return of Oasis was “really annoying” – and, by extension, represented another step along rock music’s descent into dotage. “I’m not excited about it ... to be honest,” said the band’s Conor Deegan . “I feel like we get caught in the last era – like the ’10s – and into such a nostalgic thing that we’re forgetting to make new things.”
It is worth pointing out that not everyone in Fontaines DC agreed – singer Grian Chatten distanced himself from the remarks. He was also at the premiere of the new Oasis documentary, Don’t Look Back in Anger – a soulless piece of fan service that had nothing interesting to say about the troubled relationship between Noel and Liam and which instead insisted that we simply roll with it and enjoy footage from their comeback tour, though unlike that tour, the price of going to see the documentary at the cinema didn’t skyrocket depending on the length of the queue.
Oasis will live forever in the estimation of their fans – and who doesn’t love to squeeze into some Fred Perry, retrieve that aforementioned bucket hat from the back of the wardrobe and honk their way through the chorus of Live Forever? Even when you’ve had to take out a new mortgage and put off the kitchen extension to pay for the privilege of seeing them in concert.
But as a band rather than a cash-generating nostalgia machine, Oasis haven’t been at the races for decades and their transformation into top-drawer stodge merchants was arrested only by their break-up in 2009. What a bullet we dodged – imagine the music Oasis would have continued to roll out in the 2000s and beyond had Liam and Noel’s sibling enmity not bubbled over backstage in Paris 17 years ago.
As Oasis fans survey their ruined bank accounts in advance of their Slane Castle dates, here is a teaser to ponder. What’s their favourite post-Morning Glory album? It’s obviously a trick question as each of those records is instantly forgettable. Some are so inert they can’t even bother to be bland and instead just exist in a nether-state of whinging, artistically bankrupt dad-rock.
[ Fontaines DC: ‘We just hang out with ourselves and don’t really interact as much with other people’ Opens in new window ]
That’s in contrast to Fontaines DC, who have done what every decent group should in order to prove their durability and that is to continually shape-shift and to look to the future.
Yes, their latest album, Dopamine Chamber , is good rather than great and too indebted to the brooding synth pop of late-period Joy Division and early Cure. But it does at least try to do something different and to move on from early hits such as Boys in the Better Land. Just like the Gallaghers, Fontaines are also of course playing Slane .
Oasis by comparison, are men in their 50s trying to recapture that gone-in-a-blink thrill of being in your 20s and believing that you really can live forever. But you never can go back – no matter how much you spend on Oasis Adidas merch or how enthusiastically you dance the Poznan during Cigarettes and Alcohol.
The grim fact is that we all have to grow up and that we can’t be 21 and fearless in perpetuity. That’s a truth that Oasis are unwilling to confront.
Fontaines DC meanwhile are forging ahead, trying new things and bringing their fanbase with them. They’ve released five albums with not a dud among them while Oasis rack up a fortune as live music’s eternal karaoke kings – getting rich(er) off a glorious past that was over in a heartbeat and which wasn’t all that glorious in the first place.

title: Grocery price inflation hits nearly 5%, latest data shows
description: Four years of sustained increases have cost average Irish households well over €3,000
content:
Grocery inflation has climbed again and is currently running at 4.7 per cent, according to the latest figures from Worldpanel by Numerator.
The figures suggest that the rate at which prices are climbing in Irish supermarket has gone up by almost 1 per cent since the August data was released by the retail analysts.
If inflation is maintained at the current rate over the next 12 months, a household that spends €200 a week on groceries will spend just under €500 more over the next year than they did last year.
The figures come following almost four years of sustained increases that have cost average Irish households well in excess of €3,000 compared with the years leading up to the end of 2021.
The data points to take-home grocery sales increasing by 4.3 per cent over the four weeks to October 4th compared with the same period last year.
It also highlights how Irish shoppers stocked up on over-the-counter remedies in the run-up to flu season, with spending on promoted products in this category up 17 per cent.
[ Ireland is richer and spending more than 30 years ago but is it making us happy? Opens in new window ]
At the same time, a milder-than-usual September extended the summer mood, with spending on ice cream up by €11.8 million while home-baking declined by 15 per cent over the latest 12 weeks.
“The cost of living was front of mind for shoppers in Ireland in the run-up to the latest budget. Milder weather may have delayed the decision by many to turn on the heating, but the mood among shoppers is cautious, who are thinking carefully about what they put in their basket. They’re shopping little and often and keeping a close eye on spend,” said Worldpanel’s head of retail Eimear Faughnan.
She noted that promotions remain front and centre for shoppers, accounting for almost 21 per cent of grocery spend over the latest 12 weeks.
“Special offers remain a key tool for shoppers looking to keep their grocery bills in check and make pricier items and larger packs more affordable, and the increase in promotional spending is further evidence that the focus is on value for money for many,” Faughnan said.
Branded ranges held 50.9 per cent of the market, with sales up 12.4 per cent year on year. Own label grew at a similar pace, up 3 per cent but premium own label was the standout performer, with sales up 11.9 per cent.
Although Halloween is still almost two weeks away, shoppers are getting an early start on the festive season. Branded ranges across chocolate confectionery grew by €16 million, biscuits by €15.6 million and sweets by €12.9 million.
Over the latest 12 weeks, Dunnes commanded a market share of 24.8 per cent market share, with year-on-year sales growth of 7.2 per cent, while Tesco was on 24 per cent with year-on-year value growth of 6.7 per cent.
SuperValu continues to be behind the big two with 18.8 per cent of the market, up 3.3 per cent on the previous 12 weeks. Lidl stands at 14.6 per cent while Aldi holds 10.8 per cent of the market.

title: PSNI feared gun use by dissident republicans if parade went down Garvaghy Road, court told
description: High Court in Belfast is hearing a challenge to the decisions that led to ban of Drumcree march
content:
Police believed dissident republicans may have used firearms to attack officers if the Drumcree parade passed along the Garvaghy Road in Portadown, Co Armagh, the High Court in Belfast has heard.
The court on Monday heard extracts from an intelligence report provided by Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) Chief Constable Jon Boutcher to Northern Secretary Chris Bryant during a legal challenge to Bryant’s decision to ban the march on October 9th.
The member of the Orange Order who is seeking the judicial review is also challenging Boutcher’s decision to ask Bryant to review the determination made by the Parades Commission, which had granted permission for the parade to go ahead on September 27th.
A two-week stand-off followed between members of the Portadown District of the Orange Order and the residents of the mainly nationalist Garvaghy Road after a protest blocked the march from taking place.
Richard McConkey, counsel for the member of the Orange Order, told the court the PSNI assessment “is almost certain that dissident republicans have attended the protest, and it is possible that dissident republicans have already accessed the firearms in the Garvaghy Road area”.
He added: “It is possible that in the event of police removing protesters, firearms may be used to attack police.”
McConkey also said the police assessment pointed to “reliable intelligence”, which indicated “mainstream republicans are concerned about their ability to prevent disorder or control dissident republicans, and it remains likely that the police intervention will be met with serious disorder, which may involve the use of petrol bombs”.
Barristers representing the PSNI and Bryant argued the decisions made by the Chief Constable and Northern Secretary on October 9th were legally sound and the request for a judicial review of them should be rejected.
Peter Coll, counsel for the PSNI, said its position throughout “has been to facilitate the lawful procession” permitted by the Parades Commission determination. He said its assessment was that “all available lawful and proportionate options to facilitate completion of the procession have been exhausted”.
“Any remaining options would require a substantial public order intervention that was not assessed to be proportionate, and which would carry an unacceptable risk of serious injury, disorder and a wider contagion effect across Northern Ireland,” he said.
The barrister also said that by October 9th, a “prolonged stalemate” had developed and the policing operation could not be “sustained indefinitely”.
“In the Chief Constable’s judgment, it was no longer viable to give effect to the parades commissioners’ determination,” he said.
Separately, the North’s Minister for Justice told Assembly members on Monday that the cost of policing the Drumcree parade dispute had so far cost £5.5 million (€6.53 million).
This included around £1.5 million to cover the cost of mutual aid from other UK police forces to support the PSNI, Naomi Long said, with the remainder “a mixture of overtime and additional other expenses”.
She requested that the cost of mutual aid be met in full by the UK government as it “cannot be met by the PSNI within its existing budget”.
Meanwhile, First Minister Michelle O’Neill and other Sinn Féin politicians are to be interviewed by the PSNI this week about their participation in protests against the Orange Order march on the Garvaghy Road.
In a statement, a Sinn Féin spokesperson said elected representatives who received letters from police in relation to the protests would begin attending interviews this week.
The ongoing fallout over the Drumcree dispute was again raised in the Stormont Assembly, with O’Neill challenged by the DUP over her participation in the protests.
Accusing the DUP of “hypocrisy”, she said she was “proud” to stand with the Garvaghy Road residents and would “deal with whatever processes come my way, but you are not my judge and you’re not my jury”.

title: The Rams can’t get their kicks as season goes from bad to worse
description: Los Angeles were tipped as a Super Bowl contender after assembling a star studded line-up. Now they’ve lost three of their last four games
content:
The Rams were supposed to be the closest thing the NFL had seen to a superteam in some time. Instead, they’re 2-4, have lost three of their last four games and are last in the NFC West. So much has gone awry, so quickly.
Sunday was rock bottom (for now). The Rams lost to the division’s ugly stepchild, the Cardinals – a team they had beaten in 16 of their last 19 meetings – on a day when Arizona didn’t manage to score a touchdown. They didn’t need to, because Arizona kicker Chad Ryland connected on six field goal attempts, the last one a 43-yarder as time expired.
The game was a tale of two kickers, in that the Cardinals had a superb one and the Rams didn’t have one at all. Days after releasing Harrison Mevis following a league-worst four misses in the season’s first five weeks, the Rams came into this game with Blake Grupe, whom they’d plucked off the Jets practice squad. Grupe got hurt covering a kick-off return in the first quarter, leaving the Rams literally kicker-less for the duration. (Mevis, a big fella whose nickname is the Thick Kicker, or “Thiccer,” has about 80lbs on the 5ft 7in Grupe.)
The absence of a specialist kicker affected the game. The Rams tried for a two-point conversion after a touchdown in the second quarter, preferring not to have punter Ethan Evans attempt a point after. The Cardinals sacked Matthew Stafford, and the attempt failed.
In the third quarter, the Rams faced a fourth-and-one at the Arizona 27-yard line, in what would normally be easy field-goal range. (Of course, Sean McVay may have gone for it anyway in such a spot.) Unable to even consider a kick here, the Rams pushed up the middle and were stacked up at the line for a turnover on downs. Arizona drove the other way for three points.
McVay’s bunch could have won anyway. When the Rams tied the game with 42 seconds left, McVay did sound out his punter, Evans, who nailed his PAT, suggesting maybe he was more reliable as a kicker than his coach believed. But then the Rams’ defence had a meltdown, taking an unnecessary roughness flag and allowing Jacoby Brissett to quickly march Arizona 40 yards to set up Ryland’s winner. Final score: 18-16 to Arizona, an utter disaster for the home team.
A bit of everything has gone wrong. Prized defensive end Myles Garrett, the best defensive player in the NFL, is yet to return as he rehabs from knee surgery. Future Hall of Fame defensive tackle Aaron Donald came out of a years-long retirement and has looked, well, like a man who has come out of a years-long retirement. The Rams had a solid performance against the run in this game but entered it having given up the sixth-most ground yards in football.
Meanwhile, Stafford has only looked like his MVP self in one game all year, a week two romp over the very meh Giants. Despite facing less pressure than any other QB in the league, per Sports Reference, Stafford has not been able to make his usual magic. Part of it is that he’s been rushing to get the ball out quickly; his 2.2-second average time to throw is his quickest rate on record.
Puka Nacua has only played in four games, and Davante Adams, who has served as the No 1 wideout in his absence, left Sunday’s game with a suspected knee injury. Things feel like they’re falling apart rapidly for a team expected to compete for the Super Bowl.
There is not much good news for the Rams, but there is this: The Chargers moved to 0-6 with a loss to the Chiefs, meaning the Rams still comfortably have the best record of a team based at SoFi Stadium. The two Angeleno clubs face each other in two weeks. That matchup will not be for the faint of heart.
The 25-year-old had his best game of the season in a 34-31 shoot-out win over the Jaguars in London, as Houstonians watched early in the morning. Stroud led a game-winning field goal drive after Jacksonville’s rocket-legged kicker, Cam Little, tied things up late with a 60-yard field goal.
The winning drive was a fitting capper for Stroud, who threw an interception but was usually steady, and mixed in more of the sizzle that had come with the steak early in his career. Stroud finished 24-of-34 for 312 yards and three scores and didn’t take a sack. His best work came in tandem with receiver Jaylin Noel, who had a 50-yard catch to set up a critical Houston TD just before half-time. Noel also caught a touchdown. Newly acquired wideout Marvin Harrison Jr caught three of his four targets for 34 yards.
The previously winless Titans ran that many plays in their 26-20 win over the moribund Colts, who fell to 2-4 and strayed even further from relevance under head coach Shane Steichen and GM Chris Ballard. It’s the fewest plays a winning team has run all season, three behind the 48 the Seahawks had in their season-opening Super Bowl rematch against the Patriots.
It’s not as if the Titans did all that much with those offensive snaps, either. Cam Ward needed 22 throws to reach a whopping 102 yards but still outplayed Daniel “Dimes” Jones, who took six sacks and threw two picks. A blocked punt keyed the comeback, and rookie wideout Carnell Tate, the number four pick in this year’s draft, caught his first career touchdown. Tennessee had lost a mesmerising 11 in a row in the division. Poor Jonathan Taylor: the supremely talented running back deserves better than playing on a team like the Colts.
Dallas Goedert shows off his tight end pic.twitter.com/exl69Az8u3
Dallas Goedert was just minding his business, running a corner route against the Panthers, when his business became our business. Carolina cornerback Will Lee III struggled to stay with the Eagles veteran and resorted to a particular brand of grabbiness.
Lee, exposed by the route Goedert had run, decided to expose the tight end in a different way. A defensive pass interference call gave the Eagles a first down, but it wasn’t enough to save them in what became a 25-14 home loss. The Birds lost their fourth in a row and continue to reel in an NFC East that somebody is going to have to win.
♦ Caleb Williams looks fine. The Bears’ franchise QB returned from a right hamstring strain that had kept him out since week two, and he led Chicago to a 31-23 win over the Falcons. Williams didn’t throw an incomplete pass until his 13th attempt of the game, three minutes into the second quarter, and completed 30 of his 36 throws for 305 yards and a touchdown.
It wasn’t entirely peaches and cream, as the four sacks Williams took were his most in a game since September 2025. But in general, he was comfortable with the speed of the game and kept the Bears on track despite a run game that never took off.
♦ The Steelers are doing it again, and by “it” I mean “contending in the AFC North despite being deeply unpleasant to watch”. Pittsburgh came back from 13-0 down to beat the woeful Buccaneers in Tampa, 26-19, and move to 4-2. Combined with the Browns’ buzzer-beating win over the Ravens, that result left all three of those teams tied atop the division with the Bengals (on bye) just a half-game behind.
Aaron Rodgers looked as athletic as a 58-year-old uncle, taking five sacks and throwing a pick on a screen pass. The Steelers cartoonishly squandered a first-and-goal at the three-yard line after the Bucs’ rookie backup, Jalon Daniels, threw an interception to former Buc Jamel Dean late in the fourth quarter. But after settling for three on that series and allowing Daniels to lead a game-tying drive, Pittsburgh got things under control in overtime.
Rodgers also tied Peyton Manning for third on the all-time passing touchdown list (539). Rodgers won’t catch the two men ahead of him: Drew Brees (571) and Tom Brady (649), but the fact that he got this far is a testament to his skill and longevity. In another blast from the past, Pittsburgh’s Jalen Ramsey had two sacks, including the game-ender in OT. Can I interest anyone in the Steel City in a 10-7 record and a home wild card defeat?
How did Josh Allen make this TD pass to Keon Coleman? BUFvsLV on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/CNLw6KW2tC
♦ One team who are extremely pleasant to watch? The Bills, who moved to 5-1 with a 33-30 win in Las Vegas. Josh Allen didn’t have an overwhelming statistical day but produced one of the more magical moments of his career. On a third-hand-eight in the red zone in a one-score game, Allen meandered through traffic in the backfield for a full six seconds before casually flicking a backhanded looper over six Raiders (five near him, one in the secondary) and into the waiting arms of Keon Coleman for a touchdown. The video speaks for itself. What a player.

title: Australian MP Helen Haines has critical injuries after being hit by car in ‘deliberate act’
description: A 43-year-old man with a knife in his car was arrested at the scene
content:
Australian independent MP Helen Haines has been critically injured after being hit by a car in what prime minister Anthony Albanese called “a deliberate act” outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, in regional Victoria.
Albanese confirmed on Monday that a man was in custody after the alleged attack on Haines that was now being investigated by the Australian federal police and a counterterror taskforce.
He said the motive for the alleged attack was not known, and would not comment on whether the suspect was known to police.
“Helen Haines is incredibly hard-working. She is fiercely intelligent, but most importantly, she’s just a thoroughly decent human being, full of integrity and respected right across the parliament, and from everyone who comes into contact with her, she is a well-loved member of her community, and this will come as an incredible shock to that community,” Albanese said.
He said he respected her integrity most of all.
“It doesn’t mean we always agree, but I always agree that her motives are good,” Albanese said.
“Our thoughts remain with Helen Haines at this very difficult time.”
In a statement, Victoria police said a 43-year-old man from Tarrawingee, about 10km from Wangaratta, was in custody and that a knife had allegedly been found in his car. They alleged he had been detained by a passerby when he exited the car.
The statement said the woman who was struck was in a critical condition.
“Police have arrested a man after a woman was struck by a vehicle in Wangaratta this afternoon.
“It is understood a white Toyota LandCruiser struck the 65-year-old woman outside an office on Murphy Street about 3.35pm.”
Police said that they were investigating as to whether it was an intentional act, and it was not known if “the parties are known to each other”.
Speaking at the scene, acting Supt Ashley Mason said it was being treated as an isolated incident.
He said that the bystanders who assisted in the arrest and with Haines should be commended for acting as they did when confronted with a “horrific tragic incident”.
It was a “dynamic incident” with an extensive crime scene, he said.
The prime minister and Victoria police said they were not aware of any recent direct threats to Haines.
Albanese later said on the ABC’s 7.30 programme that while he did not want to speculate on the motivation for the alleged attack, he had repeatedly warned “the temperature has increased in recent times” in relation to politics.
He had feared that would increase the risk of political violence occurring in Australia that had been seen in other western democracies.
Albanese, who became emotional at times during the interview, said he first was told that Haines had been injured in a car accident, before being informed it was allegedly a deliberate act.
The home affairs minister, Tony Burke, also said there had been an increase in threats towards politicians.
“The year before last, we had 951 reports of harassing and threatening behaviour against various high officeholders,” he said.
“The more recent financial year, that 951 has gone to 1,067.”
In a statement, Haines’s family confirmed that she had been injured and thanked bystanders for their assistance.
“This afternoon, our beloved Helen was involved in an incident outside her Wangaratta Electorate Office, and is receiving medical care,” they said in the statement.
“We thank the swift assistance of bystanders and the dedicated health workers who assisted her, and police for their response.
“Our family, and Helen’s staff, will be making no further comment at this time, and ask that their privacy be respected by the public and media.
Haines was airlifted to hospital in Melbourne.
The Victorian premier, Ben Carroll, said he knew the alleged attack would be devastating for the Wangaratta community and all those Haines represented.
“I am deeply appalled by this [alleged] violent attack on Helen Haines,” he said in a statement.
“My thoughts – and the thoughts of all Victorians – are with Helen, her family, her friends, her colleagues and her community.”
The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, said the incident was a “shocking day for our nation”, and that political attacks cannot be normalised in Australia.
The Liberal leader said he was “deeply saddened and distressed” and was praying for Haines and her family.
“This is a shocking day for our nation ... Australians will be angry and appalled by the [alleged] attack on Helen outside her electorate office in Wangaratta,” he said in a statement on social media.
In a social media post, theNationals MP Michael McCormack said it was “such awful news”.
“Sending my love and best wishes to Helen Haines for a full and speedy recovery,” McCormack said.
Police were expected to release a statement regarding the incident on Monday night.
Haines has represented the electorate of Indi since 2019.
Asio has in recent years repeatedly warned about the rising threat of politically motivated violence.
“Political differences, political debates and political protests are essential parts of a healthy democracy,” Mike Burgess, the Asio director general, said in 2025.
“Unfortunately, here and overseas, levels of personal grievance and frustration are growing.
“Rightly or wrongly some Australians feel dispossessed, disaffected, disenfranchised ... many of the aggrieved do not necessarily espouse violent views, but may still see violence as a legitimate way to effect political or societal change.”
He added last year that although Australia’s terrorism threat level remained at probable, the system was not “designed for a situation like the one we now face”.
“We do know the environment is degrading and acts of politically motivated violence are becoming more likely than probable suggests,” he said.
“Just as climate change increases the likelihood of extreme weather but does not forecast specific storms, politically motivated violence, including acts of terrorism, is more likely even though we cannot predict a specific attack.” – Guardian

title: PwC revenue growth trails Deloitte and EY
description: Europe, Middle East and Africa revenues rose 0.7% following war in Iran and a slowdown in work for Saudi Arabian government
content:
PwC’s revenue growth has lagged its largest Big Four rivals over the past year after a sharp slowdown in Europe and the Middle East triggered by geopolitical strife.
The accounting and consulting firm on Monday reported global revenues of $60.2 billion (€53.5 billion) for the year to June 30th – a 3.5 per cent increase when adjusted for currency fluctuations.
That represented an acceleration from the previous 12 months, when revenues rose by 2.7 per cent. However, rivals Deloitte and EY have both posted faster year-on-year growth in recent weeks.
“We achieved robust growth, even in the face of geopolitical and economic uncertainty,” said Mohamed Kande, PwC’s global chair.
Results were held back by the performance of PwC’s Europe, Middle East and Africa region, which grew 0.7 per cent after being affected by the Middle East conflict and a slowdown in consulting work for the Saudi Arabian government.
PwC UK, the legal entity that comprises its British and Middle Eastern businesses, said last month its revenues had declined for the first time in more than two decades.
[ PwC UK revenues slide for first time in more than a decade Opens in new window ]
Asia-Pacific, PwC’s smallest region, recorded the fastest growth at 7.7 per cent, as it began to recover from scandals in China and Australia that hit business in those markets two years ago.
PwC’s 3.5 per cent revenue growth compared with 3.8 per cent at Deloitte and 4.7 per cent at EY.
After more than five consecutive years of faster growth by EY, its revenues are now just $3.2 billion behind PwC.
Deloitte remains the largest of the Big Four firms, while KPMG – which reports its annual revenue figures later this year – is the smallest.
Like all the big consulting firms, PwC has been wrestling with the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on its business, retooling its operations to use the technology and building a suite of new services to clients such as advising on how to implement AI.
However, uncertainty over how the technology fits into existing IT infrastructure has been holding back the consulting industry.
Revenue growth in PwC’s advisory arm, its largest division, slowed to 3 per cent in the past year from 4.5 per cent, totalling $25.8 billion.
Its audit and tax divisions grew at 2.6 and 6.3 per cent, respectively, to $20.5 billion and $13.9 billion.
PwC said it had continued to add to its headcount, which reached almost 370,000 at the end of June, up from 364,000 a year earlier. – Copyright The Financial Times Limited 2026

title: Radisson Hotel Group sees further room to grow across Ireland’s hotel market
description: Radisson Blu is the most prominent brand for the group in Ireland, and it has been the largest upper-upscale brand in Europe for 15 years
content:
From the breathtaking natural landscape of Sligo and rich cultural heritage of Cork, to the world-renowned local hospitality, Ireland is the ideal location for hotel investors and operators. Irish hotels routinely outperform their European counterparts across metrics including occupancy, revenue and daily rates, according to an analysis from Savills , highlighting how Ireland is a market with significant potential for hotel development.
Ireland’s ubiquitous appeal as a destination is well established: 6.4 million foreign visitors travelled to the State last year. With an established business and events market, internationally recognisable destinations and a diverse visitor base from across the globe, Ireland is naturally a key location in Radisson Hotel Group ’s wider development strategy.
Radisson Hotel Group’s portfolio includes eight hotels in Ireland: in Dublin, Galway, Sligo, Letterkenny, Athlone, Limerick, Cork and Shannon, ensuring that its presence goes beyond the country’s big cities and is felt nationwide. The group’s Irish estate showcases how multiple propositions can target distinct market segments and traveller preferences. The system contribution of these eight hotels from Radisson Hotel Group’s direct channels is approximately 50 per cent (excluding online travel agents), meaning one in two bookings for its hotels in Ireland is coming from Radisson Hotel Group’s direct booking channels.
As Radisson Hotel Group looks at future opportunities in Ireland, the ever-growing Radisson Individuals brand continues to show significant potential. Radisson Individuals launched in 2020 to provide independent hotels with an opportunity to diversify their business mix and increase direct reservations, which have a lower cost of booking.
The affiliation brand allows hotels to not just retain their individual character but to enhance it by drawing on Radisson Hotel Group’s expertise and support across service, proposition, operations and marketing. Member properties also gain access to Radisson Hotel Group’s global distribution systems, reservation network and Radisson Rewards loyalty programme and its 30 million members. Radisson Individuals has more than 100 properties worldwide, including 10 in the UK in locations such as Bath, Inverness, Surrey and Cambridge.
Since joining Radisson Individuals, UK hotels in the portfolio have experienced a significant increase in revenue per available room, with a system contribution from Radisson Hotel Group’s direct channels between 35 and 40 per cent (excluding online travel agents) in the short period of time since the brand’s emergence.
Radisson Individuals is well-suited to 3-4 year contracts, or a longer period depending on the hotel owner’s preference. The group is proud that 65 per cent of its hotel owners have multiple hotels across the brand portfolio; however, in Ireland, its eight hotels are with only three ownership groups.
Radisson Blu is the most prominent brand for the group in Ireland, and it has been the largest upper-upscale brand in Europe for 15 years. Radisson Blu Royal Hotel, Dublin is based in the heart of the capital close to Dublin Castle, Iveagh House and the city’s cultural attractions, with a range of facilities designed for both relaxing and exploring. After spending the day sightseeing, guests can unwind at the Velvaere Spa, inspired by the Norse meaning of wellness, featuring a thermal suite and gym to offer escape and complete relaxation in the capital. Highlights of the four on site dining offerings include The Dyflin Bar, which puts a unique twist on classic Irish cuisine and celebrates local produce and the rich flavours of Ireland. Its central location makes it suited to both leisure and business travellers, while its meeting facilities and proximity to key business locations also make it complementary to the city’s growing international events and meetings market.
Over on the west coast Radisson RED Galway is the first Radisson RED property in Ireland, offering a four-star stay with 177 contemporary rooms just a short drive away from the centre of Galway city. The Radisson RED brand is known for its focus on creating casual social hubs, open plan communal spaces and eclectic artwork, offering connected spaces, contemporary design and a strong food and beverage proposition.
State-of-the-art technology and flexible design space is weaved into the hotel planning to meet the high expectations of today’s modern traveller. Self-service check in and check out kiosks guide a seamless journey, allowing guests to move through the city on their own terms.
With two food and beverage offerings on site, one of the property’s standout amenities is Lena’s Rooftop Bar & Restaurant, boasting panoramic views of Galway Bay and the city. Its menu offers quality classical cooking, local ingredients and an excellent cocktail programme, meanwhile The Claddagh Bar & Grill presents a casual dining option for diners focusing on modern Irish ingredients and local cuisine.
To thrive, hotel brands must also embrace the shift in becoming an active part of the communities in which they exist. In today’s travel landscape, properties that fail to engage with local residents and businesses ultimately struggle to reach their full potential. This integration is essential as modern travellers seek authentic experiences reflective of their destination.
Also of great importance to today’s traveller is a commitment to sustainability. As a leader in ESG for 20 years, Radisson Hotel Group is committed to net zero by 2050 through sustainable buildings, energy and operations, and is converting hotels to become verified net-zero properties.
With a strong presence across the country and growing portfolio of brands, Radisson Hotel Group views Ireland as a market with significant capacity for further expansion, particularly for the Radisson Individuals brand. Future growth will be measured by quality, not just quantity, as we shift towards a measured expansion offering distinct propositions that elevate the existing local community.

title: Davina McCall reveals new health battle against cardiovascular disease
description: The TV presenter urges women to be aware of their health and not ‘brush things off’
content:
Davina McCall has revealed she has cardiovascular disease (CVD) in a new health update after overcoming breast cancer and a brain tumour.
Speaking on her podcast, Begin Again, the TV presenter said: “I wanted to let you know, I also have cardiovascular disease, and this is a very important conversation to have.”
The former Big Brother host (59) spoke with heart attack survivor Louise McGill to highlight the importance of women’s cardiovascular health .
McCall said: “Anyone can get sick, and when I had my cancer experience ... you just suddenly feel vulnerable in a way you weren’t before ...
“Once you’ve been ill, you think, ‘Oh, I thought I was invincible.’”
McCall said she was told she had high cholesterol before being diagnosed. “I had high cholesterol and had it for quite a long time.
“It was deemed I had good cholesterol and that offset the bad or something.”
McCall urged women not to “brush things off” and make sure they are aware of their health.
She said: “Heart attacks and cardiovascular disease is rife out there, particular in women post menopause.
[ Davina McCall reveals she has undergone surgery for breast cancer Opens in new window ]
“If there’s one takeaway today it’s not to brush things off.”
CVD is the name of a group of conditions that affect the heart and blood vessels.
It is often caused by a build-up off fatty plaques in the arteries, which makes it hard for blood to flow through the body, according to the NHS.
It can be prevented with a healthy lifestyle or by taking medications if needed.
McCall has had a few problems with her health in recent years. She was diagnosed with breast cancer in October 2025 but said in April she had received the “all clear” following surgery.
McCall also underwent surgery in 2024 to remove a benign brain tumour .
The presenter had her TV debut on MTV, then spent a decade hosting Big Brother.
She has also featured in multiple other shows, including Bafta award-winning series Long Lost Family, Million Pound Drop and The Masked Singer. – PA

title: Wexford Festival Opera 2026: The Gambler review – Challenging Prokofiev comes to life  in five-star production
description: Ivan Popovsky directs a strong cast that includes the Irish tenors Gavan Ring and Seán Tester as the Wexford Festival Opera Orchestra plays a blinder
content:
Prokofiev ’s The Gambler is the left-field work from Wexford Festival Opera for 2026, the “one for the head”, as the festival likes to dub it.
The composer, who wrote his own libretto based on the Dostoevsky novella, encountered a series of misfortunes trying to get the work staged. It was a challenging opera when he completed it in 1917, was still when it was first staged in Brussels in 1927, and was again when its original version premiered at the Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow in 2001.
It’s such a busy and dissonant piece that you might imagine it was a youthful excess by the composer who would later deliver such colourful works as Peter and the Wolf, the Classical Symphony and the ballet Romeo and Juliet. But by comparison with Stravinsky’s Rite of Spring, from 1913, the opera is mild stuff.
The challenge stems from Prokofiev’s goal of writing what you might call an anti-opera. The singing defaults to a kind of agitated recitative style rather than to arias or set pieces. Subtexts and psychological states are handled by the almost hyperactive orchestra. And the wordy text flies by at dizzying speed, making it easy for any listener to feel their understanding is lagging behind the meaning.
The first two acts work as a kind of extended back story, introducing a string of characters whose concerns and relationships are all venal. Money is king, and nearly everyone is after someone else’s because they’ve already lost their own.
Of course, in the first two acts they’re mostly talking about money that’s already lost. Things get into high gear when everyone is around a roulette wheel – the chorus all turn into individual punters – and some of the losses turn into gains. But, as ever, money is mean about delivering redemption of any kind.
The production’s director, Ivan Popovsky, and his designers (Maria Tregubova, set and costumes; Paolo Bonapace, lighting) open the action in a world of stark black and white – mostly white – creating an effect that evokes a kind of snow-blindness. These are lost people. Normality has been sucked out of them, and they dance to the tune of a punishing master.
It’s when everyone gets to the roulette wheel that they perk up. This is what they live for, and the suspense they have to endure as the wheel turns is mesmerisingly reflected in the endless mechanical swirl of the orchestra and in the movements of the red-and-black-clad dancers (choreography by Luisa Baldinetti), who race around to evoke the turning of the wheel.
This production turns the scene into an unforgettable melee, all excitement and anticipation, the characters coming to life as if driven by the power of the wheel itself.
The casting is strong. The Ukrainian tenor Igor Onishchenko and the Georgian soprano Sophie Gordeladze capture the febrile, mutually enabling connection between Alexei and Polina. The Moldovan bass Alexei Botnarciuc conveys well the hopeless predicament of the General, the man whose empty pockets drive so much of the plot.
Two Irish tenors make an impression, too, Gavan Ring as the chilling Marquis and Seán Tester, projecting his voice with laser-like penetrating brightness, as the opportunistic Prince Nilsky.
The Wexford Festival Opera Orchestra plays a blinder under the Russian-born, Berlin-based Valentin Uryupin, who manages to keep stage and pit in balance while stirring up a real storm.
The Gambler will be performed again on Thursday, October 22nd, Saturday, October 24th, and Friday, October 30th. Wexford Festival Opera runs until Saturday, October 31st

title: ‘Islamist’ bomb threat email sent to ‘up to 300’ Northern Ireland schools
description: Police are treating letters as a hoax, although some schools have closed
content:
Hundreds of schools in Northern Ireland have received emailed bomb threats that police said they are treating as a hoax.
The Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) said “up to 300” schools have now reported “receiving the same emailed message which contained a generalised threat”.
It is believed similar emails have been received by some schools in other parts of the UK. Police confirmed the email originated from outside the UK.
Earlier, Stormont education minister Paul Givan said more than 150 schools in Northern Ireland had received bomb threats.
He told reporters at Stormont: “This morning 160 schools received a threat reporting – it would appear to me from Islamists threatening that sharia law will be brought into our country and that there is viable devices within those school settings and it was signed off ‘Allah Akbar’.
“That has been escalated to the PSNI, and the education authority are having emergency meetings with the police this morning.
“At this stage the advice to schools is that we’re not treating this as a viable threat but it has clearly caused huge alarm,” he said.
Givan said some schools have closed as a result of the threat. “I absolutely condemn that there has been this level of disruption caused to young people’s education.
In a statement, the education authority said it was “aware that a number of schools across Northern Ireland have received a threatening email this morning”.
“We recognise the concern this may cause for school leaders, staff, pupils and families,” it said.
“We are engaging closely with the PSNI and will act on their advice. Communications have been issued to schools, and we continue to support school leaders and keep them informed.”

title: Pet owners urged to be wary of firework noise as Halloween approaches
description: The Irish Blue Cross is urging pet owners to keep their cats and dogs safely indoors after dark
content:
Pet owners are being urged to be wary of firework noise as Halloween approaches, with nearly half of dogs badly affected by the sounds.
The Irish Blue Cross is urging pet owners to keep their cats and dogs safely indoors after dark.
Meanwhile, a Dogs Trust Ireland study found 48 per cent of dogs struggle to stay calm when fireworks can be heard.
Many dogs find fireworks frightening and distressing, which can lead to behaviours such as trembling, pacing or whining, as well as barking, panting or hiding.
This can also be “incredibly upsetting” for owners who feel powerless to help their pets, the charity said.
To support owners during fireworks season, Dogs Trust has launched the Sound Blanket, a free collection of specially designed sounds available on YouTube and Spotify that aims to help mask the sounds of fireworks.
Developed over the course of a year, the Sound Blanket was created through a partnership between Dogs Trust and the University of Salford.
The university researchers investigated the acoustic characteristics and soundwave patterns of fireworks and used their findings to develop a collection of nine sounds specifically designed to mask the sounds which triggered the fear response in dogs.
Additional testing carried out by Dogs Trust found 99 per cent of dogs tolerated the Sound Blanket and did not show adverse reactions.
Most dogs can try the Sound Blanket, but it may not be suitable for dogs who are very sensitive to music or spoken radio, the charity said.
Communications manager at Dogs Trust Ireland Paulina Padlo said: “We wanted to help owners feel more in control during fireworks season by showing them that there are lots of ways to support their dogs.
“Creating a safe, cosy space at home, closing curtains and windows, and offering enrichment activities can all help. Now, owners can also try our free Sound Blanket as another way to help their dogs feel more comfortable.”
The Irish Blue Cross also warned that fireworks could lead to scared dogs fleeing their homes and going missing.
Communications executive Corina Fitzsimons said: “The noise and flashing lights from fireworks can be terrifying for pets, who may try to escape to get away from them.
“So, please ensure your pet’s microchip details are up to date with your current phone number and home address. If you have a dog, check their ID tag is still attached to their collar or harness.”

title: Gardaí believe trio arrested after M50 pursuit were involved in earlier crime spree
description: Three masked males armed with golf clubs smashed up car and damaged house in Malahide in early hours of Sunday
content:
Gardaí believe three people arrested after a pursuit on the M50 at the weekend were involved in a crime spree in Dublin ’s northern suburbs before being caught.
The three suspects, a juvenile in his mid teens and two men in their early 20s, were in a stolen car when it stopped on the M50 near Clondalkin after initially refusing to engage with gardaí near Dublin Airport .
The trio tried to flee from the vehicle on foot and discarded items of clothing in an effort to avoid being identified from CCTV footage of some of their alleged crimes in recent days.
However, they were arrested after abandoning the car, which had hit other vehicles before being halted by gardaí.
The two men and the teenager were in a Volkswagen Golf that had been stolen in Santry in recent days.
In the early hours of Sunday, a family was threatened and their home in Malahide was damaged by three masked males.
Before that incident, one of the gang members got into a car parked in the driveway, in an apparent attempt to take the vehicle. The homeowner heard the man outside and chased him away.
However, less than a minute later, the three males appeared, armed with golf clubs, and smashed up the car and damaged the outside of the house, including breaking windows. One of them shouted into the property, demanding the car keys, before fleeing. The couple living in the house do not appear to have been injured during the incident.
Gardaí believe members of the same group were in a Volkswagen Golf first spotted by patrolling gardaí on the Naul Road near Dublin Airport, just off the northern end of the M50, on Sunday evening.
The gardaí were in the area as part of ongoing investigations into “a series of burglaries and incidents of criminal damage”.
The men in the car failed to stop at the scene and a pursuit began, involving local and divisional Garda units from across Dublin, as well as the Armed Support Unit and Garda helicopter.
“The vehicle came to a stop on the M50 near Clondalkin, where three males, two in their 20s and one juvenile in his mid-teens, were subsequently arrested,” the Garda said in a statement.
“All three are currently detained under Section 4 of the Criminal Justice Act, 1984 at Garda stations in north Dublin.
“The vehicle, a VW Golf which had been reported stolen during a recent burglary in the Santry area, has been recovered and brought for technical examination. No injuries were reported during this incident.”
An examination of the vehicle yielded a number of golf clubs and other items that could be used as weapons, including hammers.
Gardaí believe the gang had been active for some time over the weekend in the Malahide area, prowling around while masked, looking for opportunities to steal vehicles or take items of value from cars.

title: No chaos in the courts, Jim O’Callaghan says, as legal aid dispute ramps up
description: Minister expresses concern that rape cases were impacted at Central Criminal Court
content:
Minister for Justice Jim O’Callaghan has denied that there was chaos in the courts on Monday as a result of the withdrawal of services by some solicitors but raised concern that rape cases were affected by the latest escalation.
Many defence solicitors, particularly in Dublin, withdrew legal aid services after a new flat fee system for District Court cases was introduced in July.
The dispute ramped up on Monday with the withdrawal of services expanding to cases in the Central Criminal Court .
During an interview on RTÉ News, O’Callaghan denied there was chaos in the Central Criminal Court, saying there are 11 judges on the court and they were all “busy dealing with cases today”.
O’Callaghan added that of 13 listed cases, “some solicitors decided to disrupt six rape cases” and “it’s of concern to me that the only cases they sought to disrupt were rape cases that were going on”.
Earlier O’Callaghan insisted that the new regulations for the criminal legal aid system at the centre of a dispute between the Government and solicitors will not be revoked.
Speaking on Monday, O’Callaghan said he respects the work carried out by criminal defence solicitors while arguing that there has been “significant progress” in the implementation of the new legal aid system, citing the issuing of more than 3,400 legal aid certificates since it was introduced.
He said there are “very many solicitors who are working the new system and working it very effectively” while acknowledging “there is an issue in respect of solicitors in Dublin”.
O’Callaghan said he has engaged with the Law Society on this and would do so again but he urged “solicitors to continue the important work that they do, which is representing people who find themselves before the courts on criminal charges”.
O’Callaghan was speaking to reporters at the annual report launch of Ruhama, an organisation that supports women impacted by prostitution.
“I’m not going to revoke the new regulations,” he said. “The new regulations are there. I’m happy to tweak the new regulations, if there’s a necessity to do so. I’ll engage with the Law Society in respect of that.”
O’Callaghan has repeatedly argued the new approach represents a necessary reform of criminal legal aid, will achieve cost savings and is in the public interest.
He is due to appear before the Oireachtas Committee on Justice on Tuesday to be questioned over the dispute.
The escalation of the dispute was “entirely avoidable”, according to Sinn Féin spokesman for justice Matt Carthy .
Carthy said O’Callaghan had failed to “meaningfully” engage in resolution efforts.
The new payment model provides for a single flat fee of €520, irrespective of the number of charges or appearances.
Solicitors say it means they will not be paid for all the work they do, particularly in more complex cases involving children and vulnerable clients with addiction and mental health issues.
Carthy, the committee chairman, said the decision by solicitors to withdraw from all criminal defence work marked “a very serious escalation” of the dispute.
[ Meet the retirees whose hobby is watching Irish court trials: ‘It’s fascinating and costs nothing’ Opens in new window ]
“We are now facing the real prospect of significant parts of the criminal courts system grinding to a halt if this issue is not resolved urgently,” he said.
“This was entirely avoidable. For months, legal practitioners and others have warned about where this dispute was heading.”
The Sinn Féin TD said the committee would ask “serious questions” regarding how the Minister had “allowed the situation to deteriorate to this point”.
Carthy called on O’Callaghan to “engage constructively, show leadership and bring forward a resolution before access to justice is further undermined for all those who depend on our courts system”.
