Though the country faces into a potentially terrible winter, Ukraine is not losing on the battlefield. This isn’t just bravado, she says, Ukraine has liberated 250 sq km of its territory this year.
How will the war end? It would be “her” dream to see all occupied Ukrainian territory liberated, but there has to be an end to hostilities first.
“We have to get a ceasefire, but unfortunately Putin is not ready. We are defending not only our country, but Europe itself.”

title: IHRB suspend licence of trainer Jerry Murray over serious welfare concerns
description: Inspection uncovered serious deficiencies in the health, condition, care and welfare of horses in Co Offaly-based trainer’s care
content:
An Irish Horseracing Regulatory Board referrals panel has suspended the training licence of Co Offaly-based Jerry Murray over what it described as serious welfare, care and management concerns identified during inspections carried out at his premises.
An IHRB statement released on Friday outlined how an inspection by its officials on August 19th uncovered serious deficiencies in the health, condition, care and welfare of horses in Murray’s care.
At a referrals hearing chaired by Justice Frank Clarke on Wednesday, the IHRB’s chief veterinary officer Dr Lynn Hillyer outlined how there were two more visits to the yard and pointed to continuing issues concerning the welfare of certain horses and the conditions in which they were kept.
Hillyer explained that all horses present at the first inspection required veterinary intervention, either individually or at herd level. Three horses required urgent veterinary attention, including one whose condition necessitated euthanasia.
She described subsequent engagement with Murray and his vet and while remedial steps were taken, material concerns remained regarding the management of the training establishment and the welfare of some horses in his care and control.
Hillyer also outlined the extent of the continuing IHRB veterinary oversight and intervention which had been required since the initial inspection.
The IHRB told the panel that the seriousness and persistence of the welfare and management concerns, notwithstanding the remedial steps taken, together with the level of continuing regulatory and veterinary oversight required to achieve the necessary standards, was unsustainable.
John Fitzgerald of the Restricted Trainers Association told the panel that Murray accepted the gravity of the matters raised and outlined personal circumstances on his behalf.
The panel concluded that material concerns remained, and the level of continuing regulatory oversight required was unsustainable. It also had regard to personal circumstances advanced on Murray’s behalf.
It suspended Murray’s licence with immediate effect and directed that the suspension will remain in force unless and until the Referral Committee determines otherwise.
It confirmed that Murray may apply for the suspension to be reviewed on notice to the IHRB, at which time the Committee will consider the evidence then available as to whether the concerns which gave rise to the suspension have been satisfactorily addressed.

title: State should consider making weight-loss drug Wegovy available to patients, report says
description: National Centre for Pharmacoeconomics ruled the medication is value for money when used to treat overweight patients in some situations
content:
Weight-loss drug Wegovy is cost-effective, and health officials should consider making it available to public patients, an assessment by the drug pricing watchdog has found.
The National Centre for Pharmacoeconomics (NCPE) ruled the medication is value for money when used to treat overweight patients under certain clinical criteria, despite the significant cost to the State of making weight-loss medications available publicly.
However, its recommendation noted the significant cost burden that reimbursement would place on the Government.
Wegovy is manufactured by Novo Nordisk , which also makes Ozempic . Its active ingredient is semaglutide.
According to the NCPE assessment, the estimated annual treatment cost per patient of lower-dose, weekly Wegovy is €2,918, with this rising to €4,370 for the higher dose.
The five-year budget cost would be about €4.4 billion for the full eligible population groups.
However, the NCPE said within stricter HSE-specified subpopulations, this cost could be reduced to between €263 million and €3.2 billion.
The State’s medicines bill for next year will reach a record €4 billion, meaning a decision to reimburse weight-loss medications would place significant pressure on the Department of Health’s finances.
Currently, Saxenda is the only such medication that is reimbursed for weight loss. Ozempic is available under the Long-Term Illness Scheme, but this only to treat type-2 diabetes.
Individuals who want weight-loss drugs such as Mounjaro, Ozempic and Wegovy are able to pay privately for access, with prices ranging from €130 to €600 per month, depending on the brand and dosage.
The NCPE’s assessment will go to the HSE drugs group for consideration, which will then make a recommendation to the body’s senior leadership for a final decision.
The HSE said earlier this week a decision on the reimbursement of weight-loss drugs will take some time and may require a number of meetings.
[ GLP-1s in Ireland: How weight-loss medications work under the HSE system Opens in new window ]
“The State’s approach to these drugs also raises important matters of health policy which will require discussions over the coming months with the Department of Health and other key stakeholders on the potential overall impact on the health budget,” a spokeswoman said.
“The outcome of these discussions will also need to be considered by the HSE in finalising the approach to reimbursement of these drugs.”
Wegovy, manufactured by Novo Nordisk, is one of a number of weight-loss medications under consideration by the HSE for reimbursement.
Earlier this week, the HSE drugs group met to discuss potential reimbursement of rival drug Mounjaro , which is manufactured by Eli Lilly. It has not yet made a recommendation to senior management.
In December 2025, the NCPE said Mounjaro was not cost-effective but that the HSE should consider reimbursing it if it could agree a price reduction with the manufacturer.
Michael Barry, who leads the NCPE, said earlier this year that Eli Lilly had made an offer for a significant price reduction that would make the drug cost-effective, or close to it.
However, he warned it could still cost the State between €2 billion and €3 billion over five years.

title: Woman who suffered catastrophic injuries after alleged trip settles action for €2m
description: High Court told settlement reached with Bus Éireann after prolonged mediation
content:
A woman who suffered catastrophic injuries when she allegedly tripped as she took a shortcut home after a night out has settled a High Court action for €2 million.
Monika Piech (40) has to use a wheelchair and needs 24-hour care after it was claimed she suffered brain damage in the fall in Tramore, Co Waterford, seven years ago, the court heard.
Michael Counihan, Piech’s counsel instructed by MM Halley Solicitors, told the court it was their case that Piech tripped on loose wire in a grassy area and was pitched forward, falling more than a metre down on to the ground of an adjacent car park.
She was unconscious when located, Counihan said.
She had landed on her head and sustained brain damage, Counihan said. The loose wire, it was claimed, was attached to a broken-down and trampled fence.
Piech had been out on the night of March 17th, 2019, and was taking a shortcut home at about 2am after getting a takeaway when the accident happened. Counihan said investigating gardaí later found wire in the grass area. Piech was lucky to survive the fall, he said.
Piech, of Tramore, Co Waterford, had, through her mother Malgorzata Piech, sued a number of parties but the court heard that the settlement − which was reached after a prolonged mediation − was with Bus Éireann .
The settlement reflected a 50-50 apportionment in relation to liability, counsel said.
Counsel pointed out that although Piech had some drinks on the night in question, there was no suggestion of her being inebriated.
In the proceedings it was alleged that the fallen fence and wire comprised a danger.
It was further alleged there was a failure to maintain the fence and a failure to remove a broken fence and wire. It was further claimed there was a failure to eliminate the danger. It was also alleged there was a failure to warn Piech of the alleged danger.
All of the claims were denied and Bus Éireann alleged that Piech had failed to look where she was going, had needlessly endangered herself and had contributed to her own misfortune.
Approving the settlement, Judge Leonie Renolds said she was happy to hear Piech had made remarkable progress to date.

title: Pope Leo asks Putin for ceasefire to allow aid to occupied Ukrainian town
description: Pontiff showing ‘steady improvement’ after surgery, doctors say
content:
Pope Leo has asked Russian president Vladimir Putin ‌to allow a ceasefire to enable aid ​and food supplies to enter the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky, the Vatican said on Friday.
In a telephone call, the pope also expressed “deep concern” for the humanitarian situation in ​the town, taken by Russian forces in February 2022, and which ⁠faces a deepening food crisis, the Vatican said.
Leo ‌and ‌Putin ​are known to have spoken once previously, in June 2025. The pope also reaffirmed ⁠the Holy See’s ​commitment to any initiatives for ​peace, the Vatican said.
The pope (71), is recovering ‌at Rome’s Gemelli hospital after surgery ​for lung cancer. The Vatican said earlier on Friday ⁠that he is showing ⁠steady ​improvement and is able to work and do normal daily activities. It released the ​first images of the pope since his surgery, showing him celebrating Mass and standing unaided.
Russia has acknowledged critical problems with food and medical supplies in Oleshky and said its military was working to resolve them. It blamed Ukraine for the crisis, saying it was obstructing ‌those supplies getting ⁠to the town.
Oleshky, in Ukraine’s Kherson region, had a pre-war population of some 24,000, and ‌is still home to about 1,700 residents, including 47 children, according ​to Danielle Bell, head of the UN ​Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine.
Leo will be seen leading a traditional noon prayer on Sunday, the Vatican said, while preparations continue for his planned November trip to South America.
The pope was diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer, and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung in an operation on Tuesday.
Leo underwent blood tests and a chest X-ray this morning, “confirming steady improvement in his overall condition”, according ⁠to the latest medical bulletin on his condition.
“His post-operative recovery is allowing him to carry out normal daily activities with full independence,” ‌it ‌said. – Reuters

title: Israeli settlers burn olive trees and attack Palestinians and US journalist in West Bank
description: Militant settlers attacked Palestinians and beat Heidi Levine, a veteran photographer for The Washington Post
content:
Clad in black and their faces masked, dozens of militant Israeli settlers burned olive trees and threw rocks at Palestinians in a co-ordinated attack on Friday on a West Bank village’s ‌annual harvest that injured at least two people including a journalist.
Some 80 settlers, some of them carrying gas canisters, descended from a hill above a terraced olive grove where villagers from Abu Falah ​had gathered to pick ripe fruit, a cherished annual tradition in Palestinian life.
The settlers took positions in front of the terraced lanes of olive trees. Some of them used slings to launch rocks towards Palestinian villagers, who descended towards the bottom of the hill before picking up and throwing stones to defend themselves.
“The settlers want to attack us and force ​us from our homes,” said Moutaz Abdelhadi (42), a farmer who witnessed the attack in Abu Falah.
During the attack, at least two Israeli military jeeps sped through the area, kicking up dust as ⁠villagers ran out of their way.
The attack continued after the military’s arrival, with Israeli soldiers firing tear gas in the direction of the Palestinians ‌who ‌had ​dodged the jeeps. The sound of live gunfire could be heard in the area, and a Reuters photographer saw at least one armed settler fire a gun.
The Israeli military did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Palestinian medics ⁠said two people were injured and taken to hospitals in the ​area of Ramallah. One of them was Heidi Levine, a photojournalist with the ​Washington Post. Video of the attack showed Levine lying on her side on a dirt path with her hands over her face as at least three settlers ‌surrounded her.
Speaking from a hospital bed later, Levine, who ​is in stable condition, said: “I was attacked, pushed to the ground. Luckily I had my flak jacket and helmet, otherwise I probably wouldn’t even be here, ⁠because they just kept kicking me and kicking me.”
Levine said ⁠the attack ended when her Palestinian ​colleagues intervened, after which medics rushed her in an ambulance to a clinic in Abu Falah and then to hospital in Ramallah.
Her voice shook as she spoke and she had bandages over her left hand.
Israeli settler violence against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank has increased sharply, with at least 170 attacks since September 27th, around the start of the annual olive harvest, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli settlements monitoring group.
The settlers have been emboldened by the right-wing government of prime minister Binyamin Netanyahu , who has overseen a rapid expansion of settlements and smaller outposts across the West Bank.
Netanyahu has criticised the ‌violence but has taken few steps to ⁠crack down on incidents that have drawn international condemnation and sanction plans by long-time Israeli allies, including Britain.
The occupied West Bank is home to some 500,000 settlers and at least three million Palestinians. UN bodies and most countries deem the settlements illegal under international law regarding ‌military occupations. Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied.
The Abu Falah attack followed a similar attack on Friday morning in the area of Turmus Ayya village, where settlers burned ​three cars after attacking a group of farmers harvesting olives. The military did not immediately respond to a ​request for comment.
Salah Abu Niswa, who witnessed the attack in Turmus Ayya, said the settlers “snuck up like thieves, they caught someone by himself and began to beat him.” – Reuters

title: Rory McIlroy makes decent start to second round in India before fading light halts play
description: In-form Adrian Meronk is tied for the lead in Delhi as none of the Irish players complete their rounds
content:
A congested leaderboard perfectly summed up the disruption caused by the first day’s weather delays to the DP World India Championship in New Delhi where a four-way logjam – featuring Angel Hidalgo, Adrian Meronk, Joost Luiten and Thomas Detry – formed at the business end of the incomplete second round at the tournament.
Of the quartet sharing the lead, only Detry failed to complete his second round in managing just six holes before play was suspended due to fading light. All three Irish players in the event failed to complete their rounds.
Hidalgo added a second successive 68 for a midway total of eight-under par while Meronk signed for a 69 to join him on that mark and Luiten signed for back-to-back 68s. Detry was three under on his scorecard through six holes to also be on eight under for the event which is in its second year on the schedule.
Tom McKibbin, however, stalled. The 23-year-old Northern Irishman had started the day in a share of second after posting an opening 67 but was level par on his second round through his seven completed holes and slipped to tied-13th.
Rory McIlroy , looking to make ground on the two players ahead of him in the Race to Dubai, Patrick Reed and Eugenio Chacarra, was two under for the four holes he managed to complete after opening with a 70. The Masters champion and world number two, currently in third in the Race to Dubai in his bid to join Colin Montgomerie as an eight-time winner of the Vardon Trophy, was in tied-17th on four under.
Polish player Meronk, who has hit a rich vein of form since the end of the LIV Golf season and his return to the European circuit, which included a win in last month’s Alfred Dunhill Links, continued to impress.
Rory McIlroy eagles his first hole of the day 🤩 #DPWIC pic.twitter.com/iGN2Eusw7L
“To be honest, my game felt like it’s coming along for the last few months. I just couldn’t like finish the tournament well. Suddenly feels like I’m gaining the momentum, the confidence growing, and it’s a great feeling. Just when you really can trust your golf game, when you hit shots to your targets, it’s just so much fun,” said Meronk, adding:
“I think finally the game is in a good spot and I am just trying to enjoy it and play to my spots and keep on going, playing to my strengths and playing smart off the tee, placing the ball in good spots.”
Meronk’s form has been so impressive of late that he has surged to third in the early stages of Ryder Cup qualifying for next year’s match at Adare Manor, in his attempt to become the first Polish player to play for Europe.
In the Buick LPGA Shanghai championship on the LPGA Tour, South Korea’s Hye-Jin Choi continued to set the pace despite stumbling to a second round 74 to add to her opening 64 to claim the midway lead on six-under-par 138, two shots clear of Australian Grace Kim and fellow Korean Amy Yang.
Leona Maguire moved into a share of 10th after posting a second round 73 in difficult weather for a 36-holes total of level-par 144.
However, Lauren Walsh struggled to an 82 for 152 which saw her fall back to tied-56 th .

title: Andy Burnham urges Scotland to ‘stop wasting time on independence drama’
description: UK prime minister chooses day of Scottish National Party’s annual conference to give speech in Motherwell on devolution
content:
U K prime minister Andy Burnham has urged Scotland ’s nationalist government to move past the “drama” of the independence debate and to work with him instead on devolving powers from Holyrood to Scottish cities such as Glasgow and Edinburgh.
While the governing Scottish National Party (SNP) was holding its annual conference in Aberdeen, Burnham popped up in Motherwell 220km to the south to make a “genuine offer” to Scotland’s government led by its first minister, the SNP’s John Swinney .
Burnham said he feared big Scottish cities would become “underpowered” compared with English cities, unless the Scottish government agreed to decentralise more of its powers to its regions. He said Westminster and Holyrood should co-operate on the issue.
The UK prime minister also tried to slap down talk that he might grant Scotland another independence referendum – the main political goal of the SNP.
“Too much time is wasted in those dramas,” said Burnham of the independence debate.
“I think unions of countries are better because you can face a challenging world in a more confident and stronger way ... when you work together. That is my view ... He [Swinney] has a different view ... My view won’t be changing.”
Up in oil-rich Aberdeen, meanwhile, senior SNP politicians who spoke to The Irish Times seemed bemused Burnham chose the middle of their annual conference to come to Scotland to give a speech.
Speaking at the SNP conference just before Burnham’s lunchtime speech, Swinney said “of course” he would work with the UK government on empowering Scotland’s regions.
The nationalist governments of Scotland and Wales remain wary, however, that Burnham’s call to boost their regions could strip power from their national parliaments.
“I’ve got a track record throughout my political life of working to make sure as many powers as possible are exercised here in Scotland,” said Swinney.
[ Dominic Cummings stuns peers with rant about Britain’s ‘duff’ political system Opens in new window ]
He laughed off a suggestion by the UK Labour government’s Scottish secretary, Douglas Alexander, that the government in Holyrood was “hoarding” power.
“The secretary of state for Scotland is not a force for good in all this. [He] has not got a clue what he is talking about,” said Swinney.
Scotland’s government has already proposed a reform of local government in the country, whereby its 32 councils could be replaced with six or seven regional authorities which would operate more than 100 community authorities. A review of the issue is under way and a report is expected in December.
Meanwhile, Burnham was not the only Westminster politician who chose the middle of the SNP conference to head north to give a speech. Tory leader Kemi Badenoch visited an industrial facility near Glasgow, where she accused the SNP of “navel gazing” about greater devolved powers and independence.
“They have all the powers that they need,” she said.

title: When it comes to overcharging US golf fans, Ryder Cup shows Ireland to be world leaders
description: Next year’s tournament at Adare Manor was always going to turn us into grasping hopefuls
content:
A s anyone who’s been on-site at one will tell you, the worst place to be for a Ryder Cup is to be at a Ryder Cup. The spectator experience is always terrible, there are way too many people watching too little golf and the easiest way to keep up with the state of play is to open the app on your phone, which kind of defeats the purpose of being there in the first place. You are always, always better off watching it from the couch.
Well, thanks to the reporting of Muireann Duffy in these pages , we now know the second-worst place to be for a Ryder Cup. It’s waking up in Gort, Co Galway , at 4am on Friday, September 17th, 2027, having just dropped €99,000 for the pleasure of your week’s stay and saying: “Hang on, the course is how far away?”
Ryder Cup accommodation: €99,000 for a castle and €19,000 for a house in Tyrone https://t.co/uhoHiUcl5l
Fear not, because the advert on RyderCupTravelServices.com will let you know the score on that one. “Lough Cutra Castle is situated an hours drive (76km) from Adare manor …” its grammatically challenged blurb declares, proving that you can charge 100 grand to rent out your gaff for a week, but still not pay enough to have somebody proofread your ad. Also, it’s an hour’s drive on a quiet Tuesday in 2026. Good luck to you making it in double that time during Adare’s biggest ever week.
Ryder Cup Travel Services is basically the conduit here for people and businesses who want to rent out their accommodation for the week of weeks. They provide homeowners and castle-handlers with a pricing calculator for guidance as to what kind of numbers might be fetchable – and they have plenty more where that came from.
You could be waking up in Kinvara, Co Galway (111km from Adare, Co Limerick ), having dropped €88k for the pleasure. Or, if you’re a cheapskate and you only want to pony up a shade over €67k, you’ll be heading out each morning from Navan, Co Meath . Distance to the course: a mere 258km. The ad says that helicopter transport is available. At a competitive rate, no doubt.
Yes, indeed. Operation Fleece The Yanks is well under way. The Ryder Cup is a celebration of everything good about sport in Ireland: tough competition, ancient rivalries and absolutely rinsing any outsiders who feel they might like to have a piece of it.
In Ireland, we like to buy each other a pint when it’s all over. Little piece of advice, all the same. If you’re aiming to have that pint in Omagh, Co Tyrone , where Ryder Cup Travel Services are offering you a week’s stay for €19,000, maybe try to get out before play ends for the day. It’s a 400km-drive from the course and the pubs close at 11pm up north, even on the weekend.
It’s all very appropriate, of course. No better way to mark the Ryder Cup in its centenary year than to turbocharge the prices and reduce everything down to the bottom line of how much you can winkle out of people who want to be a part of it.
The tickets have long sold out, allowing the secondary market to get under way – packages are available on some of the ticket resale sites online, advertising Monday tickets for as little as €823. Irish people can’t buy them, although you’d hope we’d have more wit than to try.
There’s going to be months of this before we even see a ball in the air. Nothing like US money – and US golf money, at that – to turn us into grasping hopefuls with our hands out looking for alms. Green fees in Ireland have gone through the roof since Covid, with several of the most high-profile courses on track to breach the €500 per round barrier for visitors in 2027.
[ Ireland’s soaring green fees: Some golf courses doubled prices since 2022 Opens in new window ]
To which most people’s reaction will naturally be: “So what?” And right enough, it’s difficult to get anyone to man the barricades to defend the rights of all the Chips, Chads and Bretts who, if they’re coming to Ireland to play Royal County Down and The Old Head of Kinsale, aren’t likely to be quibbling over the price.
But everything is everything, to quote Lauryn Hill. Irish golf is one of the last places on the map where the sport isn’t the preserve of the mega-wealthy. At least not quite yet. Where your club is made up of normal people from around the community and isn’t confined to the gilded, golden classes who can afford it. Where the best of the best are the sons of barmen ( Rory McIlroy ), gardaí ( Pádraig Harrington ), teachers ( Leona Maguire ) and intercounty corner forwards ( Shane Lowry ).
The Ryder Cup was always going to be an outlier. It would have been naive to think or even hope otherwise. It has grown beyond all recognition over the past 30 years, steaming loose of golf’s moorings to become one of the few sports events that connects with the public outside its own bubble. Once that happened, there was nothing surer than it would become a honeypot for every kind of quick buck merchant imaginable.
On that score at least, we in Ireland have long since proven ourselves to be world leaders.

title: Couple settle action against National Maternity Hospital over death of baby girl
description: Linnea Henon Hesselius was born on October 6th, 2021, and died 15 days later
content:
A couple whose newborn daughter died 15 days after her birth have settled High Court actions against the National Maternity Hospital over her death.
The court on Friday was told of the settlement of the actions over the death of baby Linnea Henon Hesselius five years ago.
Doireann O’Mahony, the family’s counsel with Dr John O’Mahony, told the court that the loss of their first child had a devastating effect on Linnea’s mother and father, and they lost faith in the Irish healthcare system.
“Such was the loss of their faith in the Irish healthcare system that they relocated to Barcelona, Spain, for the birth of their second child,” counsel said.
Judge Leonie Reynolds, who offered her condolences to the couple on the death of their “beloved first child”, said it was a travesty that they lost faith in the Irish health system.
When she was born, after 27 weeks and five days’ gestation, Linnea weighed 755g. She was 15 days old when she died after developing necrotising enterocolitis, a severe gastrointestinal condition.
Paulina Hesselius Soremo, who now lives in Sweden, and Frederico Arca Henon, who now lives in Barcelona, had sued the National Maternity Hospital, Holles Street, Dublin, over the death of their daughter.
Counsel told the court the parents’ separate actions for nervous shock over the death of their daughter had been settled on confidential terms. All the settlements are without an admission of liability.
In the proceedings, it was claimed the hospital allegedly failed to identify the mother was at increased risk of pre-eclampsia and allegedly failed to prescribe low-dose aspirin.
It was further claimed there was an alleged falling below a reasonable standard of care and allegedly significant, avoidable, irreversible and devastating harm had been caused.
It was claimed Linnea’s death had left a void in the lives of her parents and they said their lives would never be the same again.
All of the claims were denied and the National Maternity Hospital contended the obstetric care and the antenatal care provided was appropriate and consistent with an acceptable standard of care for an Irish maternity hospital in 2021.
The hospital said an adequate risk assessment for pre-eclampsia was performed.
The judge noted the settlements and the division of the statutory €35,000 mental distress payment.

title: Lara Gillespie finishes fifth in omnium at UCI Track World Championships
description: The Wicklow rider had won silver in the scratch race on Wednesday in Shanghai
content:
Lara Gillespie finished fifth in the women’s omnium at the UCI Track World Championships in Shanghai, moving up two places in the final race but still short of the podium.
After winning silver in the scratch race on Wednesday, Gillespie had similar medal ambitions in the omnium, which tested the 24 riders over four diverse events, and is one of the six Olympic track cycling events at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
The 25-year-old Wicklow rider started out with a fourth-place finish in the scratch, before finishing 10th in the tempo race, which left her fifth overall at the halfway point; she dropped two places after finishing in eighth place in the elimination race, before moving back up to fifth after the points race, finishing with 89 points in all.
Britain’s Anna Morris won gold with 125 points ahead of Japan’s Tsuyaka Uchino (114), with Amalie Dideriksen from Denmark winning bronze (107). Dutch star and defending champion Lorena Wiebes crashed out in the scratch, while Thursday’s elimination champion Lotte Kopecky from Belgium finished behind Gillespie in seventh, with 86 points.
Gillespie will contest one more race in Shanghai when she lines up in Sunday’s points race (7am Irish time), clearly in form to challenge for another possible podium position.

title: Leinster’s chances of Champions Cup glory look slim for a number of reasons
description: Perhaps the biggest challenge for Leinster is that they will effectively be trying to win with virtually an entirely home-grown team
content:
Leinster have possibly never been such long odds to win the Champions Cup since the last of their four triumphs in 2018 against Racing 92 in Bilbao, and with good reason. Paddy Power makes them 9/2 third favourites, behind the French superpowers of six-time winners Toulouse and back-to-back Champions Cup winners Bordeaux Bègles and, all things considered, even those odds don’t look especially generous.
It’s not just that Leinster have accumulated so many disappointments since that triumph over Racing in the ensuing eight seasons, be it losing five finals and two semi-finals, notably the loss to Northampton two seasons ago.
But even if they were to reach another final, that will take place in Lyon at the end of May, which is likely to be in sweltering heat a-la Bilbao last season when Leinster were beaten 41-19 by Bordeaux Bègles. In all likelihood, it would also be akin to another home final for a French team, on the fairly safe presumption that at least one Top 14 side will get there.
The French clubs have a stranglehold on the trophy like no other era in the tournament’s 31-year history by dint of winning the last six in succession.
However, perhaps the biggest challenge for Leinster is that they will effectively be trying to win the Champions Cup with virtually an entirely home-grown team. Of the 40 players they’ve used in three games to date, and likewise the 23-man squad for their opening game against Clermont Auvergne in the Stade Marcel Michelin (kick-off 4.15pm local time/3.15pm Irish), all are Irish qualified.
Rewind to their breakthrough 2008-09 triumph, and it was significantly influenced by the arrival of Rocky Elsom and Isa Nacewa especially, as well as CJ van der Linde to supplement Felipe Contepomi, Chris Whitaker and Stan Wright.
For their second victory two seasons later, Nacewa and Wright were still there, while Nathan Hines and Heinke van der Merwe were also part of that famous comeback win over Northampton in the final in Cardiff.
When Leinster defended their title at Twickenham a year later against Ulster with their most complete performance in a final, Brian O’Driscoll, Johnny Sexton, Sean O’Brien et al were supplemented by Nacewa and van der Merwe again, as well as the short-term signing of Brad Thorn. He was a vital contributor and left a lasting impression from his three months at the province.
In that 2018 final, the remarkable Nacewa, surely the best overseas signing by any of the provinces in Champions Cup history, kicked three penalties in the 15-12 win over Racing 92, with Scott Fardy also starting.
Due to EPCR’s ruling around non-European players, Leinster were restricted to choosing two from Fardy, Jamison Gibson-Park and James Lowe as the latter duo had still not become Irish-qualified. Lowe missed out on the Bilbao final but had made a telling contribution to Leinster reaching the final, scoring in the final pool win over Glasgow and the quarter-final victory against Saracens.
Yet in addition to Lowe’s contract not being renewed at the end of last season, Reiko Ioane has returned to the Blues and Rabah Slimani has joined Toulon, with financial constraints and next year’s World Cup resulting in no overseas signings to replace them.
Hence, of the 43 players registered in Leinster’s squad, all but the currently injured RG Snyman are Irish-qualified. In its home-grown make-up, no squad in the competition is remotely comparable.
The French clubs have to adhere to the JIFF system (Joueurs Issus des Filières de Formation, or academy-trained/homegrown players) and Toulouse have an unrivalled production line of young French players in their system, but their squad still has eight overseas players.
They could bring in a world-class centre such as the Italian Tommaso Menoncello from Benetton to supplement the likes of his compatriot Ange Capuozzo, the Argentinian duo of Juan Cruz Mallía and Santiago Chocobares, and Blair Kinghorn.
Leinster may have had more capped players in last year’s final in Bilbao, but that is misleading, for Bordeaux Bègles have nine non-French qualified players who are of international standard, such as Salesi Rayasi. He has won only four caps for Fiji but would walk into most Test sides.
All things considered, if Leinster manage to win a fifth star his season, it would be the finest achievement of them all.
Follow each of the Champions Cup matches with Nathan Johns on our live story, beginning at 2pm on Saturday

title: Zelenskiy appeals for European help to repel Russian attacks
description: Restrictions in US support and financial problems hamper Kyiv as Russia prepares winter assault
content:
Ukraine is asking European allies for help to acquire the minimum number of air defence interceptors needed to weather a winter of Russian bombardment, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskiy has said.
It was an “open secret” that US-made Patriot launchers capable of shooting down ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones were being redirected to the Gulf, rather than Ukraine, Zelenskiy said.
Beyond its depleted air defences, Kyiv is facing a gap in its budget next year that could be as large as €70 billion.
The European Union ’s 27 leaders discussed Ukraine’s finances and the breakdown in Zelenskiy’s relationship with the Trump administration at a summit in Brussels on Friday.
Angered by Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries, US president Donald Trump has turned against Zelenskiy, striking a deal with Vladimir Putin to buy Russian diesel and reportedly putting a stop on the sharing of US battlefield intelligence that has been vital to Ukraine’s defences.
Ukraine’s access to Elon Musk ’s Starlink satellite network had also been restricted in recent days, Zelenskiy confirmed in a press conference in Brussels. This had temporarily impaired the ability of Ukrainian forces to shoot down fast-moving drones heading for civilian populations, he said.
“This is no time to withdraw support to Ukraine,” European Council president António Costa said on his way into the EU summit.
European governments will need to quickly decide how to shore up Ukraine’s wartime finances until the end of 2028, Taoiseach Micheál Martin said.
The Government was “open” to all options for how the pressing financial shortfall could be covered, he told reporters.
[ Europe should consider ‘all options’ to plug Ukraine’s budget shortfall, Taoiseach says Opens in new window ]
Martin defended the Republic’s financial contributions to Ukraine, after Dutch prime minister Rob Jetten said some EU governments were not pulling their weight.
“We are net contributors [to the EU budget] and through any European mechanism and facility, we will be higher contributors than most ... I think that’s the ultimate way to do it, and it’s the proper and effective way,” Martin said.
Late last year EU leaders agreed to jointly borrow funds as a bloc to finance a €90 billion loan to Ukraine.
Kyiv has been spending the money quicker than anticipated, due to the intensity of the fighting and changing nature of the war, as well as a drop in aid from western allies.
The loan had been backstopped by €200 billion of Russian central bank assets, which are frozen in European financial institutions by the EU’s regime of economic sanctions.
A previous EU plan to use the Russian assets to refill Ukraine’s coffers, in lieu of war reparations from Moscow, did not proceed after Belgium expressed concerns about the legality of in effect seizing the sanctioned assets.
[ Hegseth tells UK counterpart that Ukraine’s access to Starlink restored Opens in new window ]
“Ukraine is running out of funding, they cannot buy and produce what they need,” Denmark’s prime minister Mette Frederiksen said.
Frederiksen said she had not heard EU leaders talk about asking Zelenskiy to tone down his criticism of Trump’s rapprochement with Putin over diesel .
Using Russia’s sanctioned assets was “one of the best solutions at hand” to Kyiv’s money problems, because it would help finance Ukraine’s defences and make Moscow pay, she said.
It is understood senior figures in the European Commission – the EU’s executive arm, which proposes laws and co-ordinates aid to Ukraine – are considering other ways the Russian assets could be used for Kyiv’s benefit.
Zelenskiy, who joined the European Council summit for the portion of the discussion about Ukraine, said there was no sign that Russia was interested in peace.
Finding a way to plug the gap in Ukraine’s budget for 2027 was a “key” question that needed to be answered, he said.
