title: Google to spend $5m to improve forecasting of extreme weather events in Ireland
description: Plan includes creation of weather station network at Irish schools
content:
Google’s philanthropic arm will spend up $5 million (€4.46 million) on high-tech weather forecasting and climate research in Ireland, aiming to improve local forecasting of severe storms, flash flooding and other weather events.
The commitment from Google.org includes €2.5 million in funding for the Aimsir Centre and the Climate + Co-Centre – the organisation’s largest funded initiative in Ireland – and will also see the creation of a new schools-based network of weather stations.
The investment will fund a four-year research initiative that combines Google Earth AI, satellite imagery and real-time weather observations from 560 solar-powered weather stations deployed at schools across the State, known as the Climate+ School Weather AI Network (Swan).
Overseen by UCD’s Aimsir Centre in partnership with Met Éireann and the Climate+ Co-Centre, the stations will measure temperature, atmospheric pressure, rainfall, humidity, wind speed and wind direction at one-minute intervals.
The project will combine that data with historical weather patterns to build “nowcasting” models that can detect severe weather events earlier.
“This combination of central research and the distributed gathering of information, working with the network of 560 schools, is not something we’ve done anywhere else in the world,” said Kent Walker, president of global affairs at Google and Alphabet.
“It is a shift in the way the Irish weather forecasting services are doing it. They are used to having a small number of very high end data points. This is a distributed model we have, and lots of very localised data points. In the aggregate, it may lead to better forecasting for the whole country.”
The data will also be freely available online. Teachers will be provided with training and lesson plans to help students get the most out of the data. The initiative is also being supported by the Irish Schools Sustainability Network, the Irish Science Teachers’ Association, and education portal Scoilnet.
The project will roll out a pilot phase to 20 schools initially, to test the equipment’s function and longevity over the winter months. It then plans to install around 200 weather stations a year in secondary schools around the State.
The stations will connect via wifi, meaning they need to be close enough to a building to pick up the connection, but far enough away that they pick up good wind and rain data.
Aimsir’s Prof Andrew Parnell said the programme was prioritising Deis schools. The stations can also be adapted for different school needs, such as adding air quality sensors for schools in urban areas.
Head of Google Ireland, Vanessa Hartley said the initiative showed how AI could be used to address a real-world challenge.
“What makes this initiative particularly impactful is that communities across the country will play an integral role,” she said. “With weather stations located in schools across Ireland, students and teachers will have the opportunity not just to learn about weather and AI, but to contribute directly to a nationwide – and potentially global – scientific initiative.”
The project was welcomed by Taoiseach Micheál Martin.
“Ireland has built a strong international reputation for innovation, research and technology and initiatives such as this demonstrate how those strengths can be applied to challenges facing communities across the country,” he said.

title: Ó shamhail go teanga
description: Tá contrárthacht idir an Ghaeilge agus an Béarla sna bealaí a ndéantar cur síos ar bhaill an choirp
content: Seo an dara halt de thrí cinn inar gheall mé go scríobhfainn faoi na bealaí a bhíonn ag cainteoirí teanga cur síos cruinn a dhéanamh ar gach uile rud dá bhfeiceann siad. Is í an cheist atá le réiteach: an gcuireann cruth na teanga féin bac ar chainteoirí rudaí áirithe a idirdhealú ó chéile go soiléir, nó an san intinn nó sa tsamhlaíocht a dhéantar an bun-idirdhealú agus go lúbtar an teanga ansin leis an choincheap a léiriú? Is ábhar díospóireachta an cheist seo le fada agus bhí sí ina cnámh spairne ag teangeolaithe tamall maith blianta ó shin. Tugtar ‘The Sapir-Whorf Hypothesis’ go coitianta air mar gurb iad an dá údar sin a thug chun solais é an chead lá agus lean an díospóireacht seo sa litríocht ó shin - rachaidh muid isteach níos doimhne sa scéal sa chéad alt eile. Ó tharla mórán dár léitheoirí a bheith dátheangach, féadfaidh siad féin comparáid a dhéanamh idir an Ghaeilge agus an Béarla sna samplaí a chuirfidh mé ós a gcomhair anois. Agus sibhse a bhfuil bhfuil teangacha eile agaibh, féadfaidh sibh tuilleadh comparáide a dhéanamh, más fiú libh é. Amharcaimis anois mar sin ar chuid de na tréithe atá sa Ghaeilge a idirdhealaíonn í ó nósanna an Bhéarla, go bhfeice muid cén chiall a thig linn a bhaint astu, nó an bhfuil rud éigin sa timpeallacht anseo in Éirinn a chruthaigh iad, nó an dearcadh ar leith smaointeoireachta a chothaigh iad? Tá an focal ioscaid i nGaeilge, ach níl aon fhocal amháin i mBéarla ag freagairt dó. Tógaimis an t-idirdhealú a dhéanann an Ghaeilge idir péirí de gach cineál, nuair a bhíonn siad ag iarraidh tagairt a dhéanamh do cheann amháin de phéire, mar seo: leathshúil ‘one eye’, leathchúpla ‘one of twins, a twin’, leathbhróg ‘one shoe’, leathghlúin ‘one knee’ e.g. gabh síos ar do leathghlúin ‘get down on one knee’. Ní idirdhealú é seo a fhaightear i mórán teangacha, ach is ann dó mar sin féin. Cruthaíonn an méid sin, b’fhéidir, gur rud é a bhaineann le dúchas teanga nó teangacha, ainneoin go mbeadh tuairimí eile faoin méid sin. Tá an nós le fáil san Ungáiris agus san Eabhrais agus i dteangacha eile is dóiche. Is í an cheist anois, cad chuige nach bhfuil an úsáid seo forleathan, nó cad a thug ar na hÉireannaigh an nós cainte seo a chruthú? An úsáid chliste teanga agus samhlaíochta é seo, nó rud éigin a bhfuil míniú eile air? Déanaigí machnamh ar an méid sin roimh an chéad alt eile. Áit eile a bhfuil contrárthacht le fáil ann, na bealaí ina ndéantar cur síos ar bhaill an choirp i nGaeilge agus i mBéarla, abair. Cad go díreach ‘a chiallaíonn cos i nGaeilge – ceann na coise go díreach, nó an chos suas go dtí an ghlúin? Má deir duine Bhris mé mo chos, cad é go díreach a bhíonn gceist - ‘foot’ nó ‘leg’ an Bhéarla? Seo an áit a bhfuil na coincheapa sa dá theanga difriúil óna chéile, agus caithfidh cainteoirí aird a thabhairt ar na difríochtaí céanna. Bíonn seo ina ábhar buartha ag foclóirithe chomh maith céanna. Is dóiche gurb é an bealach is fearr leis na hidirdhealuithe seo a thuiscint i gceart, scrúdú a dhéanamh ar na húsáidí a bhaintear as na focail a bhíonn i gceist i gcomhthéacsanna eile. Seo a leanas samplaí ábhartha den méid atá i gceist agam. Leathlámh ‘one hand/arm’. Leathchogar ’a loud whisper’. Cé go gciallaíonn cos ‘a leg’, tabhair faoi deara go ndeirtear a leithéid seo: Ní rachaidh ná mo chos / áit do choise / cuirfidh siad cosa faoin scéal / chuir siad cos i bpoll leis / cos scine. Tá an focal ioscaid i nGaeilge, ach níl aon fhocal amháin i mBéarla ag freagairt dó. Is fada an focal troigh sa Ghaeilge – ciallaíonn sé ‘bonn na coise’. Seo an focal a úsáidtear sa Nua-Ghaeilge inniu le tomhas a dhéanamh – troigh ar fhad, ‘a foot long.’ Bíonn na focail seo le fáil in áitainmneacha chomh maith: Port Láirge , ón fhocal Láirg ‘a thigh’; Pluck ón fhocal Pluc ‘a rounded cheek’; Éadan Doire , Edenderry ón fhocal ‘forehead’, agus go leor leor eile. Áit eile a bhfuil difríocht shuntasach le feiceáil idir an Ghaeilge agus an Béarla, an úsáid a bhaintear as treoracha sa dá theanga. Ach cheal ama agus spáis, fágfaimid sin go dtí an chéad alt eile. Nóta don léitheoir: Má tá ceist ar bith agat ba mhaith leat a chur ar Dhónall i dtaobh focal, nathanna, logainmneacha nó sanasaíocht na Gaeilge, seol teachtaireacht chugainn ag sceal@irishtimes.com . áit do choise a fháil = to gain a foothold cuir cosa faoi scéal = to lend wings to a story ní rachaidh ná mo chos = ‘not a foot’, ‘I won’t bother’

title: ‘Slam-bang’ shotgun criminal sees prison term increased to seven years
description: Victim was struck on pedestrian crossing and sustained life-changing injuries and spent three months in hospital
content:
A recidivist criminal who seriously injured a pedestrian as he fled on a stolen motorbike after firing an improvised “slam-bang” gun at a house has had his five-year prison sentence increased by two years on appeal.
The 67-year-old victim was on a pedestrian crossing when he was struck by the high-powered motorcycle, which had been stolen two weeks earlier.
He sustained life-changing injuries and spent three months in hospital, 25 days of which were in intensive care.
The defendant, Jamie Russell, has 102 previous convictions including numerous road traffic offences.
In resentencing Russell on Monday, the Court of Appeal – having viewed CCTV footage of the collision – described it as “one of the worst cases we have seen”.
The court heard the so-called slam-bang shotgun attack was carried out as a “a cold act of revenge”, after Russell was “humiliated” by the circulation on social media of a video showing another individual headbutting him.
Russell (25) of Harbour View Road, Knocknaheeny, Cork pleaded guilty to a number of offences including possession of an improvised shotgun and ammunition at Laurel Ridge Shanakiel, Cork, on August 14th, 2024, and dangerous driving causing serious bodily harm at Mount Agnes Road, Fair Hill, Cork, on the same date.
He was jailed for seven years with the final two suspended by Judge Dermot Sheehan at Cork Circuit Criminal Court.
The Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) sought a review of the sentence on the grounds it was unduly lenient.
The court viewed CCTV footage of the incident and heard submissions from both sides before resentencing Russell to nine years imprisonment, with the final two years suspended. The 25-year-old was also disqualified from driving for six years.
At the appeal hearing barrister Imelda Kelly, representing the DPP, said CCTV footage showed Russell dismounting from the motorbike and approaching the house at about 5.40pm before firing a shot from an improvised “slam-bang” shotgun.
She said Russell then reloaded the firearm and made about 10 attempts at a second discharge before he fled the scene on the same vehicle.
The dangerous driving incident happened about five minutes later at Mount Agnes Road in Fair Hill as the victim was attempting to cross the road at a pedestrian crossing. Russell fled the scene on foot but was later identified by CCTV.
Kelly argued the sentencing judge should have imposed consecutive sentences in respect of the firearms and dangerous driving offences.
She said the “slam-bang” gun was a functioning firearm and had the potential to be “lethal”.

title: Actor Selma Blair arrested in New York after alleged assault on flight
description: Blair’s lawyer says actor, who has multiple sclerosis, missed several doses of ‘powerful medication’
content:
Actor Selma Blair was arrested after she was accused of injuring two flight attendants on a trip from Los Angeles to New York .
She was also accused of kicking a police officer taking her to the hospital and kicking a nurse once she got there.
Blair pleaded not guilty on Monday night to two counts of assault for state charges involving the officer and the nurse.
She also faces separate federal charges based on what happened on the flight, which her representatives say was brought on by a severe medical emergency.
The 54-year-old actor was detained by police at about 11pm on Sunday after the Delta Air Lines jet parked at the gate at John F Kennedy International Airport, the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey said in a statement.
Blair and one of the flight attendants were taken to a hospital for evaluation, the Port Authority said.
A police officer taking Blair to Jamaica Hospital Medical Centre has alleged that while she was securing Blair to a stretcher, Blair pulled a leg from the straps and kicked her repeatedly around the face, neck and chest, causing serious pain and substantial swelling.
Later, a nurse moving Blair alleged the actor kicked her in the chest, causing substantial pain.
Blair was arraigned on two counts of second-degree assault late on Monday at a court in Queens, where a judge set her bail at $20,000 (€17,856) dollars cash or $60,000 dollars bond and set the next hearing for January. She left the court with her lawyers
Her lawyer Shawn Barnes told a judge her actions were not intentional. He said the actor, who has multiple sclerosis, missed several doses of “a powerful medication that controls severe neurological symptoms,” according to the New York Daily News and New York Post.
He said she had gotten on the flight in Los Angeles after a heavy workload, and hit her head during the flight. He said these factors along with the altitude led to “a state of severe confusion and disorientation”.
A Blair representative said that the actor had a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct.
Details of what happened aboard the aircraft weren’t immediately disclosed by the airline, police or the FBI, which was investigating, but Delta said in a statement it “has zero tolerance for unruly or unlawful behaviour, as the safety of our customers and crew always comes first”.
The FBI also issued Blair a notice charging her with assault related to her actions aboard the aircraft, according to a federal law enforcement official who spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to speak publicly about the matter.
Those charges will be handled through the petty violations court in federal court in Brooklyn.
No date has been set for Blair’s appearance.
Blair had major roles in films including 1999’s Cruel Intentions, 2001’s Legally Blonde and 2004’s Hellboy.
In recent years, she has advocated for disability rights. Blair was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in 2018.
In 2023, she joined former president Joe Biden at the White House to celebrate the anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act. – AP

title: Public sector strike almost certain as pay row continues
description: Inside Politics: Healthcare workers, teachers, courts staff and many others are now set to mount pickets outside their workplaces on Wednesday
content:
Barring an eleventh hour reprieve, it seems certain that the first wide-scale strike by public sector workers since the economic crash will go ahead tomorrow.
As Pat Leahy and Emmet Malone report on the front page, the Government is increasingly resigned to the action going ahead, with more than 300,000 public sector workers set to undertake a 24-hour work stoppage.
It comes after an attempt by Minister for Public Expenditure Jack Chambers to initiate talks at the Workplace Relations Commission was swiftly rebuffed by union leaders on Monday.
Healthcare workers, teachers, courts staff and many others are now set to mount pickets outside their workplaces on Wednesday as the row over the approach to talks on a new public sector pay deal continues.
An independent mediator may be approached by the Government side in the hope of getting negotiations started, but sources suggested this is unlikely to happen until one or even both of the single-day stoppages scheduled for the next eight days have taken place and there is more pressure from the public for a solution to be found.
Malone sets out which services will be affected by the strikes here .
Nearly all courts will shut down and thousands of schools will close, with some 90,000 teachers set to strike.
Life-preserving services in hospitals will continue, but with about 32,000 public sector nurses involved in the strike, the Irish Nurses and Midwives Organisation said staffing levels broadly equivalent to overnight rosters would be provided.
Non-consultant hospital doctors who are members of the Irish Medical Organisation will provide Sunday levels of staffing through the day shift.
Local authority services are also expected to be severely disrupted, with many libraries and public offices among the facilities set to close.
There will be no proceedings in the Dáil, Seanad or committees on Wednesday as a result of the strike action.
It appears at this point that there will be at least one day of strike action before talks begin in earnest on a new public sector pay deal to replace the one that expired at the end of June.
Coverage of the sentencing of former Olympic swimming coach George Gibney – who was jailed for more than 15 years for the sexual abuse of four girls in the 1970s and 1980s – includes this front page story by Malachy Clerkin. In another article , Orla Poole, a survivor of abuse by Gibney says: “At 80 years of age, he can still hurt someone. He doesn’t deserve to be out on the streets. He has avoided culpability for over 50 or 60 years, and he has never taken responsibility. For me, I think he needs to die in prison.”
On the Opinion pages, Fintan O’Toole argues that the blue-green smoothie running the country – that’s Fine Gael and Fianna Fáil by the way – has no plan and even less passion.
Elsewhere, our Eastern Europe Correspondent Daniel McLaughlin writes that Ukraine has backed US president Donald Trump’s energy “ceasefire”, but asks is Russia on board?
Olivia Kelly and Niamh Towey report that homeowners in both Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown and Fingal will see no increase in their local property tax bills next year after councillors voted to retain the rate at 2026 levels.
Health Correspondent Shauna Bowers has an explainer on how weight-loss medications work under the Health Service Executive system and how its expert drugs group will meet today to discuss the potential reimbursement of Mounjaro.
The British attorney general will approve future prosecutions of former British soldiers and others under long-awaited changes to Troubles legacy legislation going before the House of Commons. Ireland and Britain Editor Mark Hennessy reports .
European telecommunications ministers will gather in Limerick – hosted by Fine Gael’s Patrick O’Donovan – for an informal meeting as part of Ireland’s presidency of the Council of the European Union.
The Cabinet meets this morning. Our tee-up story includes how the Taoiseach will chair a new Cabinet committee on artificial intelligence.
Dáil proceedings kick off with Leaders’ Questions at 2pm.
Government business in the afternoon includes debates on the Employment Equality and Institutional Burials (Amendment) Bill 2026 starting at 2.55pm. Under the proposed legislation the gender pay gap at companies with more than 50 employees will be published on the Gender Pay Gap Portal. The same legislation contains a separate measure to allow for first cousins of children believed to be buried at the former mother-and-baby home in Tuam to be included in an identification programme that sees the excavation, recovery, identification and reburial of children’s remains at the site.
The report and final stages of the Broadcasting (Amendment) Bill 2026, which includes bringing RTÉ under the remit of the Comptroller and Auditor General for audits, will also be debated in the Dáil this afternoon.
A Sinn Féin private members’ motion on home heating oil costs will be debated from 7.47pm.
There will be statements on the Local Democracy Taskforce report and implementation plan in the Seanad from 4pm.
The Committee on Public Petitions meets at 11am to consider a raft of petitions, including on amending learner driver accompaniment requirements and another on the immediate reduction of fuel tax.
Minister for Justice Jim O’Callaghan is before the Committee on Justice at 3pm as it considers the Strategic Lawsuits against Public Participation Bill 2026.
Russia’s illegal war of aggression against Ukraine is the topic of discussion at the Committee on Foreign Affairs, which meets at 3pm and is expected to hear from ambassadors from Estonia, Lithuania, Latvia and Finland.
The Budgetary Oversight Committee will be looking at the Film Tax Credit with representatives of Irish Equity and the Irish Film Workers Association, also at 3pm.
An Coimisiún Toghcháin, the Electoral Commission, will be at the Committee on Housing, Local Government and Heritage to discuss its report on election posters and work related to the Electoral Register. The committee meets at 3pm.

title: Wind, rain and thunderstorms forecast as Met Éireann issues warning for three counties
description: Status-yellow wind warning will be in place for three counties on Wednesday, says forecaster
content:
It will be a wet and windy day in many parts of the country on Tuesday, with heavy rain and thunderstorms possible in some areas.
It is expected to be bright and blustery with sunny spells and scattered showers, according to Met Éireann .
Some of those showers may be heavy with the chance of isolated thunderstorms. Those showers will ease throughout the afternoon as they become mostly confined to the northwest.
[ Google to spend $5m to improve forecasting of extreme weather events in Ireland Opens in new window ]
Highest temperatures will range from 12 to 16 degrees, coolest in Ulster, with moderate to fresh and gusty west to southwest winds. The winds will be stronger along north and northwest coasts.
Cloud will start to increase over the northwest early on Tuesday night with some light rain or drizzle possible. Lowest temperatures will range from 8 to 12 degrees in light to moderate southerly winds, strong and gusty along Atlantic coasts.
A status-yellow wind warning will be in place for Donegal, Galway and Mayo from 6am to 6pm on Wednesday.
Southwesterly winds will be very strong at times, especially along the coasts.
Met Éireann said the potential impacts in these three counties include debris and loose objects displaced, difficult driving and cycling conditions, and some fallen trees and branches.

Large coastal waves combined with moderate surge may also lead to wave overtopping in exposed coastal areas, the national forecaster said.
Wednesday is expected to be a wet and windy day in other parts of the country with highest temperatures of 12 to 16 degrees.
[ Is Ireland ready for a monster El Nino? Expect ugly potatoes, transport chaos and widespread disruption Opens in new window ]
Widespread rain will be heavy and persistent on Wednesday night with the heaviest rain affecting the southwest, west and north.
Temperatures will range from 10 to 14 degrees in moderate to fresh southwest winds with strong to near gale-force along coasts.
Mixed conditions will continue later in the week with spells of rain and showers, but also some drier periods. It will be breezy or windy at times too.
The weather is expected to turn colder but more settled later this week and at the weekend.

title: Cruthaigh do phíosa potaireachta féin trí Ghaeilge
description: Thall is Abhus: Cruthaigh do phíosa potaireachta féin; Ceardlann Scríbhneoireachta ar an Dinnseanchas; Féile Bia úrnua agus Spotsolas ar Ealaíontóir Éireannach – Stórmara
content:
Is breá liom a fheiceáil go bhfuil borradh mór faoi imeachtaí Gaeilge timpeall na tíre agus go mbíonn rath ar imeachtaí d’achan chineál fosta. Ní bhíonn na Gaeil sáinnithe sna Pop Up Gaeltachtaí níos mó ná ag glacadh páirt i gCiorcail Chomhrá amháin, mar bíonn réimse leathan imeachtaí á reáchtáil trí mheán na Gaeilge fud fad na tíre ar bhonn rialta.
Ós ag caint ar imeachtaí spraíúla atá mé, beidh seisiún potaireachta trí Ghaeilge á eagrú in Dublin Pottery Painting Studio i mBaile Átha Cliath 7 an 2 Samhain 2026. Gheobhaidh gach duine péint, stionsail agus uirlisí lena bpíosa potaireachta féin a dhearadh agus a phéinteáil. Cuirfidh an fhoireann glónra ar do phíosa, bácálfaidh siad in áith é, agus beidh deis agat ansin do shaothar lámhdhéanta a thabhairt abhaile leat.
Ní chaithfidh taithí photaireachta ar bith a bheith agat roimh ré agus ní rang ealaíne a bheidh sa seisiún seo ach an oiread. Cuirfear spás deas réchúiseach ar fáil do dhaoine a bheith cruthaitheach, sult a bhaint as an phróiseas péinteála agus neart Gaeilge a labhairt lena chéile. Beidh cead ag daoine a ndeochanna féin a thabhairt isteach leo fosta, mar sin tabhair leat cúpla cara, buidéal fíona agus bain sult as an oíche!
Caithfidh tú sliotán ama a chur in áirithe ar Eventbrite agus €5 a íoc le d’áit a chinntiú. Téigh chuig www.dublinpottery.com le tuilleadh eolais a fháil. Tá an stiúideo lonnaithe i Margadh na Feirme, Baile Átha Cliath 7, D07 P896.
Ceardlann Scríbhneoireachta ar an Dinnseanchas le Cló Iar-Chonnacht
Beidh ceardlann scríbhneoireachta ar ábhar an dinnseanchais ar siúl ag Cló Iar-Chonnacht agus an Fhéile Idirnáisiúnta Litríochta CÚIRT Dé Sathairn seo chugainn, an 24 Deireadh Fómhair 2026, in Ionad Cultúrtha an Dochtúir Ó Loinsigh, Baile Bhuirne, Co. Chorcaí. Beidh an cheardlann ar siúl idir 2-5pm.
Tá an cheardlann seo á reáchtáil ag Cló Iar-Chonnacht le roinnt blianta anuas agus cuirfear fáilte roimh scríbhneoirí nua nó scríbhneoirí a bhfuil saothair foilsithe cheana acu páirt a ghlacadh ann. Is iad stiúrthóirí na ceardlainne an babhta seo ná Seán Óg Ó Duinnín, Lorraine Ní Chathasaigh agus Micheál Ó Conghaile. Déanfar saothair nuascríofa a phlé agus a mheas ag an cheardlann agus caithfear súil ar thraidisiún an dinnseanchais fosta, foirm thraidisiúnta scríbhneoireachta Gaeilge a mhíníonn bunús logainmneacha in Éirinn trí scéalta, miotaseolaíocht agus béaloideas.
Má tá tú féin ag iarraidh páirt a ghlacadh sa cheardlann, níl le déanamh ach dán nó píosa próis (ficsean, splancscéal nó aiste, gan dul thar 5 leathanach) a bhaineann le gné éigin den dinnseanchas a sheoladh chuig moccic22@outlook.com roimh an 17 Deireadh Fómhair 2026. Níl costas ar bith ag baint leis an cheardlann ach tá spásanna teoranta ar fáil.
Féile Bia úrnua le teacht go Conamara i mbliana
Tá muintir Chois Fharraige réidh chun scoth na beatha a chur os comhair an phobail agus an chéad Fhéile Bia riamh le titim amach sa cheantar idir 23-26 Deireadh Fómhair.
I measc na n-imeachtaí is mó a bheidh ar siúl an deireadh seachtaine seo chugainn tá ‘An Féasta Mór’, béile trí chúrsa lán de tháirgí mara áitiúla, ‘Flúirse an Fhómhair’ le hAedín Ní Thiarnaigh agus Margadh Bia & Ceardaíochta i gColáiste Chonnacht, An Spidéal.
Ag caint dó le Scéal an tseachtain seo, dúirt Seán Seoighe, Oifigeach Turasóireachta Chomhlacht Forbartha an Spidéil: “Tá áthas orm a fheiceáil go bhfuil chuile rud ag teacht le chéile anois agus muid ag súil go mbainfidh an pobal an oiread taitnimh as na himeachtaí agus a bhain muidne as iad a phleanáil. B’iontach an deis a bheith ag obair le táirgeoirí agus cócairí áitiúla ar nós Diarmuid Ó Mathúna, Joe Flaherty agus Eimear Killian agus a gcuid grá don cheird a fheiceáil. Beidh muid ag súil le fás agus forbairt a fheiceáil ag teacht ar an bhféile amach anseo freisin!”
Tá cuid de na himeachtaí díolta amach cheana féin ach is féidir teacht ar chlár iomlán na féile ar Eventbrite.
Spotsolas ar Ealaíontóir Éireannach – Stórmara
Tá mo chroí istigh sa seodra agus is breá liom píosaí seodra a cheannach mar chuimhneacháin nuair a bhím ar laethanta saoire in Éirinn nó ag taisteal thar lear. Bainim sult as a bheith ag amharc siar ar achan phíosa atá bailithe agam le caitheamh na mblianta, go háirithe nuair a bhíonn scéalta nó cuimhní deasa ag baint leo.
D’aimsigh mé an branda álainn Stórmara ar na meáin shóisialta agus níorbh fhada gur thit mé i ngrá! Cruthaíonn Emma, an bhean atá taobh thiar den bhranda, píosaí seodra ar leith as gloine na mara a aimsíonn sí ar an trá in Iarthar Chorcaí. Úsáideann sí an ghloine dhaite agus airgead steirling athchúrsáilte le muincí agus fáinní a dhearadh agus a chruthú.
Deir Emma go bhfuil gloine na mara iontach speisialta mar “ní mar a chéile aon dá phíosa”, agus tá sé sin le feiceáil go soiléir sna píosaí seodra atá ar díol aici. Is breá liom an réimse leathan cruthanna, méideanna agus dathanna a bhíonn ar fáil ó Stórmara agus mholfainn go mór cuairt a thabhairt ar an suíomh www.stormara.ie .

title: Europe’s future ‘being decided in Ukraine’, Baltic ambassadors to tell Oireachtas committee
description: Officials from Finland, Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia to discuss Ukraine as Russian attacks increase
content:
Ambassadors for Baltic countries will warn the Oireachtas foreign affairs committee on Tuesday that Ukraine is the front line in Russia’s war of aggression against EU values and that increasing aid to Ukraine will strengthen EU security.
The ambassadors of Finland, Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia will all attend the committee to discuss the situation in Ukraine, as Russian attacks on civilian infrastructure increase in advance of the winter.
All will stress that supporting Ukraine’s defence against Russian aggression is not just helping an ally, but is in the EU’s vital interests.
Opening statements for the ambassadors for Tuesday’s meeting were circulated to committee members on Monday night.
The Finnish ambassador, Leena Gardemeister, will tell members that “both of our nations understand the meaning of independence and freedom”.
She will say that “as a country that shares more than 1,300 kilometres of border with Russia, and a history of wars with [the] Soviet Union, Finland understands Ukraine fighting for its survival.
“Ukraine is not only defending itself, but it is defending everything we cherish in the EU. It is defending freedom, it is defending democracy, and it is defending respect for human rights, rule of law, and human dignity.”
Kairi Saar-Isop, the ambassador of Estonia, will tell the committee: “We will never recognise borders redrawn by force and Russia’s occupation and illegal annexation of Ukrainian territories. This is a matter of principle and international law.”
[ Europe is changing, but Ireland has yet to notice Opens in new window ]
She will also say that “the future of Europe is being decided in Ukraine, and it is existential for us. Europe must remain determined and united in its Ukraine-policy. We have to increase the support for Ukraine in all spheres: political, military, humanitarian and financial”.
Latvian ambassador Agnese Salina will say that “Latvia knows from its own history what it means when an imperial neighbour claims the right to decide the fate of those around it. It is a fate we would not wish upon anyone”.
Latvia has previously reported persistent Russian hybrid attacks, and Salina will stress that “it is also a mistake to think that this war is somewhere far away and is affecting only Ukraine. Not only the countries bordering Russia are at risk”.
“Indications are clear,” according to Salina’s statement. “Russia is not going to stop its war in Ukraine and is preparing for a potential long-term confrontation with the West countries. Russia only understands strength. It can therefore be stopped by joint and decisive action.
“The values and principles at stake protect every single state,” Salina will say. “Sovereignty is not conditional. Territorial integrity must be respected. The United Nations Charter applies to all. By standing with Ukraine, we stand with the whole international rules-based order that ensures the existence and safety of all, even smaller states.”
The Lithuanian ambassador, Jonas Grinevicius, will say that the Ukrainian experience is a valuable resource for the EU as it prepares for any possible conflict with Russia.
“We are still too hesitant to accept Ukraine’s valuable wartime experience – in defence, civil protection, resilience to disinformation, cybersecurity, healthcare and safeguarding cultural heritage. EU level co-ordination is needed to draw on Ukraine’s unique experience in warfare and achieve mutual benefits through deepening co-operation in the field of security both on national but also on regional levels.”

title: Laochra Mhaigh Eo i mórchluiche na gclubanna
description: Tabharfaidh Mistéalaigh Chaisleán an Bharraigh aghaidh ar an nGarraí Mór ag deireadh na míosa.
content:
Níl aon insint ar an spreagadh agus ar an ardú meanman a fuair pobal na peile i Maigh Eo ón mbua stairiúil a bhí acu mí Iúil agus Craobh na hÉireann buaite acu den chéad uair le 75 bliana. Tá sluaite móra bródúla ag freastal ar na cluichí club sa chontae ó shin i leith. D’fhéadfá a rá go bhfuil líon na n-imreoirí idirchontae ar cheann de na gnéithe is mó a mheallann daoine chuig na cluichí club. Ag tús na míosa, ní raibh ach ceithre fhoireann fágtha sa rás i gCraobh Shinsearach Peile Mhaigh Eo agus comhrac an bhradáin idir cuid de na himreoirí is fearr sa chontae.
Sna cluichí leathcheannais, cuir i gcás, bhí Paddy Durcan, Donnacha McHugh agus Bob Tuohy le Mistéalaigh Chaisleán an Bharraigh; Aidan O’Shea, Matthew Ruane agus Jack Livingstone le Bréachmhaigh; Eoin McGreal agus Enda Hession leis an nGarraí Mór. Bhí Ryan O’Donoghue agus Seamus Howard le Béal an Mhuirthead. Sa chéad chluiche leathcheannais, thug na Mistéalaigh aghaidh ar Bhréachmhaigh i mBaile Chathail agus chas An Garraí Mór le Béal an Mhuirthead i mBéal an Átha sa cheann eile. Bhí an sprioc chéanna ag na foirne uilig: an cluiche ceannais a bhaint amach agus deis a bheith acu Corn Paddy Moclair a ardú. Bhuaigh Paddy Craobh na hÉireann le Maigh Eo in 1936.
I gCraobh an Chontae, is minic gurb iad na himreoirí nach mbíonn chomh feiceálach sin ar an ardán náisiúnta a dhéanann an difríocht.
Tá Mistéalaigh Chaisleán an Bharraigh ar cheann de na clubanna is rathúla i stair na peile i Maigh Eo. Tá 31 chraobh sinsear buaite acu, agus bhuaigh siad an ceann is déanaí in 2017. Bhí an club i mbarr a réime an uair sin agus bhuaigh siad an Chraobh trí bliana as a chéile idir 2015 agus 2017. Tá neart taithí idirchontae sa chlub i mbliana freisin. Tugann an taithí ar an leibhéal is airde atá ag leithéidí Durcan, McHugh agus Tuohy breis doimhneachta do na Mistéalaigh mar a léiríodh sa chluiche ceathrú ceannais nuair a thug siad aghaidh ar Achadh Mór. Bhí na Mistéalaigh chun tosaigh 0-13 in aghaidh 0-5 ag leath ama agus cé gur chuir Achadh Mór níos mó brú orthu sa dara leath, bhí an lámh in uachtar ag fir Chaisleán an Bharraigh sa deireadh 0-19 in aghaidh 1-10. Chinntigh siad a n-áit sa chluiche leathcheannais in aghaidh Bhréachmhaí. Níl siad i bhfad óna chéile - go deimhin, níl ach ceithre chiliméadar idir an dá chlubtheach!
Bhí Bréachmhaigh iad féin ar thairseach na staire cúpla uair roimhe seo ach bhí díomá orthu nuair a buaileadh iad sa chluiche ceannais in 2013, 2015, 2018 agus in 2020. Sa chluiche ceathrú ceannais i mbliana, bhí Bréachmhaigh ró-láidir do Chathair na Mart. Bhuaigh siad 2-18 in aghaidh 0-18 i gcluiche inar léirigh siad an cumas atá acu scóranna móra a fháil. Bhí Gareth Dunne agus Robbie Fadden i measc na n-imreoirí a d’aimsigh cúl do Bhréachmhaigh. Tá roinnt imreoirí aitheanta i saol peile Mhaigh Eo ag an bhfoireann freisin, ina measc Aidan O’Shea agus Matthew Ruane, chomh maith le Jack Livingstone. Coimhlint stairiúil a bhí ann sa chluiche leathcheannais idir iad agus Caisleán an Bharraigh ach bhí an bua ar deireadh ag na Mistéalaigh, 1-16 in aghaidh 0-14.
Thug An Garraí Mór aghaidh ar Bhéal an Mhuirthead sa chluiche leathcheannais eile. Baineann go leor staire le Cumann CLG An Garraí Mór agus sé chraobh shinsearacha buaite acu. Tháinig a dtréimhse is rathúla idir 1974 agus 1982, nuair a bhuaigh siad na teidil in 1974, 1975, 1976, 1979, 1981 agus 1982. Sa chluiche ceathrú ceannais, bhí troid chrua acu i gcoinne Fhánaithe na Daoile, Crois Mhaoilíona. Bhí na himreoirí buacacha idirchontae Kobe McDonald, Jordan Flynn agus Conor Loftus ag imirt le Crois Mhaoilíona agus cé gurbh iad na Fánaithe rogha na n-údar an lá sin, ní raibh mórán idir na foirne sa deireadh agus tháinig An Garraí Mór slán le bua 0-14 in aghaidh 0-12.
Bhí sprioc an-suntasach ag Béal an Mhuirthead agus iad ar thóir rud nach raibh buaite ag an gclub riamh cheana: craobh sinsear Mhaigh Eo. Bhí an club sa chluiche ceannais roimhe seo ach níor éirigh leo an corn mór a thabhairt leo. Léirigh siad a gcumas ionsaitheach sa cheathrú ceannais in aghaidh Chlár Chlainne Mhuiris. Bhí bua 5-13 in aghaidh 0-20 acu agus bhí Fionn Ó Donnchú agus Seamus Howard i measc na n-imreoirí a fuair na cúil. Is toradh é sin a léiríonn an bhagairt atá ag Béal an Mhuirthead os comhair an chúil. Tá Ryan O’Donoghue i gcroílár na foirne, fear ildánach a bhfuil cúlra sacair agus dornálaíochta aige chomh maith leis an bpeil Ghaelach. Bhí O’Donoghue an-éifeachtach chomh maith agus é ag aimsiú ocht bpointe. Tá Howard ar phainéal an chontae freisin agus bhí an bheirt acu ríthábhachtach agus iad ag iarraidh An Garraí Mór a shárú. Ach ar deireadh bhí an lá leis an nGarraí Mór tar éis am breise - 2-16 in aghaidh 2-15 - agus iad ar ais sa chluiche ceannais den chéad uair ó 1982.
Ainneoin go bhfuil an-éileamh tar éis a bheith ar na himreoirí idirchontae i ndiaidh na gcluichí le cúpla seachtain anuas, ní hionann sin agus a rá gur cluiche idir na himreoirí idirchontae amháin a bheidh ann. I gCraobh an Chontae, is minic gurb iad na himreoirí nach mbíonn chomh feiceálach sin ar an ardán náisiúnta a dhéanann an difríocht. Beidh bainisteoirí na bhfoirne ag súil le taispeántas foirne óna a gcuid imreoirí ar fad.
Ath-imirt ar chluiche ceannais 1982 a bheidh i gCraobh Peile Mhaigh Eo nuair a thabharfaidh Mistéalaigh Chaisleán an Bharraigh aghaidh ar an nGarraí Mór ag deireadh na míosa. 44 bliana ó shin, bhuail an Garraí Mór na Mistéalaigh sa chluiche ceannais 1-08 go 0-6. Beidh iomaíocht ghéar idir an dá chlub céanna arís agus iad ag súil le Corn Paddy Moclair a ardú. ‘Críost linn’ an mana atá scríofa ar gheansaí idirchontae Mhaigh Eo agus is ag Dia atá a fhios cén fhoireann a bheidh ag ceiliúradh i gceann coicíse.

title: Mental health of students must be prioritised across campus under new framework
description: Students see wellbeing as foundation rather than add-on to college success
content:
Irish colleges will have to embed the wellbeing and mental health of their students across their entire campus under a new guide published on Tuesday.
The revised National Student Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Framework, called Folláine le Chéile (Wellbeing Together), was launched by the Higher Education Authority (HEA) on Tuesday.
It commits to embedding the wellbeing of third-level students across the entire campus through institutional culture, policies and teaching.
The framework recognises feedback sought from students who told them they saw wellbeing as a foundation rather than an add-on to their success at college.
It references the vulnerability of students in the early stages of college, with over one third of first year students reporting that they considered leaving their course.
The report also references international evidence of deteriorating mental health among young adults, saying these challenges are “increasingly shaped by structural and socio-economic pressures, including financial insecurity, housing shortages, and the cost-of-living crisis”.
The student housing crisis is also referenced as one of the key drivers of reduced wellbeing.
The report referenced how students are often working part-time to fund their accommodation costs, while others face demanding commutes, all of which negatively impacts their college experience and their general wellbeing.
In an effort to address these difficulties and build on the original framework, first published in 2020, this revised guide streamlines the implementation actions and provides additional guidance to higher education institutions.
[ ‘Worrying amount of anxiety’: Survey points to living costs as key mental health strain Opens in new window ]
It has narrowed down the original nine themes into three – leading, learning and nurturing – and places a stronger emphasis on mental health promotion, wellbeing and prevention.
It also recognises the needs of all types of students, including those engaged in distance education and studying part-time, as well as those studying on-campus.
Senior leadership in third-level institutions will be responsible for setting the tone of the college’s wellbeing agenda, the framework says, prioritising strategy, funding and culture that supports the mental health of their students.
Academic staff are charged with promoting supporting environments, designing accessible curricula and guiding students to services when concerns arise.
Student services – from counselling to admissions, libraries and sport, among others – are also tasked with promoting wellbeing.
Colleges must develop data systems to monitor the efficacy of their student mental health strategies under the framework.
[ ‘Loneliness and isolation are among the most alarming challenges young people now face’ Opens in new window ]
In a statement about the new framework, Ross Woods, senior manager for mental health and wellbeing at the HEA, said “feedback from students shows that while academic outcomes remain important to them, they see wellbeing as a foundation rather than an add-on to student success.
“In this context, the framework supports institutions to embed wellbeing within institutional culture, policies, teaching and learning, support services and external partnerships, all with the ultimate aim of enhancing the college experience and supporting student success.”

title: ‘A lot of people are losing hope’: A state Trump turned red now appears more divided
description: Protests greet arrival of Donald Trump for an Ohio event that is greatly reduced in scale and intensity from mega-rallies two years ago
content:
On Columbus Day here in Youngstown, Ohio , the street outside the Covelli Centre, where the Phantoms play ice hockey on winter nights, heard two distinct stories. On one side, a loud and raucous protest against president Trump and the administration and, on the other, the Trump merch’ sellers waiting for the Maga crowds arriving in the mild autumn sunshine. The Republican fans arriving from the east of the street were forced to run a gauntlet through protesters, who heckled them with taunts about Epstein and paedophilia.
This latest rally, primarily for Jon Husted, the senator locked in a vital race against the Democratic candidate Sherrod Brown, has brought Trump to Ohio for the second time in a week. Mahoning County was once a Democratic bastion. Youngstown is its urban heart and for years it was its economic furnace, too. Decades of neglect by successive administrations left it open to a new message.
It could be said that Trump turned this fabled Rust Belt City a deep political red. In 2020, he became the first Republican presidential candidate to win the county in half a century. In 2024, he won Mahoning again, by a clear 10 points. Now, Husted has claimed that he has sensed “a change of energy” among the Republican base in recent weeks.
But in the late afternoon, outside the arena, it was the protesters who carried most of the day’s energy.
“This area went so big for Trump and the Republicans last time, but I am glad there is a strong showing of this support,” said Chris McBride, who travelled from nearby Warren to attend the gathering.
“Gas prices is one of those things that trickles down to everybody but it’s not just what you’re paying at the pump, it’s what you are not able to afford because of what you are paying at the counter. Daily life has gotten more expensive. Youngstown and Warren already have low economic output so you are making hard problems 10 times harder for people. Ice is very much present around here. A Mexican restaurant I used to go to – the people who owned it just got deported. I wish more people would pay attention to that.”
Pat Gill moved from Canton to Youngstown a year ago. Around the downtown are symbols of new business and entrepreneurial initiatives – breweries and start-ups reimagined in the imposing, long abandoned industrial buildings. This is an evocative part of the country. But Youngstown’s recovery from its fabled industrial might – “them smokestacks reachin’ like the arms of God into a beautiful sky of soot and clay”, as Bruce Springsteen put it in his mournful ode to the city – has been slow and tortuous. Gill (24) is among a generation waiting to see what the city can offer it.
“I feel like Youngstown is trying. It really is. But I feel like a lot of people are losing hope. I feel like a lot of people my age are turning to things like drugs. I know so many people who overdosed on fentanyl. I’ve been clean for a year off of hard drugs. And seeing everything getting blasted in your face all the time, on the internet, on the news, it makes people feel, like, just not good.”
For the older demographic, the date of September 19th, 1977, will hold a permanent significance: 5,000 jobs lost in one day in the Campbell plant, presaging a collapse of about 50,000 jobs over the following decade. Few cities could sustain a fall into that kind of economic vortex. “Tough times don’t last. Tough Cities do” is an unofficial slogan.
Inside the arena, Trump’s story was about the ongoing revitalisation of the Rust Belt and he came equipped with numbers and statistics.
“After years of steel mills and factories closing across Ohio, our steel industry is roaring back to life. Manufacturing is booming. And American exports have soared to the highest level in history,” he told them, referencing an $800 million Kimberly-Clark investment in Warren and a $48 million investment by Valluourec, a French steel and pipe production company, in Youngstown.
His voice echoed around the hockey arena, which holds a capacity of 7,000, and the crowd stood to applaud at that. The rear tiers were closed off but two open sections available for attendees remained empty. In the front row of the floor seating were some familiar Maga loyalists, including the “brick suit guy”, Blake Marnell, and the “Front Row Joes”, who habitually follow Trump like Deadheads of old. The enthusiasm for Trump remains even if, as a spectacle, this Monday night appearance in the Rust Belt was greatly reduced in scale and intensity from the sort of mega-rallies Trump commanded two years ago.
But Trump’s daily schedule of rallies in toss-up states like Ohio is about repetition of the message, and stirring and energising his base.
“This is almost as important as the presidency,” said one Republican, Peggy, before the event began.
“Absolutely. Because you got these socialist people who are just ... crazy. I don’t understand them.”
She was there with Debbie and Bill Zammery. The trio had just walked through the picket line of protesters calling at Republicans as they passed. They were unfazed by the experience. “It’s absurd. ‘He’s a paedophile.’ Is that the best you can come up with? It’s just crazy talk,” Debbie said.
“We’ve got a lot of mentally unstable people in America,” Bill added.
He believes the midterms are vital for the Trump presidency but is uncertain about the overall outcome.
“In America you can’t be confident about anything any more. Whatever is going to happen is going to happen. That’s why people have to get out and vote.”
Inside the arena, Trump offered a speech that contained his familiar mix of accomplishments listed and dark premonitions of what will happen if the “Dumocrats” are returned to power. He had the Haitian community in Springfield on his mind. He had the Somali community in Minneapolis on his mind. The day had opened with the news that federal agents had raided the home of Somali congresswoman for Minnesota Ilhan Omar.
Trump paused his speech when a protester began shouting from the crowd and was brusquely removed by security. Protests and interruptions have become a feature at the president’s rallies over the past few weeks. Then, he offered a dark vision of what awaits his believers if they relinquish the balance of power over the past few weeks.
“You will look at me right now and you will say he is going to be the last Republican president in history. I will be. I will be the last Republican president because they [the Democrats] will add about 12 more electoral votes, 10 more congresspeople, they’re gonna rig the supreme court through a lot of people.”
Later, Jake Paul, the mixed martial arts fighter and social media phenomenon and a son of Cleveland, took to the stage. “Youngstown! OH! IO! Man, it is good to be home. I grew up about an hour from here in Cleveland. We love Ohio. My mom is here, she still lives here, blue-collar people just like all the people here in Youngstown. I get confused by the people on the left, all the protesters. Do they not have jobs?’
The crowd laughed hard. But in Youngstown, the joke has a bitter ring to it.

title: Geilleagar na meaisíní sliotáin
description: Insíonn an taithí dúinn ón am atá thart nach féidir linn fanacht ar an mbóthar eacnamaíochta ar a bhfuilimid
content:
Nuair a bhí mé i mo dhéagóir i mBóthar na Trá i nGaillimh, ba ghnách linn dul síos go dtí an prom agus cuairt a thabhairt ar na hionaid siamsaíochta chun cluichí físeáin a imirt.
Ag an am céanna, bhain an formhór againn triail as na meaisíní pócair nó meaisíní sliotáin a bhí sna hionaid.
Bhí roinnt de mo chairde a d’éirigh go hiomlán gafa leis an gcearrbhachas agus iad beagáinín níos aosta.
D’fheicfeá iad ina suí os comhair na meaisíní ar feadh na hoíche, ag cur airgead isteach sna sliotáin mar a bheadh zombaithe ann. Fiú nuair a bhuafaidís suim mhór airgid, thosódh siad ag cur na mbonn ar fad isteach sa mheaisín arís.
Buaileadh go dona iad leis an andúil. Ghoidfeadh daoine airgead, déarfadh siad bréaga lena gcairde agus lena muintir, agus go hiondúil ní bheadh go leor airgid acu chun iad féin a chothú.
Bhí mé ag iarraidh samhail nó meafar a cheapadh agus mé ag éisteacht leis na hóráidí faoin mBuiséad an tseachtain seo.
Rith sé liom go raibh an cineál polaitíochta atá againn in Éirinn faoi láthair cosúil leis an stuif a bhí ar siúl sna hionaid siamsaíochta na blianta fada ó shin.
Is í an fhadhb a bhaineann le bheith i do pholaiteoir ná gurb é “ní hea” an frása is deacra a d’fhéadfá a rá riamh.
Ní féidir lenár bpolaiteoirí - idir fhreasúra agus rialtas - srian a chur orthu féin agus gan dul sa seans le hairgead tirim an Stáit.
Trí bliana ó shin sháraigh caiteachas bliantúil an Stáit an tairseach €100 billiún den chéad uair. Ba sprioc thábhachtach é sin.
Ach anois, níl sa mhéid sin ach pinginí beaga. Caithfidh an Stát €125.6 billiún san iomlán in 2027.
Agus beidh orthu an t-airgead breise sin ar fad a chaitheamh gach bliain.
Agus má tá an méid atá tite amach i dtaobh chaiteachas an rialtais le blianta beaga anuas le cur san áireamh, níl mórán seans ann go mbeidh an Rialtas in ann coinneáil leis an teorainn 6% in arduithe caiteachais atá leagtha síos aige dó féin.
Tá an cháin chorparáideach ag ceilt na fírinne faoinár ngeilleagar.
Tá cáin chorparáideach na hÉireann ollmhór. Tagann cuid shuntasach di ó líon beag cuideachtaí ilnáisiúnta, a ngintear a mbrabúis trína gcuid comhlachtaí ar fud an domhain ach a dtaifeadtar a gcuid cánach anseo in Éirinn.
Ar ndóigh, tá córas cánach na tíre seo ar cheann de na cúiseanna a roghnaíonn na cuideachtaí ilnáisiúnta sin teacht anseo agus bonn a bheith acu sa Stát.
Agus an borradh mór sa cháin chorparáideach, is manna ó neamh é don rialtas a chneasaíonn na cneácha airgeadais ar fad!
Tugann gach tráchtaire rabhadh faoin mbaol eacnamaíoch a bhaineann le titim thubaisteach sa teacht isteach i gcáin chorparáideach atá sealadach. Agus níl dabht ar bith go dtarlóidh sé sin am éigin sa todhchaí.
An fhadhb ná go bhfuil caiteachas seasta á íoc againn ón bhfoinse shealadach seo. Agus is airgead mór atá i gceist.
Agus sin é an áit a dtagann polaitíocht an chasaíne isteach.
Muna gcuirtear an teacht isteach breise ón gcáin chorparáideach san áireamh, léiríonn figiúirí an rialtais féin go mbeadh easnamh bunúsach thart ar €12 bhilliún ann in 2026.
Ní haon ionadh go raibh an Chomhairle Fhioscach Chomhairleach (IFAC) chomh cáinteach sin faoin mBuiséad Dé Máirt.
Dúirt an Chomhairle go bhfuil an Buiséad ag cur airgeadas poiblí na tíre ar chonair níos measa agus go bhfuilimid go mór i dtuilleamaí cáin chorparáideach ardriosca.
Agus tagann cuid mhaith den cháin chorparáideach sin ó líon beag cuideachtaí ilnáisiúnta.
Is í an fhadhb a bhaineann le bheith i do pholaiteoir ná gurb é “ní hea” an frása is deacra a d’fhéadfá a rá riamh.
Tá sé i nádúr an pholaiteora daoine a shásamh. Tá sé i bhfad níos éasca cinneadh crua a sheachaint má tá ciste airgid áisiúil agat ó Meta, Google, TikTok agus Apple.
Tá a fhios agam go bhfuil an earnáil sláinte costasach casta. Ach chuile bhliain bíonn caiteachas na sláinte ag ardú go leibhéal nua, agus leanann sé ar aghaidh de shíor.
I bpíosa anailíse a scríobh Pat Leahy an tseachtain seo caite, dúirt sé dá dtitfeadh cáin chorparáideach go mór sna blianta atá romhainn, agus dá dtarlódh sé sin ag an am céanna le fiú leath den tuairim is €10 mbilliún breise atá beartaithe a chaitheamh in 2027, go mbeadh impleachtaí tromchúiseacha aige sin ar gheilleagar na hÉireann.
Tá Éire níos saibhre ná mar a bhí sí riamh.
Tá daoine á n-íoc i bhfad níos mó ná mar a bhíodh.
Ach in ainneoin na nuachta dearfaí sin, braitheann a lán daoine fós go mbíonn siad gann ar airgead an t-am ar fad.
Is é cuid den chúis atá leis sin ná go bhfuil caighdeán maireachtála níos airde acu. Ach tá ardú mór tar éis teacht ar na costais a bhaineann leis sin.
Faraor, cosúil le gach cearrbhach, tagann pointe nuair a chaithfidh tú a rá:
“Ní mór deireadh a chur leis seo, agus caithfidh mé glacadh leis an bpian a thiocfaidh leis.”
Ní eacnamaí mé, ach insíonn an taithí dúinn ón am atá thart nach féidir linn fanacht ar an mbóthar ar a bhfuilimid.
Agus am éigin sna blianta atá romhainn, tiocfaidh nóiméad nuair a chuirfear stop leis an roth rúiléide mar go mbeidh líon na chips tite go mór.
Agus nuair a tharlóidh sé sin, beidh orainn a bheith ag súil le Dia nach mbeidh sé chomh dona agus chomh huilíoch leis an gcúlú a thosaigh in 2008 a rinne scrios ar chóras geilleagrach na tíre. Ní féidir leis an tír a bheith ina leagan de na boic bhochta a chaill a n-airgead go léir sna meaisíní sliotáin i mBóthar na Trá tráth den saol.

title: Ag réiteach na mbóithre
description: Níorbh iad Sinn Féin a chothaigh na dúshláin is déanaí ó thuaidh ach beidh siad sásta leis an dóigh a bhfuil siad ag déileáil leo
content:
Leis an fhógra ó Státrúnaí Thuaisceart Éireann Chris Bryant Dé hAoine seo caite go raibh cosc curtha aige ar mhórshiúl an Oird Oráistigh ar Bhóthar Gharbhachaidh i bPort an Dúnáin, tá deireadh tagtha le sáinn Dhroim Crí, ar na sráideanna ar a laghad. Beidh cás ag cur i gcoinne an chinnidh sna cúirteanna an tseachtain seo, ach pointe an-chinniúnach sa scéal a bhí ann.
Tá faoiseamh ar gach duine nach raibh ag iarraidh an mórshiúl seo a fheiceáil, agus ba é an socrú seo díreach an rud a bhí ó Shinn Féin ón am a bhronn Coimisiún na Mórshiúlta cead ar an Ord Oráisteach sa chéad dul síos.
Agus cinneadh an Státrúnaí ag teacht go hiomlán leis na mianta a bhí acu, thig leis an pháirtí a bheith sásta leis an bhealach ar láimhseáil siad an cheist seo.
Le cúpla seachtain anuas, d’éirigh le Sinn Féin láithreacht láidir sheasmhach a léiriú sna meáin, rud a bhí in easnamh le tamall agus an páirtí ag streachailt buanna a bhaint amach de bharr na ndeacrachtaí ag leibhéal an Fheidhmeannais.
Faoiseamh nach beag a bheidh ann don Aire Liz Kimmins agus do Shinn Féin trí chéile go bhfuil sí anois in ann ordú a thabhairt le tús a chur leis an obair go prás.
Go deimhin, fiú agus an fhógairt déanta an tseachtain seo caite go bhfuil litreacha eisithe ag an PSNI chuig roinnt ionadaithe de chuid Shinn Féin mar gheall ar an mhéid a thit amach ar an 27 Meán Fómhair, ní chuirfidh sé sin imní orthu.
Ní chuirfidh fiú an vóta mímhuiníne i Michelle O’Neil mar Chéad-Aire an Fheidhmeannais isteach ar an pháirtí, ná uirthi. Níl bealach ar bith go n-éireodh lena leithéid de vóta mar gheall go mbeadh tacaíocht trasphobail de dhíth air, agus mar sin ní iarracht dháiríre atá i gceist í a bhaint ón oifig. Níl ann ach deis do na páirtithe aontachtaithe a bheith ag tabhairt drocham di mar gheall ar ar thit amach le cúpla seachtain anuas. Dá mbeadh an DUP dáiríre faoi O’Neill a chur amach as oifig, bheadh ar an LeasChéad-Aire Emma Little Pengelly éirí as a ról, agus is cosúil nach bhfuil an DUP ag iarraidh an cinneadh ollmhór sin a ghlacadh ag an phointe seo.
Bhí an chuma ar an scéal le tamall nach raibh ag éirí le Sinn Féin buanna a fháil ag leibhéal an Fheidhmeannais mar gheall ar chaidreamh leis an DUP atá imithe in olcas, sin agus mar gheall go bhfuil cuid de na hAireachtaí a bheadh riachtanach do thosaíochtaí Shinn Féin i lámha an DUP faoi láthair.
I dtoghchán an Tionóil in 2022 d’éirigh leis an pháirtí 29% den vóta céadrogha a bhaint amach. Toradh iontach a bhí ann don Shinn Féin agus d’éirigh leo oifig an Chéad-Aire a ghlacadh den chéad uair riamh.
Léirigh pobalbhreith le linn an tsamhraidh go raibh Sinn Féin ar 22% den vóta céadrogha, céatadán atá fós iontach láidir, agus bhí siad chun tosaigh ar aon pháirtí eile, ach titim shuntasach a bhí ann ó 2022 mar sin féin. Agus toghcháin don Tionól agus do na Comhairlí Áitiúla ag teacht aníos i mí Bealtaine 2027, bheadh baol ann don pháirtí dá leanfaí leis an treocht sin, go háirithe maidir le ról an Chéad-Aire a choinneáil.
Ba é ceann de na coimitmintí móra a rinne Sinn Féin am an toghcháin in 2022 ná an A5 a thógáil. Le fada an lá tá pleananna ann an bóthar seo a thógáil idir Doire agus Achadh na Cloiche i gContae Thír Eoghain, rud a bheidh an-tábhachtach maidir le sábháilteacht ar bhóithre agus a thabharfadh aitheantas go raibh infheistíocht infreastruchtúir de dhíth in iarthar na cúige. Ach bhí deacrachtaí móra ag an tionscadal mar gheall ar agóidí agus cásanna cúirteanna le blianta anuas.
I gcás sa Chúirt Achomhairc an tseachtain seo caite, cuireadh cinneadh a rinne an Ard-Chúirt anuraidh ar ceal, cinneadh a d’fhág go raibh coimhlint idir tógáil an A5 agus na spriocanna atá aontaithe ag Feidhmeannas Chnoc an Anfa maidir leis an athrú aeráide. Tá an bac sin glanta anois agus beidh tionchar ag an rialú seo ar thionscadail eile chomh maith, an t-uasghrádú atá de dhíth go géar ar an A1 i gContae an Dúin ina measc.
Agus an Aireacht Bonneagair ag Sinn Féin, ceist ollmhór a bhí sa A5 don pháirtí, go háirithe agus iad ag amharc chun tosaigh ar fheachtais na bliana seo chugainn. Ní hamháin go bhfuil tábhacht leis an bhóthar ann féin, ach lena léiriú gur féidir le polaiteoirí Chnoc an Anfa tograí móra infreastruchtúir a chur i gcrích.
Faoiseamh nach beag a bheidh ann don Aire Liz Kimmins agus do Shinn Féin. Níl sé as an áireamh go dtiocfadh leis an chás seo dul chuig an Chúirt Uachtarach, ach léiríonn an bua sa Chúirt Achomhairc nach raibh aon locht ar Kimmins ná ar a Roinn agus go raibh siad ag cloí leis na treoirlínte mar a bhí siad leagtha amach.
Mar sin, cé nach raibh smacht ag Sinn Féin ar an mhéid a thit amach le cúpla seachtain anuas, beidh an páirtí ag dúil le torthaí níos fearr sa chéad phobalbhreith eile, is dócha, rud a bheidh ina chuidiú dóibh agus an t-ullmhúchán ar siúl do thoghcháin 2027.

title: Breaking Bad actor and disability rights activist RJ Mitte dies aged 34
description: Actor and character he portrayed on TV as son of Walter White both ‌had cerebral palsy
content:
Actor RJ Mitte, whose personal ‌experience living with cerebral palsy informed his role as Walter White Jr, the physically disabled son of a methamphetamine kingpin in Breaking Bad, has died aged 34.
News of Mitte’s death in Brownsville, Texas, was confirmed in a statement released through the talent management agency that represented the actor. No other details about the circumstances of his death were given.
“It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of beloved actor, philanthropist, and passionate disability rights ​advocate RJ Mitte,” the statement said.
Mitte was best known for his breakout role on the AMC cable TV series Breaking Bad, playing the only son of actor Bryan Cranston’ s ⁠lead character, Walter White, a terminally ill high school teacher who descends into a secret life of crime cooking crystal ‌meth.
Drawing ‌from ​his real-life background as a person with cerebral palsy, Mitte brought a rare measure of genuineness to a television character whose physical disability was portrayed as largely incidental to the storyline.
His performance as ⁠Walter ‘Flynn’ White Jr, who walked with crutches and spoke with ​a slur, gained early attention from fans who dubbed him “the breakfast ​king” for his recurring appearances in scenes around the family breakfast table.
But his role grew in prominence as the story arc of ‌the series progressed. He starts out as a carefree ​teenager who admires his father, then struggles to reckon with the family’s disintegration as the truth about Walter White’s meth-making “Heisenberg” alter ⁠ego emerges.
“Mitte brought authenticity to the role and ⁠built a platform on disability awareness ​and inclusion,” the statement said, noting his affiliation with a number of philanthropic organisations devoted to cerebral palsy and other muscle-control disorders.
The acclaimed series, often cited by critics as one of the best television dramas of all time, ran from 2008-2013, garnering 16 Emmy Awards, including two for best drama series.
Cranston said he is in “deep despair” following the death of Mitte.
In an emotional Instagram post, Cranston said the pair had exchanged text messages in recent weeks and tried to arrange a catch-up.
“I’m in deep despair as I write this tonight. RJ Mitte, my sweet son on Breaking Bad has died.
“I met him when he was only 14 years old when he was cast as Walter White Jr, a part he played with such joy and enthusiasm.
“Born with Cerebral Palsy, he never – ever – allowed that challenge to be an excuse for anything. “
Aaron Paul, who played Jesse Pinkman, said in a statement: “I am at a loss. I am heartbroken over this news. RJ, I love you my friend. You will be missed.”
Dean Norris, who played Walt Jr’s uncle Hank Schrader, wrote on social media: “Though RJ didn’t play my TV son, I always looked out for him as a young kid on set. He was a sweetheart of a young man and will be greatly missed. This is so heartbreaking, I can’t believe it. Thinking of him and his family.”
After Breaking Bad, Mitte later played a high school wrestler with cerebral palsy in the 2021 coming-of-age film Triumph.
Mitte, whose credits also include the films The Recall and The Oak Room, had been working to promote a new film Talking to Strangers, appearing as a podcast guest to discuss the film in recent days, according to ‌Hollywood trade publication Variety.
Off screen, Mitte ⁠served as a Screen Actors Guild spokesman for performers with disabilities, and was a celebrity ambassador for the United Cerebral Palsy foundation.
Born in Jackson, Mississippi, Mitte suffered brain damage at birth, was adopted as an infant and was ‌diagnosed with cerebral palsy at age 3. He was fitted with leg braces and crutches for much of his childhood, but through athletics and exercise eventually outgrew his ​need for walking devices.
Mitte was raised by his adoptive mother following his ​parents’ separation. - Reuters

title: South Korea goes on missile manoeuvres amid tensions with Washington
description: Seoul’s test launch of hypersonic missile is a hedge against US betrayal after Washington restricts intelligence sharing
content:
South Korea ’s test launch of a hypersonic weapon last week is an important step in upgrading its defences in case war returns to the peninsula. It’s also a hedge against American betrayal.
When North Korea fired a number of ballistic missiles into the East Sea on Monday morning, it was the fourth such launch this month and at least the tenth since the beginning of the year. But Monday’s exercise was an especially ostentatious show of force days after South Korea announced the successful test launch of a domestically developed hypersonic glide vehicle.
Moving at more than five times the speed of sound, these missiles can manoeuvre mid-flight, making them hard to intercept and to predict where they will strike. The missile South Korea tested last week is launched with a rocket booster before it separates and glides towards its target without the need for engine power.
This means they can travel great distances at high speed, remaining undetected or dodging interceptors before striking a target the enemy has failed to anticipate. This ability to penetrate North Korea’s missile defences could give South Korea an advantage if war should return to the peninsula.
“We must secure our national security through our own strength,” South Korea’s president, Lee Jae Myung, said after the hypersonic test.
“The government must not rest on today’s success but must further advance the technology so that the hypersonic glide vehicle can establish itself as a robust strategic asset safeguarding our future security.”
The missile launch comes amid tensions between South Korea and the United States, with Washington restricting intelligence sharing with Seoul for the past few months. The trouble started in March when South Korea’s unification minister, Chung Dong-young, publicly mentioned a North Korean uranium enrichment facility.
The location came from intelligence shared by the US, and Washington viewed Chung’s remarks as a unilateral, unauthorised intelligence disclosure. The US in June excluded a representative from South Korea’s National Intelligence Service from a trilateral meeting with Japan on cyber threats from North Korea.
Lee told a cabinet meeting in Seoul this morning that the relationship with Washington was the main axis of South Korea’s diplomacy. But he said that when differences arose they should be dealt with in a way that respects South Korea’s dignity.
“Diplomacy should be pursued in a way that always upholds South Korea’s dignity and safeguards its national interests (while) any submissive or kowtowing stance should be shunned,” he said.
“The guiding principle of South Korea’s diplomacy is pragmatism. The most important thing for South Korea is its national interests.”
Since his return to the White House last year, Donald Trump has said repeatedly that he would like to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong-un , whom he met three times during his first term as president. Trump said on Monday that he might try to meet Kim when he is in Asia next month for a meeting of Asia-Pacific leaders in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.
“That’ll be exciting, won’t it? But I get along with him,” he said.
Kim has shown no interest in returning to talks with Trump after a summit in Hanoi collapsed when the Americans added fresh demands. The North Korean leader, who is in a stronger position since deepening his defence and economic relationship with Russia, has made clear that abandoning his country’s nuclear weapons is out of the question.
The US is lowering its sights and could instead seek a moratorium on testing intercontinental ballistic missiles that could reach the US from North Korea. This would offer no added protection to Pyongyang’s neighbours in South Korea and Japan, Washington’s increasingly put-upon allies in east Asia.
