title: Losses at Krispy Kreme’s Irish business more than double to €3.07m
description: Revenues are now down 10% over two years as cash-strapped customers reduce their doughnut purchases
content:
Pretax losses at the Irish arm of doughnut maker Krispy Kreme more than doubled to €3.07 million last year as a challenging economic environment affected store footfall alongside rising cost pressures.
Krispy Kreme has expanded rapidly over the eight years since it opened its first outlet in Blanchardstown to great fanfare and lengthy queues. It operates 14 stores and a growing number of “access points” at retail partners.
Sales dipped for the second year in a row to €13.47 million, according to accounts just filed for Krispy Kreme Ireland Ltd, from €14.1 million in 2024. After several years of rapid growth as the US group expanded its presence in Ireland, sales are 10 per cent off their 2023 peak of €14.94 million.
The pretax loss of €3.07 million for 2025 is well ahead of the €1.3 million loss recorded the previous year.
The directors said the company “has operated in a challenging economic market environment with macroeconomic factors affecting footfall in the shops and cost pressure in all input cost lines”.
They cited high inflation impacting consumer disposable income, input costs and lack of labour and goods in the market as factors impacting operations.
A non-cash impairment cost of €692,000 on property, plant and equipment exacerbated losses. Directors said this related to the estimated future trading impact of the challenging macroeconomic environment.
Company directors said they expected 2026 “to present a challenging commercial environment, particularly as the ongoing macroeconomic environment creates uncertainty for consumers’ future behaviour but remain confident that the company is well positioned to continue to be successful by providing an excellent product and service experience”.
For last year, the business recorded a loss before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation of €211,000. At the operating level, losses came to €2.72 million, rising to €3.07 million once finance charges are taken into account.
The loss takes account of non-cash depreciation costs of €1.81 million and operating lease costs of €1.1 million.
Numbers employed in the business rose slightly last year to 176 from 167 and staff costs came to €5.45 million, up from €4.95 million in 2024. Directors’ pay totalled €134,000.
At December 28th last, Krispy Kreme’s accumulated losses in the Irish business stood at €2.23 million while cash funds fell to €684,000 from €1.16 million at the same time the previous year.

title: Cuimhní geala ar an earrach thiar
description: Labhraíonn Mike Scott faoin tréimhse chlúiteach a chaith The Waterboys ar an Spidéal agus faoin áthas atá air go bhfuil beatha nua á tabhairt d’amhráin an albaim Fisherman’s Blues i láthair na huaire.
content:
Tá casadh ar bhóthar Bharr na gCurrach ar an mbealach siar go Conamara, ar a nochtar radharc ar an bhfarraige. Síneann an bóthar amach romhat siar i dtreo an Spidéil. Ligtear osna ón gcolainn.
Sa gceantar seo cuireadh barr maise ar cheann de na halbaim is íocónaí i stair cheol na hÉireann - Fisherman’s Blues le The Waterboys - in ainneoin nach Éireannach a scríobh, ach Albanach fir agus a bhanna, nuair a bhí siad ag cur fúthu i dTeach an Spidéil in 1988.
Tháinig Mike Scott go hÉirinn ar dtús in 1986, ar cuairt ar a chomhcheoltóir, an fidléir Steve Wickham.
“B’éigean dom bogadh ó m’árasán i Londain. Dúirt Steve ‘tuige nach dtagann tú go Baile Átha Cliath? Fan sa seomra breise tamall!’ D’fhan mé leis ar Shráid Lennox go dtí gur éirigh a bhean bréan den cheol déanach istoíche!”
D’imigh an chathair i bhfeidhm air, áfach, agus mhair a chuairt na blianta fada.
“Tá meon éagsúil anseo. Thuig mé an difríocht idir Londain agus Albain. Agus tá an éagsúlacht seo níos doimhne fós. Cé go labhraítear Béarla anseo, tá intinn agus samhlaíocht na nÉireannach difriúil. Ceaptar go bhfuil tionchar [na Gaeilge] ar an aigne fós. ‘People still “do be ” thinking, just “after” thinking this…’ smaoinítear sna foirmlí sin, fiú as Béarla. Domsa mar scríbhneoir, an cineál duine atá ionam, tá sé níos scaoilte, níos fiáine anseo. Thit mé i ngrá le hiarthar na hÉireann go háirithe.”
Domsa mar scríbhneoir, an cineál duine atá ionam, tá sé níos scaoilte, níos fiáine anseo. Thit mé i ngrá le hiarthar na hÉireann go háirithe.
Labhraíonn sé faoi thionchar an tírdhreacha ar an gceol agus ar an teanga, sin agus ar mheon na ndaoine: “Tá an Ghàidhlig níos corrchnámhaí agus scornúla ná an Ghaeilge. Ceapaim go bhfuil an ceol - agus teanga - faoi thionchar na talún. Tá an talamh anseo níos boige, níos réidhe. Ní hé nach bhfuil sé creagach, ach tá Albain níos creagaí. Ba chainteoir Gàidhlig mo sheanmháthair, ach briseadh an slabhra agus níor tugadh don chéad ghlúin eile í, mar gur bhog a teaghlach chuig na hÍsealchríocha... Ach chloistí an teanga, go háirithe ar an raidió.”
Bhraith sé ar a chompord sa Spidéal mar sin, agus an Ghaeilge le cloisteáil ina thimpeall. Ní raibh Mike ach 10 mbliana d’aois nuair a bheartaigh sé go raibh gairm an cheoltóra roimhe. Mhúnlaigh ceol na 60idí agus na Beatles go háirithe é. “Labhair chuile dhuine faoi na Beatles. Nuair a bhí mé ceithre bliana d’aois d’eisigh siad She Loves You. Ansin Hard Day’s Night. Bhí gach albam éagsúil ón gceann roimhe. Thug sé le fios dom gur chóir go gclaochlódh an ceol… agus sin lena raibh mé ag súil mar sin, go ndéanfainn amhlaidh le mo cheol féin.”
Bhronn cara teaghlaigh pianó air mar bhronntanas, féirín a mhúnlaigh laethanta a óige. “Rithinn abhaile ón scoil agus chasainn ar feadh na n-uaireanta fada é - chomh crua sin gur briseadh neart eochracha. Ar feadh na mblianta, scríobh mé gach amhrán i ngléasanna ar nós E maol nó D maol, toisc go raibh na heochracha dubha fós ag feidhmiú.”
Oibríonn saontacht agus cruthaitheacht as lámha a chéile go minic. Lig Mike don fhiosracht agus don nuálaíocht gníomhú, rud atá le cloisteáil i stíl spraíúil luathcheol The Waterboys. Athraíonn an próiseas scríbhneoireachta le himeacht ama, áfach, agus an rud ar thug sé “divine mystery” air agus é sna 20idí, aithníonn sé mar phróiseas céimneach anois é: “bím ag faire ar an amhrán ag teacht le chéile, céim ar chéim, agus tuigim an rud atá ag tarlú le chuile chéim.”
Taifeadadh Fisherman’s Blues i ndiaidh tréimhse thraochta agus sos fada.
“Ní raibh uaim filleadh ar an stiúideo i mBaile Átha Cliath agus na patrúin chéanna oibre a bheith againn. Nuair a chruthaíonn tú istoíche mar a bheadh créatúr oíche ionat, bíonn tú as alt leis an saol mór. Mar sin cheap mé tuige nach gcríochnóinn in Iarthar na hÉireann é?
“Ball dár gcriú, John Dunford - bainisteoir Sharon Shannon a bhí ann ar feadh na mblianta sular cailleadh é - thiomáin sé chomh fada leis an gClár agus An Caoláire Rua ag breathnú ar hallaí pobail, scoileanna, bálseomraí… ach ní raibh aon rud ceart.”
Agus iad ag ól sa Spidéal, mhínigh siad a gcás sa teach tábhairne. Sul i bhfad, bhí glaoch curtha ar mhuintir Theach an Spidéil. Teach mór le radharc ar an bhfarraige, timpeallaithe ag crainn.
“Bhí Mrs. Buckley ag cur fúithi ann. Bhí sí gann ar airgead, agus cónaí uirthi i gcúinne amháin den teach, a bhí deacair le téamh óir bhí sé chomh mór sin. Bhog muid isteach, agus shocraigh muid ár dtrealamh taifeadta ann.”
Thum siad iad féin sa bpróiseas taifeadta, agus i saol agus cultúr na háite freisin, rud atá le sonrú ar rianta an albaim, go háirithe ar a leagan de The Stolen Child (le W.B. Yeats) ar a bhfuil an t-amhránaí Tomás Mac Eoin le cloisteáil.
“Bhí raca téipeanna sa siopa áitiúil… sean-nós Chonamara den chuid is mó. Bhí ceann ar leith a thaitin go mór liom. Ar an gclúdach bhí leaid ina shuí os comhair a thí. Fiche Bliain ag Fás a bhí air. Ceann de na hiontaisí is mó ar ar tháinig mé riamh!”
Nuair a bheartaigh sé dreas cainte a chur le Stolen Child, thuig sé cén glór ab fheiliúnaí len é a rá. “Bhí scríofa ar an téip gur ar an gCeathrú Rua a bhí Tomás. Thiomáin baill an bhanna siar, agus isteach leo sa teach tábhairne ag fiafraí d’fhear an bheáir cá n-aimseoidís é! Carachtar iontach a bhí ann. Sna caogaidí, dathúil, greannmhar. Bhí sé bacach, ildathach mar dhuine, mar a bheadh carachtar ó shaol eile ann. Agus d’aontaigh sé go ndéanfadh sé an píosa a thaifeadadh!”
Cuireadh fáilte rompu i saol ceoil na háite, ní hamháin le linn na tréimhse sin i measc na gceoltóirí, ach i gcroí éisteoirí na hÉireann ar feadh na mblianta fada ina dhiaidh sin. Cloistear “ bhúhúhú” Fisherman’s Blues ag seisiúin cheoil i ngach cearn den tír fós. A ndílseacht don áit ba chúis leis sin dar le Mike: “tháinig Rolling Stones ... le hamhrán a chasadh le Frankie Gavin nó cibé rud, ach ansin d’éalaigh siad leo arís. D’fhan muidne. Chloígh muid leis. Chuaigh Trevor ag casadh le Sharon Shannon, is ceoltóir traidisiúnta anois é. Tá cónaí ar Steve i Sligeach. Is mise an t-aon duine a d’fhill ar rac agus ról!”
Tá cuimhní geala aige ar an tréimhse sin i measc na gceoltóirí traidisiúnta áfach, ag roinnt scéalta óna laethanta i mbun seisiún leo - agus ag freastal ar Oireachtas na Samhna leo fiú. “Bhí mé ann oíche an chomórtais mhóir amhránaíochta. Is cuimhin liom a bheith sa mbeár ina dhiaidh, le Séamus Ó Beaglaoich agus grúpa fear eile. Ba phribhléid í a bheith ina gcomhluadar agus iad ag casadh amhrán. Máistrí iad ar fad, ach Séamus - is guth órga a bhí aige. A voice from the spring of the world from the morning of the moon .”
Labhraíonn sé go ceanúil faoin earrach a chaith siad sa Teach mór sin ar an Spidéal. “Earrach álainn a bhí ann, rothlaínn chuig an teach mór ar maidin, ag saor-rothlú liom síos an cnoc agus ansin cois trá chuig Teach an Spidéil féin. Bhí sé draíochtúil. Bhíodh bricfeasta againn sa teach mór le chéile. Yeah, bhí sé cool.”
Tá an draíocht sin le cloisteáil ar an albam, a bhfuil rian na farraige agus na háite le brath air, chomh maith le lorg chuile dhuine a ghlac páirt sa leagan áirithe sin de bhanna The Waterboys (ina raibh tuairim is 85 cheoltóir éagsúla thar na blianta dar le Mike): Mike féin ar ghiotár, Steve ar an bhfidil, Anthony [Thistlethwaite] ar an sacs, agus Trevor [Hutchinson] ar an dord. An cumas tobchumadóireachta a bhí acu ba chúis le rath na seisiún seo. “An t-amhrán We Will Not Be Lovers, taifeadadh in aon téic amháin é. Bhí liric agam, thosaigh mé ar an ngiotár, chuir siad an téip ar siúl… Tháinig an banna isteach duine ar dhuine, ag tógáil ar an méid a bhí á chasadh agam. Níor casadh é ach uair amháin. Sin atá ar an gceirnín nua.”
Tá an t-amhrán áirithe sin théis athbheochan a bheith aige ar TikTok, agus glúin nua á chloisteáil, de bharr gur casadh é ar an tsraith de chuid Netflix Something Very Bad Is Going To Happen.
Tá nósanna éisteachta athraithe ó bhí Mike óg: “Bhí ról lárnach ag an gceol i bhforbairt an chultúir ar bhealach nach bhfuil anois. Saol eile a bhí ann. D’fheiceadh chuile dhuine an t-amhrán céanna, an t-amhránaí céanna, ar an teilifís náisiúnta. Bhí chuile dhuine ag faire ar na rudaí céanna. Anois táimid ar fad inár mbolgáin féin, inár gcluasáin nó seinnliostaí féin.”
Cuireann sé fáilte mar sin roimh an lucht éisteachta óg nua seo agus an t-eispéireas comhroinnte a bhaineann leis. “Táim sásta go bhfuil aitheantas á fháil ag an amhrán sin ar deireadh!”
Anuas ar an aitheantas áirithe sin, tá saol nua á thabhairt do na hamhráin in athuair ar cheirnín nua Atlantic Rain: The Lost Fisherman’s Blues Recordings a eisíodh i mbliana, agus ar ardáin ag Fisherman’s Blues Revue a thiocfaidh go 3Arena Bhaile Átha Cliath ar an 5 Meán Fómhair, ag cur fáilte in athuair roimh Steve Wickham agus Steve Earle ar an stáitse in éindí le Mike. Bhúhúhú.

title: Euro zone inflation jumps to 3.3%, paving way for ECB rate hike
description: Higher energy costs and a pick-up in service prices drives price growth across bloc in August
content:
Higher energy costs drove euro zone inflation back above 3 per cent in August, paving the way for another European Central Bank (ECB) rate hike next week.
Price growth across the bloc accelerated to 3.3 per cent last month, up from 2.9 per cent in July, driven almost entirely by higher oil and gas prices, data from Eurostat indicated.
The latest figures are consistent with the ECB’s own expectations and suggest that a widely anticipated increase in the deposit rate to 2.5 per cent next week will be a relatively easy decision. It would be the bank’s second move this year after a ​hike in June.
Markets have already priced in the move with the focus now firmly on what happens down the ‌line amid a complicated geopolitical backdrop with the US and Iran still on a war footing.
Policymakers will take heart from the fact that underlying price pressures remained modest, suggesting the second-round effects of higher energy prices are not as widespread as many feared.
The Eurostat figures indicated core inflation – which ⁠exclude volatile food and fuel prices – eased to 2.4 per cent last month from 2.5 per cent as growth in services prices, the single biggest ‌component ‌of ​the consumer price basket, slowed to 3 per cent from 3.3 per cent.
Financial markets see two more rate hikes in the next year on the premise that higher energy prices ‌will eventually start seeping into broader ⁠price setting, especially since the war in Iran is showing no signs of winding down, keeping inflation high.
Natural gas prices are also rising while the broader economy has also proven resilient to the economic stress of wars, tariffs, and ‌higher rates, so the ECB may need to do more to stem price pressures, some economists argue.
In addition, global peers, including the US Federal Reserve, may also be ​forced into rate increases, boosting market bets for a global rate-hike cycle.
Still, even if the ​ECB is forced into further hikes, there appears to be little urgency in follow-up moves, so policymakers may skip the October meeting and focus on the next round of economic projections in December.
“The sharp rise in headline inflation contrasts with a drop in underlying measures of price increases,” David Powell, senior euro-area economist, told Bloomberg.
“That divergence supports our view that the ECB is unlikely to tighten by as much as financial markets are currently pricing in,” he said.
“A cooling labour market should limit the pass-through of higher commodity prices into goods and services inflation more broadly, although a more persistent energy shock could still put another hike – potentially in December – on the table,” he said.
ECB board member Isabel Schnabel told Bloomberg last week that borrowing costs must rise further to bring price gains back to target. Other policymakers have expressed similar views.
Higher energy prices drove Irish inflation to 3.4 per cent in August, the highest level in three months, according to the latest Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices (HICP).
– Additional reporting: Reuters and Bloomberg

title: Cath na mBannaí ar ais d’Fhéile Dorn san Aer 2026
description: Thall is Abhus: Grúpaí agus ceoltóirí réabhlóideacha de dhíth; Picture This; Spotsolas ar Ealaíontóir Éireannach – Siobhan McKenna.
content:
An réabhlóidí ceoil thú? An bhfuil tú ag iarraidh dul san iomaíocht chun €2,000 a bhaint agus do chuid ceoil a chluinstin ar an raidió? Bhuel, seo do sheans páirt a ghlacadh i gcomórtas Chath na mBannaí 2026!
Tá coiste na féile Dorn san Aer agus RTÉ Raidió na Gaeltachta sa tóir ar ghrúpaí agus ar cheoltóirí réabhlóideacha úra le “taispeántas spleodrach” a chur os comhair an lucht féachana i nGaoth Dobhair Dé Sathairn 26 Meán Fómhair 2026. Cuid lárnach den fhéile trí lá is ea comórtas Chath na mBannaí, agus é mar sprioc aige “an splanc sin a las Rónán Mac Aodha Bhuí a choinneáil beo” agus ardán a thabhairt do cheoltóirí óga mar a rinne Rónán é féin i gcaitheamh a shaoil.
Cuirfear fáilte roimh mheascán craiceáilte de ghrúpaí agus de cheol mar chuid den chomórtas seo agus tá cead leaganacha nó aistriúcháin d’amhráin a chum daoine eile a sheinm chomh maith le ceol nuálach nuachumtha. Ní cheadófar amhráin Bhéarla.
Ná caill an deis pota mór airgid a thabhairt abhaile leat, do cheol a chur os comhair an tslua agus comóradh a dhéanamh ar an lorg a d’fhág Rónán Mac Aodha Bhuí ar ealaín, ar cheol agus ar chultúr na nGael.
Téigh chuig dornsanaer.ie le cur isteach ar an chomórtas seo. Tá na hiarratais le bheith istigh roimh an 20 Meán Fómhair 2026 agus níl aon chostas ag baint leis an phróiseas iarratais. Ádh mór!
‘Tóg Mo Lámh’ eisithe mar shingil ag Picture This
Is deacair a chreidbheáil go bhfuil sé deich mbliana ó tháinig Picture This chun cinn i saol an cheoil leis an singil Take My Hand, agus le ceiliúradh a dhéanamh ar an chloch mhíle seo, tá leagan Gaeilge den amhrán eisithe go forleathan ag an bhanna den chéad uair riamh.
Cuireadh ceirnín leathfhada amach ag deireadh mhí Iúil le cúig leagan úrnua den sáramhrán, agus is é Tóg Mo Lámh an chéad leagan Gaeilge den amhrán a eisíodh go hoifigiúil mar shingil. Seo céim shuntasach do cheann de na hamhráin Éireannacha is mó a chuaigh i bhfeidhm ar dhéagóirí na 2010idí – mé féin san áireamh!
Chomh maith leis an leagan Gaeilge, tá taifeadadh iomlán, athmheascadh Madism agus leagan úrnua Take My Hand (And We Can Go Walking) ar an cheirnín úr.
Roinn Ryan Hennessy agus Jimmy Rainsford, arb as Baile Átha Í iad, a gcéad fhíseán ceoil ar Facebook in 2016. Bhain siad na milliúin radharc amach agus níorbh fhada go raibh siad ar bharr na gcairteacha mar cheann de na bannaí pop is rathúla in Éirinn le deich mbliana anuas.
Dá mba mhaith leat Tóg Mo Lámh a chluinstin beo i mbliana, tabharfaidh an banna faoi chamchuairt speisialta fud fad na hÉireann sa gheimhreadh agus beidh siad le feiceáil i mBéal Feirste, Droichead Átha, Loch Garman, Corcaigh, Luimneach, Sligeach, Gaillimh agus Doire. Is féidir do thicéad a cheannach ag picturethismusic.com .
Mascára daite ag éirí níos faiseanta ná riamh
Tá sé ina fhómhar faoi dheireadh agus ní fada go mbeidh dath an óir ar na duilleoga! Mura bhfuil tú réidh le slán a fhágáil ag dathanna geala an tsamhraidh go fóill, tá cúpla bealach ann le giota beag áthais a thabhairt isteach i ngnáthamh na maidine.
Is breá liom féin a bheith ag spraoi thart leis an smideadh a chaithim ó lá go lá ach ní minic a bhíonn an t-am agam iarracht cheart a dhéanamh an chéad rud ar maidin. Tchítear domh go ndéanann mascára daite difear mór, go háirithe nuair a bhím ag iarraidh cuma níos bríomhaire a chur orm féin gan stró.
Téann dathanna éagsúla mascára go deas le dathanna éagsúla súl. Deirtear go n-oireann mascára glas do shúile donna agus mascára burgúnach do shúile gorma, agus measaim féin go mbíonn mascára gorm go hálainn ar achan duine.
Spotsolas ar Ealaíontóir Éireannach – Siobhan McKenna
Caithfidh mé a rá go dtaitníonn an t-am seo bliana go mór liom. Is breá liom aer úr na maidine ag tús an fhómhair, go háirithe nuair nach mbíonn sé fuar go leor cóta mór trom a chaitheamh agus gur leor cairdeagan beag nó geansaí deas thar t-léine.
Cruthaíonn Siobhan McKenna, an bhean taobh thiar den bhranda álainn Moss + Cable, réimse galánta geansaithe agus éadaí cniotáilte a bheadh iomlán foirfe ó thús deireadh na bliana. Tá gach uile phíosa fóirsteanach d’fhir agus do mhná araon agus is breá liom go mbaineann sí úsáid as dathanna geala cuidsúlacha ina cuid dearaí.
Chomh maith leis sin, déantar gach ball éadaigh de chuid Moss + Cable in iardheisceart Dhún na nGall, agus mar sin de is féidir a bheith cinnte go dtáirgtear na héadaí ar bhealach inbhuanaithe agus go n-úsáidtear olann atá bog agus marthanach.
Is féidir amharc ar réimse iomlán éadaí Moss + Cable ag mossandcable.com .

title: ‘The trauma, for kids especially, is huge’: A family’s struggle to get out of homelessness
description: David Carroll says rising rents, cost-of-living issues and mental health difficulties are putting people under increasing pressure
content:
Aisling (36) is homeless with her three children – aged eight, six and three – for a second time.
The house she had been living in seven years ago with her then one-year-old daughter was sold.
“I remember the first time going up in the lift [at homeless accommodation] and breaking down and sobbing. I was terrified.”
Two years later she was successful in renting a house.
“We were there three weeks when there was a knock at the door. It was the bailiffs. The landlord had lost the house. The receiver very kindly let us stay while the [repossession] process went on, which took about three years.”
Though Dublin City Council was due to buy the home through the tenant-in-situ scheme, “the sale fell through” and the family became homeless again.
Though the family is now in supported homeless accommodation provided by the Depaul charity, Aisling describes as “horrific” their journey through three other placements over the past two years.
“We had just a bedroom, no cooking facilities. In one of the places kids weren’t allowed have toys because they were a ‘fire hazard’, I was told.
“There was no storage so all our stuff was in black bags under the bed.
“We weren’t allowed visitors, so no one could come and give me a hand. Even for appointments, I had to drop them somewhere because no one was allowed come and mind them.
“We were put in one place in Kildare. My kids go to school in [Dublin city centre]. I had to travel the whole way in. They actually got medals in school for having the best attendance, didn’t miss any days. It was hard but everything else had been taken away from them so I wanted school to be the one constant thing. They needed some stability.
“It was really tough. I ended up in Connolly Hospital psychiatric ward because of my mental health. I couldn’t believe we were homeless again – the impact on my kids. Even my eldest, she’s eight – she has had only four years in a house.”
She was allocated the Depaul supported accommodation, specifically for families, in the north inner city following advocacy by a mental health social worker.
“I have two bedrooms and a kitchen so I can actually cook for the kids. There is huge support here as well. I have a key worker, and Depaul do days out with the kids, activities with the adults.
“And I can have visitors, so I can get a break, even to go for a walk.”
Depaul, which publishes its annual impact report on Tuesday, said “the scale of the ongoing housing and cost-of-living crisis placed unprecedented pressure” on its frontline services last year.
Though it had what it described as “record-breaking results” in supporting people out of its homelessness, the “family homelessness crisis escalated rapidly.
“The increasing demand for family and mental health support underscores the urgent need for early intervention and stronger prevention efforts to protect vulnerable families and individuals.”
The charity saw a 93 per cent increase in mental health concerns among its service users, with 1,361 needing support.
“Depaul supported 1,456 families in 2025, up 28 per cent from 1,138 in 2024, and supported 2,574 children across its residential and support services. Five babies were born to mothers living in Depaul’s emergency services during 2025, which illustrates the harsh reality of infants beginning their lives in temporary hostel accommodation.”
Chief executive David Carroll called for earlier interventions in helping people avoid entering homelessness .
Speaking on RTÉ Radio on Tuesday, he said this would mean working with people within communities before they entered temporary accommodation.
“We can find the signals of deteriorating tendencies on the back of maybe rental issues, antisocial behaviour, drug and alcohol difficulties and supporting people within community settings is really important.
Aisling is hopeful of finding long-term housing “before Christmas”. A housing association has offered her a home to rent. She has to satisfy a number of standard checks before finding out whether she can take the offer.
Asked whether she thinks people in Government understand the impact of homelessness on families, she says: “I don’t think anyone gets it, except people who have been through it. The trauma, for the kids especially, it is huge.
“I wish there were more places like these Depaul apartments for homeless families. The difference it has made has been phenomenal.”
